title: The 10 highest-rated movies of the 2020s so far, according to Letterboxd
description: From Oscar-winning dramas to acclaimed documentaries, these are the top-ranked films of the platform's community of cinema fans
content: Letterboxd has become an increasingly influential measure of a film's popularity, offering an alternative to traditional critics' reviews and box-office figures. Launched in 2011, the film-focused social platform allows users to rate movies with up to five stars, write reviews and create lists. Its popularity has surged from about 1.8 million members in 2020 to more than 28 million by April 2026, with particularly strong appeal among Gen-Z. Unlike Rotten Tomatoes , which measures the percentage of critics who give a film a positive review, Letterboxd uses a weighted average of members' ratings. Its rankings offer an insight into audience enthusiasm, with independent films and documentaries competing alongside Hollywood blockbusters. Based on a combined ranking of narrative features and documentaries compiled on October 17, these are the 10 highest-rated films released since 2020, each with at least 25,000 Letterboxd ratings. Their Rotten Tomatoes critics' scores are included for comparison. Letterboxd score: 4.7/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 98% Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's documentary follows Elizabeth Holmes , the disgraced founder of blood-testing company Theranos, during the final weeks before her imprisonment for fraud. Given access to Holmes and her family, the filmmakers explore her claims of innocence while questioning the nature of truth and manipulation. Released in October, the nearly three-hour film briefly achieved a 4.8-star Letterboxd score, becoming the platform's highest-rated release. You Can See Everything also earned $15 million during its North American opening weekend, the biggest documentary debut in more than two decades. The film has received five Critics Choice Documentary Award nominations, including Best Documentary Feature. Letterboxd score: 4.6/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 100% Palestinian filmmakers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal join Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor to document the destruction of Palestinian communities in Masafer Yatta in the occupied West Bank. Filmed over several years, the documentary follows Adra's efforts to record demolitions and displacement, alongside his developing friendship with Abraham. Despite struggling to secure a US distributor, the film won Best Documentary Feature at the 2025 Academy Awards, becoming the first Palestinian film to win an Oscar. During his acceptance speech, Adra spoke of his hopes that his newborn daughter would not experience the displacement and violence his community faces. Read The National 's review of the film here . Letterboxd score: 4.5/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 100% Oscar-winning filmmakers Abraham and Szor follow up No Other Land with this documentary that examines Israeli military operations in Gaza through anonymous testimonies from intelligence and military personnel. Filmed on rooftops in Tel Aviv, the film investigates how acceptable levels of civilian casualties are calculated during air strikes. Its title comes from an Israeli military term used to count expected civilian deaths. Produced by The Guardian and JW Films, with Jonathan Glazer as executive producer, Naza won the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice International Film Festival after receiving a 25-minute standing ovation . The film subsequently secured theatrical distribution in 56 territories, including the Middle East , with plans for free global streaming. Read The National 's review of the film here . Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 93% Tunisian filmmaker Kaouther Ben Hania reconstructs the final hours of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab , who was trapped in a car under Israeli fire in Gaza in January 2024. Combining real recordings of Hind's emergency calls with dramatised scenes, the film follows Palestine Red Crescent Society workers attempting to organise her rescue. It won the Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice International Film Festival and received an Oscar nomination. The film has also remained central to calls for accountability. In August 2026, Ben Hania and Palestinian actor Motaz Malhees questioned whether an Israeli military investigation into Hind's killing would deliver justice. Read The National 's review of the film here . Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 86% Spanish filmmakers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi explore identity, relationships and personal struggles across generations in this drama inspired by an unfinished work by poet and playwright Federico Garcia Lorca. Spanning three periods of Spanish history, the film follows three interconnected lives shaped by longing, loss and inheritance. Its ensemble cast includes Penelope Cruz, Glenn Close, Miguel Bernardeau and singer Guitarricadelafuente. La Bola Negra shared the Best Director prize at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival before winning the People's Choice Award at Toronto and an audience award at San Sebastian. It was also selected as Spain's submission for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards. Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 95% Miles Morales returns in this animated sequel, travelling between dimensions after encountering a team of Spider-People responsible for protecting the multiverse. His journey brings him into conflict with Miguel O'Hara, whose determination to preserve the established order threatens Miles's future. Directed by Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers and Justin K Thompson, the film expands on the distinctive animation of 2018's Into the Spider-Verse , combining multiple artistic styles. It won seven Annie Awards in 2024, including Best Animated Feature, and received an Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature, losing to Hayao Miyazaki's The Boy and the Heron . Read The National 's review of the film here . Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 92% Denis Villeneuve's science-fiction epic continues Paul Atreides's journey on the desert planet Arrakis as he joins the Fremen and seeks revenge against those responsible for his family's downfall. Timothee Chalamet reprises his role as Paul, alongside Zendaya as Chani, with Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem, Florence Pugh and Austin Butler completing the ensemble. Adapted from Frank Herbert's novel, the film explores political power, religious prophecy and the consequences of revenge. Dune: Part Two earned more than $700 million worldwide and won two Academy Awards in 2025, for Best Sound and Best Visual Effects. It was also nominated for Best Picture. Read The National 's review of the film here . Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 98% Thai filmmaker Pat Boonnitipat's family drama follows M, a young man who moves in with his terminally ill grandmother after learning of her cancer diagnosis. Initially hoping to secure an inheritance, he gradually develops a deeper understanding of family responsibility and the sacrifices involved in caring for someone. Starring Putthipong Assaratanakul and Usha Seamkhum, the film became a major box office success across South-East Asia, attracting attention for its portrayal of ageing and family relationships. It won the Audience Award at the 2024 New York Asian Film Festival and became the first Thai film shortlisted for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film. Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 96% Based on Tatsuki Fujimoto's manga, Chainsaw Man – The Movie: Reze Arc continues the story of Denji, a young devil hunter who can transform parts of his body into chainsaws. His life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Reze, a mysterious girl who offers the possibility of romance and an ordinary existence. Their developing relationship soon draws him into another violent confrontation with supernatural enemies. Directed by Tatsuya Yoshihara and produced by animation studio Mappa, the film earned acclaim for its energetic action sequences and distinctive animation. It also became an international box-office hit, following the success of the original television series. Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 97% Japanese filmmaker Hirokazu Kore-eda examines a troubling incident at a school through the perspectives of a mother, a teacher and two young boys, gradually revealing how misunderstandings can distort the truth. The story begins when single mother Saori notices unusual changes in her son Minato's behaviour and suspects a teacher is responsible. As events unfold from different viewpoints, the film explores childhood, prejudice and the difficulty of understanding others. Written by Yuji Sakamoto, Monster premiered at the 2023 Cannes Film Festival, where it won Best Screenplay. It also features one of the final film scores composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto , who died in March that year.

title: 'We had a plan B, C and D': UAE retailers pledge to keep food prices stable amid Iran war disruption
description: Retailers and producers to limit increases on essentials as people look to reduce discretionary spending
content: Food industry leaders in the UAE have pledged to keep prices in check and shelves well stocked, as they look to curb the effects of the Iran war . The conflict, which began on February 28, has caused widespread disruption across the region. The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz , where commercial ships have been attacked by Iran, has hit supply chains and fuelled an increase in the cost of food, transport, insurance and energy around the world. Shamim Sainulabdeen, director of private labels at Lulu Group International, which operates more than 100 outlets in the UAE, said the retailer would follow government guidelines and refrain from increasing the price of staples, commodities and essential goods. "We are a responsible retailer, so we are absorbing some costs. The government insists on keeping the price stable for our fast-moving staples," he said. The supermarket company has chartered vessels to speed up deliveries, instead of having orders shipped with those of other companies. The Dubai Statistic Centre's latest consumer price index showed food inflation rose to 8.05 per cent in September, up from 7.39 per cent a month earlier. In a study by consultancy Redseer this year, 78 per cent of respondents in the UAE noted higher grocery prices and 51 per cent identified food inflation as their main concern. For producers, keeping ingredients and farm supplies on the move has been central to easing the pressure on prices during challenging times. Tareq Al Hosani, chairman of Al Ain Farms Group, said the company had contingency plans in place before the war broke out. They included using Fujairah port, working with suppliers and contacts in Saudi Arabia and other neighbouring countries and using air freight. Strategic reserves of feed and other supplies provided a further buffer for production. "We always had a plan B, plan C and a plan D to continue to be able to serve our market," he said. Mr Al Hosani said the company had taken on additional costs to minimise the impact on the public. Customer loyalty and growth in sales helped the company maintain profitability while limiting price changes, he added. "We are trying to swallow as much as we can from that cost variation and we are trying to put the minimum on the clients because you know this is only a transition," he said. "It's only a short period and we owe it to our clients who put their trust in us." Nagham Hassan, a Middle East market analyst for investment platform eToro, said the conflict had accelerated the rate of global inflation. She said people were favouring more affordable options, as they look to reduce discretionary spending. "Both Lulu and Spinney's stated that private label sales increased, and usually private label is a more economic option than the other brands that are out there," she said. More people are making trips to supermarkets, but are spending less each time, Ms Hassan added. The UN Trade and Development agency has previously warned that higher energy, freight and insurance costs linked to the disruption in the strait could increase food costs and put pressure on household budgets. In April, the UAE government launched the Essential Goods Prices Platform, overseen by the Ministry of Economy and Tourism, to monitor price changes on 8,343 products at 525 shops operated by 13 major retailers. The tool was expanded in August after recording 143,000 visits in the first four months. The government took action to protect customers from unjustified price increases after a surge in demand for essentials in the early weeks of the war. The ministry carried out more than 7,000 inspections of retailers in the two weeks after the conflict broke out. It said at the time that it was “intensifying monitoring efforts” to ensure price stability, particularly for nine essential goods – cooking oil, eggs, dairy products, rice, sugar, poultry, legumes, bread and wheat. The price of those items cannot be raised without approval from the ministry and a national committee set up to assess food costs.

title: UAE's G42 signs pacts to explore AI infrastructure in Greece
description: Initial agreements also signed for government services, life sciences and smart cities
content: Abu Dhabi-based G42 has signed an initial pact with public and private partners in Greece to explore artificial intelligence infrastructure in the country. The deal was part of the 18 memorandums of understanding, agreements and commercial partnerships valued at €12.75 billion ($14.3 billion) signed between the UAE and Greece during an official visit to the European country by Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed , Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi. The pacts were signed at the UAE-Greece Strategic Forum in Athens. G42 and five of its portfolio companies also signed initial agreements with Greek entities for government services, life sciences and smart cities, the company said in a statement on Friday. The agreements “mark an important milestone in expanding G42’s intelligence grid across Europe, bringing together advanced compute infrastructure and proven AI platforms for government and industry”, said Mansoor Al Mansoori, chief executive of G42 International. The intelligence grid covers the full AI value chain, from data centres and advanced compute to cloud infrastructure and industry-specific applications. Under agreements with Greece's Copelouzos Group, Khazna Data Centres and Core42 will explore the development of an AI factory in Greece, G42 said. Khazna will lead the development of the physical infrastructure, while Core42 will provide cloud and AI compute capabilities to support organisations in sectors including banking, telecoms, shipping and government. The deal “strengthens the country’s position as a strategic digital and energy hub in South-east Europe”, said Christos Copelouzos, chief executive of Copelouzos Group. The factory will support the digital transformation of the Greek economy, attract new investment and create highly skilled jobs, he added. G42 has been working to help countries build domestic AI capabilities. In February, G42 signed a framework agreement with a Vietnamese consortium to develop sovereign AI capabilities and cloud infrastructure across the South-East Asian country. G42 said its subsidiary Presight will also collaborate with Greece’s Ministry of Digital Governance to explore the use of AI-powered analytics and real-time intelligence capabilities focusing on urban mobility and municipal operations. The collaboration will initially focus on using agentic AI to support municipal waste management and water network monitoring through analytics, G42 said. “Cities generate enormous volumes of data every day, but their real value comes from turning that information into intelligence that improves how cities function and how people live,” said Thomas Pramotedham, chief executive of Presight. Meanwhile, Inception42 will work with Greece’s Ministry of Digital Governance and Artificial Intelligence to use agentic AI across government and education. Areas of focus include using AI-powered tools to support cabinet meetings and monitor progress against government priorities, training government officials to work with AI agents, and developing AI tutors and learning platforms to enhance educational outcomes. Tech-enabled health care company M42 has also signed an initial pact with Athens LifeTech Park (ALTP) for a partnership spanning life sciences research, genomics sequencing infrastructure, population genomics, clinical development and connecting institutional biobanks. The deal is aimed at supporting biomarker research in priority areas including oncology, rare genetic diseases and neuroscience, the statement said. The pact also covers a bilateral programme offering UAE life sciences start-ups a base at the ALTP Incubator for European market entry, and Greek and European ventures access to the UAE through M42’s network.

title: Mohamed Salah on song for Trabzonspor in Europa Conference League
description: Egyptian star provides a goal and an assist during win over Hearts
content: Egyptian star Mohamed Salah had a day to remember as he celebrated his 150th appearance in Uefa competitions with a goal and an assist as Trabzonspor defeated Scottish side Hearts 2-0 in the Europa Conference League. The Scottish visitors came close when Malachi Fagan-Walcott hit the post, but the hosts went ahead with Salah converting from the penalty spot after a Tomas Bent Magnusson foul. The Egypt international then set up Dju Franculino for a classy finish shortly before the hour. It was the club's 200th continental goal and even though Trabzonspor were reduced to 10 men in added time following Sidny Lopes Cabral's red card, they held on to victory. Salah has been in sensational form for the Turkish side. Earlier this month, Salah set a new Turkish Super Lig record as he became the fastest player to register 10 goal contributions. The Egyptian provided an assist in Trabzonspor's win over Samsunspor – his third assist of the campaign. With seven goals since his summer move from Liverpool , Salah reached double figures in goal contributions in only seven games for his new club. Salah has since increased his tally to eight goals in the Super Lig. Meanwhile, Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan, making it three wins from opening three games in the Europa League. Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth in control. Milan goalkeeper and captain Mike Maignan received a red card early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never recovered from that point. Amine Adli scored in the 84th minute to make it 3-0. “It means a lot. We came off two victories, so that gave us a good feeling for this game,” Kluivert told TNT Sports. “We trust ourselves. It doesn't matter who we play against. We know what we're capable of, and I think we showed that today.”

title: Abu Dhabi’s NMDC awarded projects worth $763m by Saudi Aramco
description: Completion of work expected within two years
content: Abu Dhabi’s NMDC Energy has been awarded new projects worth Dh2.8 billion ($763 million) by Saudi Aramco to complete offshore engineering, procurement and construction-related works. Completion of the projects is expected to take between 18 and 23 months, NMDC Energy said in a statement on Friday to the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX), where its shares are traded. It did not provide further details. The new deals add to the Dh2.2 billion in projects secured by the company in the second quarter of this year. The company's project backlog stood at Dh3.3 billion at the end of June. NMDC Energy, a majority-owned subsidiary of NMDC Group, offers end-to-end solutions including engineering, procurement, pipe laying, project management, fabrication, installation and commissioning. The company raised Dh3.22 billion from an initial public offering in 2024 and reported a net profit of Dh251 million for the first half of this year, with revenue reaching Dh9.5 billion. Chief executive Ahmed Al Dhaheri told The National last year that NMDC Energy was aiming to strengthen its collaboration with Chinese companies and looking for opportunities in Iraq, North Africa and Nigeria as part of its global expansion plan. The company was seeking contracts to serve offshore and onshore segments of the energy industry in Iraq, with mostly offshore jobs in Nigeria, he said.

title: Protests, the cost of living and a widening wealth gap
description: Almost half of the world's wealth is held by 1.5 per cent of the adult population, as anger grows over living costs and public services
content: Protesters in several countries in Europe and Asia are voicing anger over the cost of living, public services and their prospects. France has had the largest demonstrations, with more than 500,000 people marching at the weekend and outbreaks of looting and rioting. There is no single, unifying motivation for the broader international protests, but underlying them is undoubtedly the rising cost of living. This global inflation is exacerbated in the minds of some protesters by a widening wealth gap, and our chart of the week points to how broad that gulf really is. UBS’s Global Wealth Report 2026 estimates that 58 million adults, 1.5 per cent of the world’s total, are worth more than $1 million each and hold 48.4 per cent of global wealth. At the other end, 1.62 billion adults, or 42.1 per cent, have less than $10,000 each; together, they hold just 0.6 per cent of the world’s wealth. The pressure on household budgets is another part of the picture. The attached charts show how much consumer prices have risen since 2000. In France, a basket of products costing $100 in 2000 cost $151 in 2025. In Serbia, it rose to $1,054. Iran and Turkey are higher still, so the comparison uses a logarithmic scale. Inflation has eased from its recent peaks in many countries, but that means prices are rising more slowly, not returning to where they were. Fuel is another major factor in energy infrastructure in Europe and Asia. The price of energy has contributed to protests and public anger across Europe and Asia. These facts and figures do not, of course, explain every protest or prove that wealth inequality caused them. India’s demonstrations, for example, centre on changes to voter lists. But they show why lower inflation alone may not feel like relief: prices remain far above their past levels, and in some countries wages have not kept pace.

title: F1 power rankings and US GP predictions: Verstappen eyes hat-trick while Antonelli has title in grasp
description: Season reaches home straight with Italian closing in on first drivers' championship crown
content: Formula One heads to Austin this weekend with Max Verstappen looking for a hat-trick of wins while Kimi Antonelli is within touching distance of a first world championship. Circuit of the Americas combines fast flowing corners with heavy braking zones and a long back straight. It asks a great deal of both car and driver. This weekend, track temperatures are expected to climb above 55°C which puts tyre wear firmly in the spotlight. The drivers who manage their rubber best should be the ones fighting at the front. Our power rankings measure who will arrive in Austin in the best shape. We take into account recent form, raw speed, how much each driver extracts from their car, momentum and how well their strengths might suit the Circuit of the Americas. Here are our top 10 rankings and predictions for the race. Form: Bahrain P11, Singapore P8. Championship: P14 Singapore was Hulkenberg’s most productive weekend of the season. He took P7 in the sprint and P8 in the race where he spent the closing laps resisting a much quicker George Russell. Audi believes recent work on the car is beginning to pay off, although Hulkenberg was quick to temper expectations. The Circuit of the Americas will tell us if their progress is genuine and worthy of excitement. Form: Bahrain P6, Singapore P5. Championship: P7 Successive top six finishes have steadied him after a difficult period. He should have left Singapore with more but the McLarens collided on the final lap of the sprint which ended his race and led to internal talks within the team. McLaren chief executive Zak Brown believes Piastri is recovering his confidence and the driver looks like himself again. McLaren is bringing small floor changes to Austin alongside work aimed at improving braking, something that ought to help the Australian in Texas. Form: Bahrain P5, Singapore P10. Championship: P8 Hadjar’s Singapore result deserves an asterisk. His weekend was wrecked by a succession of technical problems, including power-unit and gearbox issues. He eventually started from the pit lane and yet he still recovered to P10. Laurent Mekies admitted Red Bull “owe him one” after failing to give the French-Algerian driver a proper chance to show his pace. RB22 car has progressed immensely well so Hadjar ought to have a good weekend. Form: Bahrain P7, Singapore P7. Championship: P9 Lawson is now one of the most dependable drivers on the grid. Two successive P7 finishes and P5 in Singapore’s Sprint race, Lawson is collecting points. With his 2027 future still undecided, the New Zealander is making his case on track. He has now finished ahead of Lindblad in 10 of their 14 Grands Prix together. Can he keep his seat? Form: Bahrain P9, Singapore P4. Championship: P6 Singapore dented Norris ’ momentum after the Sprint clash with Oscar Piastri cost McLaren points and promoted internal talks. His pace is still strong but questions must be asked about his decision making. McLaren has drawn a line under the crash but the British river will head to Austin with a lot to prove. Form: Bahrain DNF, Singapore P9. Championship: P2 Russell continues in his unlucky streak. He was heading towards taking P3 in Sepang when his engine failed and he was forced to retire. That forced him into a huge power-unit penalty in Singapore where he started 19th and recovered to P9. Reliability issues continue to haunt the driver and Toto Wolff admitted, “Malaysia and Singapore were difficult weekends for us and we have worked hard to understand where we fell short.” Both Mercedes drivers will be driving the latest specification cars and Russell will hope lady luck will be on his side in Texas. Form: Bahrain P3, Singapore P6. Championship: P3 He finished second in the Sprint and qualified P3 for the Singapore GP but Sunday didn’t go as planned. Hamilton missed Ferrari’s pit entry under the virtual safety car, stayed out and endured until his ageing tyres surrendered three positions late on. “Sorry, boys. I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points.” Ferrari brings a new floor to Austin designed to give the SF-26 car a wider operating window. Hamilton’s five victories at this track should stand him in good stead. Form: Bahrain P4, Singapore P2. Championship: P5 Leclerc finally escaped his run of fourth places with a superb second in Singapore. He attacked Verstappen at the start and briefly looked capable of truly challenging before the Red Bull pulled clear. It was a throwback to 2022 but the truth is, as Leclerc admitted, the Ferrari lacks the pace. Ferrari’s new upgrade is the last big one of the season and the new floor should help the team generate more consistent aerodynamic load allowing for better balance. Form: Bahrain P2, Singapore P3. Championship: P1 Despite Mercedes’ problems, Antonelli always finds a way of fighting at the top. He battled braking problems throughout a difficult Singapore race but he recovered well on fresh tyres to pass Norris and Hamilton for P3. Antonelli now has 14 podiums from 17 races and leads Russell by 102 points. Victory in Texas could give him the chance to seal the title this weekend if other results go his way. Form: Bahrain P1, Singapore P1. Championship : P4 Verstappen has gone from chasing his first victory of the season to looking like the favourite for every upcoming race. He followed his win in Malaysia with a clean-sweep in Singapore , taking Sprint pole and victory before repeating the feat in the GP. It was his first win at Marina Bay in 10 attempts. Red Bull’s progress is now clear, and the car now looks to be the best on the grid. Verstappen has always done well in this circuit and will be gunning for a third successive victory to stop Antonelli winning the championship. 1. Max Verstappen Two consecutive victories, it’s virtually impossible to stop the Dutchman when he finds momentum. He has now looked competitive across several circuit types and he knows how to win in the Circuit of the Americas 2. Kimi Antonelli He could win it all in Texas and the youngster will be challenging himself to win this race. The team now understands its latest upgrade better and will hope to avoid any reliability issues. 3. Charles Leclerc After managing a strong result in Singapore, the latest upgrade should help Leclerc to challenge once again. He won in Austin in 2024 and will hope to manage at least a podium finish this Sunday.

title: Binance's Qafila 2026 campaign rewards Gen Z users driving digital finance adoption across the region
description: Initiative arrives against a backdrop of growing digital financial participation throughout the Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan
content: Binance has unveiled a generous regional initiative designed to rally eligible users to celebrate shared financial journeys and explore a broader range of digital financial tools. Qafila 2026 launched with US$1 million in USDC rewards, bringing together eligible users across the Middle East, North Africa (MENA) and Pakistan. New data from Binance - the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume and number of registered users - reveals that 50 per cent of users across that geography are aged 18-29. Binance says Qafila reflects its “commitment to evolving alongside its community” as user needs extend across trading, earning, payments, learning and access to global financial markets. The Qafila initiative arrives against a backdrop of growing digital financial participation in the region, supported by new Binance user data that highlights the rising influence of Gen Z and broader adoption of digital financial services across MENA and Pakistan. The 18-29 age group, representing the adult Gen Z demographic, accounts for 50 per cent of the Binance user base across MENA and Pakistan, rising to 54% in Pakistan. This underscores the importance of younger generations in shaping the region’s evolving digital financial landscape, explains Tarik Erk, head of MENAT and senior executive officer at Binance. “MENA and Pakistan are priority markets for Binance, where growing digital adoption is changing what users expect from financial services,” he tells The National. “Our focus is to evolve alongside our community, bringing greater choice, practical utility and education into one ecosystem through our vision of All Finance on Binance . Erk adds: “Qafila celebrates that community and the different ambitions driving its financial journey.” Named after the concept of a caravan, the word draws on an idea familiar across Arabic- and Urdu-speaking communities - that of people moving forward together while pursuing their own ambitions. The Qafila initiative brings that shared purpose into a regional experience, connecting users across markets through participation, discovery and rewards. Beyond demographic trends, Binance’s regional data also points to growing engagement across its ecosystem. It reported more than half - 52.9 per cent - of verified users across MENA and Pakistan had engaged with two or more Binance products. The UAE recorded the highest adoption rate at 69.3 per cent, followed by Bahrain (57.2 per cent), and Pakistan (52.6 per cent). The Binance ecosystem now spans services and experiences from trading and earning, to payments, Binance Square and Binance Academy, reflecting its expanding role beyond trading as it brings together financial tools, education and community engagement in one platform. The exchange says these trends reflect broader developments in digital financial participation across MENA. Previous research by Binance cited it as the fastest-growing region for stablecoin savings on Binance Earn; the area’s share of global stablecoin balances held through the platform increased from 5.53 per cent to 9.21 per cent. The region’s share of global stablecoin trading volume on Binance also rose from 7 per cent in 2023 to 11 per cent this year. This made it the fastest-growing region by trading-volume share over that period. Within MENA, the UAE was shown to account for the largest stablecoin holdings, highlighting the region’s growing adoption of digital assets for trading, holding value, and earning rewards on eligible assets. These regional developments sit within a wider shift in financial participation across emerging markets. Binance’s global platform data shows that 77 per cent of its users are based in these growth economies, a substantial increase from 49 per cent in 2020. Global Binance Research findings further highlight the prevalence of a new generation of financial users. Gen Z accounts for 44 per cent of Binance Direct Stocks and bStocks users. Meanwhile, its share of new TradFi users rose from 41 per cent in January to 47 per cent in July 2026. Essentially, the global findings highlight the wider participation of younger users in traditional financial markets through digital platforms which, in turn, reinforces the importance of access, choice and financial education, says Binance. It also notes these evolving user needs reflect its All Finance on Binance vision, which brings digital assets, traditional financial markets and everyday financial tools together in one ecosystem. Qafila elevates this outlook for eligible communities across the region through shared participation and access to locally available products and services. Admissible participants can participate in activities across the Binance platform, including trading, Simple Earn and community referral activities, subject to applicable market rules. Qafila offers a total reward pool of US$1 million in USDC to support the experience, with tasks, eligibility and rewards varying by market and user. Binance says this regional initiative translates into a “shared journey” shaped by different ambitions, practical needs, and ways of participating in digital finance. This page was produced by The National in partnership with Binance

title: Europe's summer heatwaves 'caused 50,000 excess deaths'
description: Analysis of more than 850 European cities found tens of thousands of deaths during peak summer months
content: Europe's hottest summer on record may have killed more than 50,000 people across 30 European countries, researchers have found, as they called on governments to reduce the use of fossil fuels. Scientists from Imperial College London and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine examined excess heat deaths in 854 cities in Europe from June 1 to August 31 this year, comparing it to data for the same period dating back to the year 2000. The modelled death toll of 50,391 was the highest in the research covering the past 26 years, far in excess of the next highest in 2022, when about 29,000 excess heat -related deaths occurred and 2003, with around 18,000 excess deaths. The summers of 2022 and 2003 involved record-breaking heatwaves. This summer, late June was especially severe , with almost a third of deaths happening from June 17 to July 1, when the daily mean temperature across Europe was more than 5°C above the 1991-2020 average. The heat was a danger only for elderly people. An estimated 6,000 people under the age of 65 are thought to have died as a result of heatwaves during summer this year. Cities in Europe's major economies had the highest total estimated heat-related deaths. The highest was in Italy, where 13,303 excess deaths from higher temperatures were recorded, followed by France (7,268), Spain (6,824), Germany (6,340) and the UK (4,354). The study also analysed weather data and climate models to compare how summer temperatures have changed between today's climate and pre-industrial temperatures. They found that two thirds of the excess heat deaths could be attributable of global warming , “primarily as the result of burning fossil fuels”. The findings were published as two peer-reviewed papers in the journal Nature Health on Friday. Though the findings provide an estimate, the modelling method used has been found to produce results in line with the records of excess deaths published by national health authorities for previous heat waves. Dr Claire Barnes, a co-author of the report from the Centre of Environmental Policy at University College London, called for “target interventions” to protect people in summers to come. “These numbers are a stark reminder that our hotter, more extreme summers are having an increasingly severe impact on public health,” she said. “Behind these statistics are real people whose lives were lost and real families who grieve for them.” The findings also reflected the “growing need to rapidly transition away from fossil fuels to slow the pace of change and limit future warming”. The research comes as the UK government has approved the controversial Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea, in a move opposed by environmental campaigners. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the move was needed to protect British consumers from rising energy costs. “At a time when people are really struggling, it's right that we look in a responsible way at maximising the existing energy reserves we have in Britain that could help. “Even on our ambitious climate path, we’ll still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come. That’s why we’re taking a pragmatic approach to the North Sea.” The report's authors also called for cities to adapt to hotter weather. “It is becoming increasingly clear our cities are poorly adapted to rising heat and it is critical we improve our efforts towards adaptation,” said co-author Dr Pierre Masselot of the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. “This means cooling the cities through more green spaces and less pollution, and providing health care for affected populations.” The excess deaths and emergencies from heat also put additional strain on British hospitals, that was comparable to a “really bad winter virus season”, according to Prof Andrew Hartle, an intensive care consultant at the Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust. Hospital buildings and equipment have also not adapted to the heat, he added. “Here in the UK, the summer is historically the quietest time for our health service. This summer, however, saw demand and strain that was akin to a really bad winter virus season. “Patients already in hospital have also been overheating, with much of the UK’s hospital estate largely not built to withstand these temperatures, and there are serious risks to equipment from heat too,” he said.

title: Premier League predictions: Villa end Man City's perfect start, Chelsea beat Spurs in derby thriller
description: We pick out the winners and losers from the latest round of English top-flight fixtures
content: Ipswich showed some fight at Manchester City last weekend before eventually falling to a 3-2 defeat and have now lost four out of their last six games. But the Tractor Boys remain safely mid-table in 10th place on nine points. Forest's home loss to Arsenal means Oliver Glasner's side – sitting one point and one place off rock bottom – are looking to avoid a fourth successive defeat. Prediction: Ipswich 1 Forest 1 It has been a good week for Villa who followed up their victory at Newcastle United last weekend by easing past Viking in the Uefa Champions League on Wednesday, when they made it three wins from three in Europe. Unai Emery's men have now lost just once in nine matches across all competitions. Man City's victory over Ipswich maintained their perfect Premier League start after taking maximum points from seven matches – a club record . They also returned to winning ways in the Champions League, after last week's loss to title holders Paris Saint-Germain, when they thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, with Phil Foden grabbing a hat-trick. Prediction: Villa 2 Man City 2 Arsenal's gritty 1-0 win at Forest meant they kept the pressure on leaders Man City who lead the Gunners by three points. Mikel Arteta's men then drew at Bayern Munich on Wednesday, thanks to Declan Rice's late leveller. But Arsenal suffered a body blow in Germany when Bukayo Saka limped off after just 10 minutes with a thigh problem which could rule him out for next few weeks. Everton home loss to Chelsea was their first of the season but the Merseysiders have now won just once in six league matches, with four of those being draws. They are eighth in the standings on 10 points. Prediction: Arsenal 2 Everton 1 Coventry failed to make it three wins on the spin when they were beaten 3-1 at Spurs leaving them one point and once place above third-bottom Fulham. Fulham registered their first victory at the seventh attempt when they edged out Hull City 1-0 at Craven Cottage, thanks to Alex Iwobi's deflected strike, despite having Ryan Sessegnon sent off in injury-time. Prediction: Coventry 1 Fulham 3 Chelsea head into this London derby on the back of two successive wins, the last which a 2-0 victory at Everton courtesy of Pedro Neto's double which leaves them fourth in the table. The result was marred by an injury to goalkeeper Emi Martinez who was carried off on a stretcher after breaking his jaw in a clash of heads that left him needing surgery. Spurs ended their wait for three points by beating Coventry 3-1 at home which saw James Maddison, making his first start since April 2025 due to a serious knee injury, open the scoring with a superb finish. Victory lifted Robert de Zerbi's side off the bottom and up to 16th place. Prediction: Chelsea 3 Spurs 2 Palace manager Pierre Sage is fighting to keep his job after last weekend's 5-0 humiliation at Brighton which means the Eagles have the worst defensive record in the top-flight after conceding 17 goals in seven matches. In the Europa League on Thursday, Palace drew 2-2 away to Besiktas. Newcastle's home defeat to Villa means the Magpies have won only once in five games, losing three out of their previous four. Matthias Jaissle's side are 11th in the table on eight points, one above Palace. Prediction: Palace 0 Newcastle 2 Hull have now taken one point from a possible nine, after losing to Fulham last time out, and have not won since beating Coventry on August 29. But the Tigers remain in the top half having drawn three of their last five games. Brentford lost for the first time this season when they lost at home to Liverpool after having Yehor Yarmoliuk and Vitaly Janelt sent off. The Bees have drawn four of their seven matches and are sixth in the table, one point above Hull. Prediction: Hull 1 Brentford 1 Liverpool will be looking for a third win on eight days having beaten Brentford and then Villarreal in the Champions League, the latter a 4-3 thriller at Anfield with Alexis Mac Allister hitting a brace and teenager Rio Ngumoha setting up two goals. The Reds are one point and one place outside the Premier League top four. Brighton's flying start to the season goes on after hammering five past Palace, making it five successive wins which leaves them in third place – two points behind Arsenal. The Seagulls faced Jablonec in the Uefa Conference League on Thursday and came away from the Czech Republic with a 0-0 draw. Prediction: Liverpool 2 Brighton 2 Man United's problems ramped on Wednesday when they were battered 4-1 at Como in the Champions League, after which captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned the tactics of manager Michael Carrick. The Red Devils have now gone seven games without a win across all competitions, their worst run since 2015, while also dropping down to 13th in the domestic league and 21st in Europe. Bournemouth sealed their first win of the campaign by beating Sunderland 2-0 with Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson scoring. Marco Rose's first three points as a Premier League manager lifted his team out of the bottom three. The Cherries then prevailed 3-0 against Italian giants AC Milan in the Europa League on Thursday. Prediction: Man United 3 Bournemouth 2 Sunderland have dropped down to bottom spot after four consecutive defeats and taking one point from a possible 15. Their trek to Poland to take on Lech Poznan in the Europa League saw the Black Cats draw 1-1 on Thursday. Leeds' home draw with Manchester United means Daniel Farke's side have lost just once in the league this season and sit seventh in the standings, although they have drawn four of their previous six games. Prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 2

title: Cristiano Ronaldo seeks redemption as Rodgers eyes Al Qadsiah record in Al Hilal clash
description: Portuguese star hopes to put difficult week behind him as Al Nassr take on Al Faisaly
content: Brendan Rodgers will be doubly motivated for the latest round of the Saudi Pro League when Al Qadsiah face heavyweights Al Hilal on Friday. Al Qadsiah have emerged as the surprise league leaders this campaign after 10 games, one point ahead of Hilal who have played one match fewer due to the rescheduling of games. For Rodgers, maintaining their lead at the top will be the main target at the Prince Saud bin Jalawi Stadium in Dammam, mainly because Hilal have a rearranged SPL fixture later in the season (v Al Riyadh on December 19) up their sleeve. But Rodgers will have his sights on another prize. The former Celtic boss, who guided Qadsiah to fourth in the league last season, is now on the verge of becoming the most successful manager in the club’s history. Al Qadsiah’s last-gasp win over Al Taawoun took Rodgers to 26 league wins, equalling the record set by former boss Michel. Victory over Hilal will allow the Northern Irishman to occupy the top spot by himself. Qadsiah will be aiming to raise their game substantially after being held goalless for over 90 minutes by relegation-threatened Al Taawoun. They needed Tijjani Reijnders, summer signing from Manchester City , to score the winner in the sixth minute of stoppage time and maintain their top spot. Meanwhile, Cristiano Ronaldo will be desperate for some positive news after a spate of setbacks on and off the pitch. This week, Ronaldo was given a 30-day suspension and ordered to pay a fine of €255 as punishment for walking out on the national team. Ronaldo had left Portugal's base in Copenhagen ⁠ahead of their Uefa Nations League match against Denmark earlier this month over disagreements over his role in the team. Thereafter, Ronaldo stumbled badly on the pitch as Al Nassr scraped past Neom at Al Awwal Park. The Portuguese superstar looked set to score his 982nd career goal but failed to convert a penalty just before half-time. His bad week continued as Ronaldo wasted another great chance, firing over the crossbar from close range after being set up by Sadio Mane. Nassr still managed to complete a 1-0 win but will need to up their game against Al Faisaly on Friday. Manager Ange Postecoglou tried his best to defend Ronaldo. “This is the nature of football, and it is good that we create this number of chances, and we will work on making up for the mistakes,” he said. “We work as a family, so a win will be good for everyone and a loss will fall upon the whole team, so we must support one another and move forward.” Ronaldo was in the news once again when former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag questioned his ​fitness ​and preparation during a second ⁠stint at the club. Under Dutchman Ten Hag, Ronaldo struggled in the 2022/23 season, scoring once in 10 league appearances before leaving the club in ⁠November 2022. Despite the negativity, Ronaldo will have his sights firmly set on his next big target; the 41-year-old is 19 short of the 1,000 career goals landmark.

title: UFC in Abu Dhabi: 'Street Fighter' Volkanovski says Evloev has plenty, but not enough to beat him
description: Fighters faced off for the final time at UFC 333 pre-fight press conference
content: Alexander Volkanovski arrived at the UFC 333 pre-fight press conference on Thursday sporting a new look. The Australian's distinctive bald head was covered by a blond wig as he dressed up as his character "Joe" in the Hollywood movie Street Fighter . Volkanovski, 38, will put his UFC featherweight title on the line against the undefeated Movsar Evloev in the headline bout at UFC 333 on Saturday. If he has his hand raised at Etihad Arena, he will surpass the legendary Jose Aldo for most title fight wins in the 145-pound division with nine. Volkanovski (28-4) said he respects Evloev, an elite wrestler and the No 1 contender. He admires the Russian's all-round game but said despite his credentials, Evloev's skills pale in comparison to his own. "I believe I've seen that puzzle before, but he's undefeated and knows how to win, but I just don't think that's enough," he said. "He's got all the skills; he can take it anywhere. I think he's the most well-rounded [fighter], but I think I get my hand raised 'And still ...' once again." Volkanovski is in his second reign as champion, and another victory will only add to his claims as the greatest featherweight in history. Evloev, dressed in a three-piece suit and flat cap in the style of Tommy Shelby's character in the hit show Peaky Blinders , has yet to taste defeat in his 20-fight career, a fact Volkanovski wants to change. "He doesn't have a loss yet. So, that's something that I want to take from him." Evloev, 32, earned his shot at gold with a victory over Lerone Murphy earlier this year. He elected to stand and trade with the Englishman before a point deduction for a low blow forced him to revert to type and grapple. Volkanovski urged his opponent to stick to his strengths but warned that it would be he who dictates where the fight goes. "I think he could have made that fight look a lot easier. You could see he was the better fighter. But like I said, just don't try that on me; come bring your best game. Try and take me down," said Volkanovski. "If it's going to be forced on the feet, it's because I'm going to make it be on the feet. And this will be the most dangerous we've ever seen Mov because he's never been forced to fight on the feet. So, he can't panic shoot. He's going to have to panic punch. Let's see how dangerous he is on his feet." Evloev said he was ready to throw down wherever the fight takes place and that he will make Volkanovski eat his words. "I don't have a game plan. I can solve everything. He brings striking, OK, no problem. If you want to be knocked out, I'll do that. But when he says I cannot take him down or something, with all respect to the champ, I can do anything I want, and I'll prove it." The co-main event sees Petr Yan defend the UFC bantamweight championship he took from Merab Dvalishvili last December. There has been plenty of bad blood in the build-up. Saturday will be the third meeting between two of the best 135-pounders of their generation. Dvalishvili won the first encounter and hopes to close out the trilogy with another win. If he is to do so, he will have to do it in his opponent's territory. The biggest cheer was reserved for the Russian champion, and there is no doubt he will enjoy the majority of the support from the crowd come fight night. As has been the case all week, Dvalishvili was unfazed and got a big pop of his own when he name-checked the city where he hopes to reclaim the title. "Saturday night, this is my territory. I love Abu Dhabi and Abu Dhabi loves me, right? Let's go!," said the Georgian, who has 21 wins against five losses. "I'm the king, bro. People always will be with me because I love people and they love me. They support me and I'm grateful for that. "Mentally, I'm very strong. You know, all I have to do is just bring myself in the octagon Saturday and everything will be good. I believe in myself and I believe in my style. I can beat him this time." Yan said that his recent victory over Dvalishvili will count for little this time around. "Guys, for me this is a new fight. I don't want to think about the last fight. Today I have a big goal: I want to smash this guy. I want to defend my title," said Yan. The Russian (20-5) will be fighting in Abu Dhabi for the fifth time and has fond memories of the UAE capital. He beat Jose Aldo to win the bantamweight title for the first time in 2020 and has followed that up with wins over Corey Sandhagen and Marcus McGhee. "Abu Dhabi for me is the best place. I remember 2020 when I was here and win my belt against Jose Aldo, and I have already defended my title here [against Sandhagen]," Yan said, "And on 24 October, I smash this guy one more time."

title: Dressmaker and eight simulator games that make everyday tasks surprisingly fun
description: These games find entertainment in the art of doing one thing well
content: Not every video game needs an elaborate story, a sprawling open world or enemies to defeat. Sometimes, the simple satisfaction of completing a task is enough to keep players entertained for hours. Simulation games have found creative ways to turn ordinary activities into absorbing experiences. Whether making coffee, repairing a car or painting a picture, players can explore different crafts without the expense, mess or consequences of attempting them in real life. Some reproduce the tools and techniques of their chosen activity with surprising attention to detail. Others encourage experimentation, allowing players to make mistakes and discover their own approach. The recent success of Dressmaker on Steam is a compelling example of this appeal. Here are nine games that make the seemingly ordinary entertaining. Released on September 21, Dressmaker has become an unlikely hit on Steam , attracting more than 11,000 purchaser reviews in less than three weeks, with an overwhelmingly positive reception. Developed by Cozy Lives, the game turns sewing into a surprisingly involved creative process. Players operate a dressmaking shop, choosing fabrics, arranging patterns, cutting material and stitching garments together using a virtual sewing machine. Every decision, down to the placement of a button or lace trim, affects the finished dress. There are customers to satisfy, commissions to complete and plenty of opportunities for experimentation. Those feeling mischievous can even deliberately produce terrible outfits. Few creative pursuits are as satisfying to watch as a lump of clay being transformed into a carefully shaped vase. Master of Pottery places that process in the player's hands. Inspired by traditional Chinese pottery techniques, the game recreates several stages of ceramic production, including shaping, firing, painting and glazing. Players can experiment with different forms and decorative patterns before exhibiting their finished works in a personal showroom. Visitors have their own preferences, and successful creations can attract buyers. First available in early access in 2019 before its full release in September 2026, the game combines artistic experimentation with the pleasure of gradually building a collection of handmade objects. Anyone who has watched a barista prepare an elaborate coffee order might have wondered whether they could do a better job. Espresso Tycoon offers the opportunity to find out, albeit with considerably more responsibility than making the occasional cappuccino does. Its 3D coffee editor allows players to experiment with ingredients and create customised drinks, while customer preferences help determine which recipes succeed. The simulation also places players in charge of running a cafe. Hiring employees, managing supplies, decorating the premises and balancing finances are all part of the experience. It is an interesting combination of culinary creativity and entrepreneurship, particularly for anyone who has entertained the idea of opening their own coffee shop. Gardening requires patience, attention and an understanding that plants rarely grow according to a convenient schedule. Garden Life captures much of that process while removing some of its frustrations. Players inherit an abandoned community garden and gradually restore it by planting flowers , removing weeds, watering plants and pruning overgrown vegetation. Its gardening mechanics draw on real techniques, while a procedural growth system allows individual plants to develop differently depending on their surroundings. There are also neighbours to help, flowers to sell and new areas to unlock. For players without access to a garden or those whose real plants have a habit of dying, it offers an inviting alternative. Artistic ambition meets a wonderfully absurd premise in SuchArt , which places players in the role of a supposedly brilliant artist living in the year 2130. Working from a studio in space, they can paint almost anything using brushes, palette knives, stencils and a variety of unconventional implements. The game's physics-driven painting system allows colours to mix and different tools to produce distinct textures and strokes. It has also found an appreciative audience, with 97 per cent positive feedback among more than 2,000 English-language Steam reviews. Perhaps its greatest attraction is the absence of artistic restrictions. Players can pursue serious painting projects or cover their surroundings in increasingly chaotic experiments, with no actual studio to clean afterwards. Preparing a meal becomes considerably more complicated when every ingredient, utensil and cooking accident is governed by a physics engine. Cooking Simulator recreates a professional kitchen with ovens, grills, knives, blenders and more than 140 ingredients. Players must chop, season, cook and plate dishes while paying attention to timing and temperature. Developer Big Cheese Studio has reported sales of one million copies of the game and its add-ons, demonstrating the appetite for virtual cooking. While its career mode encourages precision across more than 80 recipes, the sandbox mode is arguably where things become most entertaining. Players can experiment freely, break equipment or accidentally set the kitchen ablaze. It is a game that rewards culinary competence while enthusiastically accommodating incompetence. Modern cars can be intimidating machines, particularly for those who struggle to identify anything beneath the bonnet. Car Mechanic Simulator 2021 attempts to demystify their workings through an extensive virtual workshop featuring more than 4,000 individual parts. Players diagnose mechanical problems, dismantle components, replace damaged equipment and gradually restore vehicles to working condition. There are customer jobs to complete, garages to upgrade, and neglected cars to discover at auctions and junkyards. More ambitious projects involve rebuilding vehicles from almost nothing. The simulation offers an unusually detailed look at automotive maintenance, making it especially appealing to car enthusiasts interested in understanding the mechanical processes behind their favourite machines. There is something strangely mesmerising about watching a filthy surface become clean under a jet of high-pressure water. PowerWash Simulator builds an entire game around that sensation, asking players to remove accumulated dirt from houses, vehicles, playgrounds and other increasingly elaborate locations. Its success has been remarkable. Developer FuturLab announced in March 2025 that the game had reached 17 million players across platforms, a milestone that helped pave the way for a sequel. Different nozzles and cleaning equipment help tackle stubborn grime, while completed jobs earn money for better tools. There are no elaborate strategies to devise. Sometimes, the pleasure of seeing a job properly finished is reward enough. Designing stickers sounds like a modest occupation, but Sticky Business turns it into a colourful creative enterprise. Players run an online sticker shop, combining illustrations, shapes and decorative elements to produce original designs. These are arranged into printable sheets, with efficient layouts helping to reduce wasted materials. Customer orders must then be packaged and sent, with additional decorations and little gifts available to personalise each delivery. The game also introduces a gentle narrative element through customers whose stories unfold as they return to the shop. It captures the appeal of running a small creative business, from the satisfaction of designing something original to the pleasure of seeing someone appreciate the finished product.

title: The UN's next leader must be given room to deliver
description: Even an accomplished secretary general cannot overcome every obstacle alone
content: The UN was founded in 1945 on the belief that countries emerging from an apocalyptic global conflict could rebuild and find common ground. Eight decades later, that principle remains important, but as wars multiply and alliances shift, there are growing questions about the organisation’s ability to meet the demands of a fragile world. With its leadership model and institutional structure designed for another era, can the UN to renew itself? As the race to succeed Antonio Guterres as secretary general heats up, the answer to this question becomes even more demanding. A new era with a new leader can give the UN new impetus, even if many of the challenges remain. The candidacy of Lana Nusseibeh , UAE Minister of State and former permanent representative to the UN, brings even more interest to this issue for the UAE and the wider region. Her credentials as a candidate are impressive. Ms Nusseibeh’s diplomatic experience and familiarity with multilateral negotiations make her a serious contender for the secretary general’s office. She represented the UAE during its two-year term as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council in 2022-2023. Her bid deserves real consideration, even as other candidates bring their own considerable strengths. The prospect of an Arab woman from the Middle East leading the world’s foremost multilateral institution is also significant. When long-standing security relationships become less certain, and threats to shipping and regional stability intensify, the international community needs effective diplomacy and co-operation. The UN too often struggles to translate its convening power into action. Its deliberations can be paralysed by divisions among major powers, while its agencies face overlapping responsibilities and limited resources. Such apparent inertia erodes public confidence in multilateralism itself. The next secretary general, whoever it may be, must do more than mediate disputes and issue statements. The office should become a catalyst for institutional reform, with a stronger emphasis on early intervention, effective mediation and better co-ordination between UN agencies. Clear priorities and measurable accountability would help ensure that commitments translate into tangible improvements that people can see. Ms Nusseibeh has spoken of bringing countries together and achieving concrete results. These are welcome ambitions that build on the UAE’s experience of working with states that hold divergent interests. For the UN, which increasingly needs to restore trust across geopolitical divides, such an approach could be rejuvenating. However, even an accomplished secretary general cannot overcome every obstacle alone. Meaningful reform will require member states, particularly the permanent members of the Security Council, to accept that a lack of direction and consensus carries its own costs. The UN remains too important to be allowed to drift into irrelevance. Its next leader must have the vision to renew its purpose, and its member states must give that leader room to deliver. The measure of success is not in promises but results.

title: US lifting sanctions on 'dark fleet' not expected to solve tanker crisis
description: Ship owners wary of sailing across Strait of Hormuz because of risks involved
content: Lifting sanctions on “dark fleet” or shadow fleet vessels is not expected to solve the tanker crisis engulfing oil markets while the Iran war continues and owners remain wary of sailing through the Strait of Hormuz and risking crews' safety. The US move “could provide some relief, particularly around the Arabian Gulf where tanker availability has been strained, but I wouldn't expect it to solve the current tanker crisis”, said Salih Yilmaz, senior industry analyst of energy at Bloomberg Intelligence. The administration of US President Donald Trump this week authorised the sale of sanctioned oil tankers in a move to allow the vessels to start legitimately shipping crude and ease pressure on oil prices that have surged since the outbreak of Iran war in February. “A large share of sanctioned vessels appears to be already operating in Russian, Iranian or other restricted trades rather than sitting idle, so sanctions relief would mainly redistribute existing capacity into mainstream markets,” Mr Yilmaz added. Another big constraint is ship owner’s reluctance to operate in the Arabian Gulf as attacks on tankers continue, killing and injuring crew members. There have been 120 confirmed attacks on ships as of October 22, with 22 seafarer fatalities since the war began in February, according to the latest update from the International Maritime Organisation . Tanker owners are paying as much as $100,000 per month to ship's captains, along with a bonus of $50,000 for each trip, because of risks involved in sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a recent Financial Times report. “The bigger constraint today is the risk of operating around Hormuz. Owners are demanding very high compensation for exposing vessels and crews to attacks,” Mr Yilmaz said. The US government is working with investors who buy idled sanctioned tankers, refurbish them and use them to transport non-sanctioned oil, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said at an event in New York this week. “We’re going to move some of the ships from what I call the ‘bad-guy fleet’ to the ‘good-guy fleet'," Mr Wright said. “They will not carry sanctioned oil any more.” Wanying Zhang, a freight analyst at Vortexa, was also not optimistic about the US move increasing tanker availability in the markets. “Our analysis suggests that any easing of Ofac [Office of Foreign Assets Control] sanctions is unlikely to trigger a significant return of sanctioned tankers to mainstream trades,” she said. “A substantial share of Ofac sanctioned tankers remain subject to UK or EU sanctions, which could continue to restrict their access to European trades even if US restrictions are lifted.” Ofac is a financial intelligence and enforcement agency of the US Treasury Department that administers and enforces economic and trade sanctions based on US foreign policy and national security goals. It has been imposing sanctions on vessels linked to Iran and Russia for carrying crude to global markets. The relatively old age of these vessels could also delay their return to mainstream trade, given potential maintenance, inspection, insurance and commercial requirements. About 70 per cent of Ofac-listed tankers are at least 20 years old which limits the number likely to be accepted by mainstream charterers, analysts added. Ship broker Braemar said 170 very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were currently under US sanctions. It added that only 44 vessels are under 20 years old and acceptable to charterers, with 33 at least 25 years old and 92 between 20 and 24 years old. “Given the advanced age of most the ships sanctioned by the US, and the fact that a lot of the ships sanctioned by the US are also sanctioned by the EU or UK, we do not expect this move to lead to too many extra additions to the available tanker fleet,” said Mary Melton, senior tanker analyst at Braemar.

title: Woman diagnosed with arthritis after 10 years of pain dismissed as stress
description: Diagnosis highlights that condition can affect young people
content: When Afna Shanavas first complained of pain at 16, doctors suspected stress. It would take another 10 years for her to discover she had arthritis. Writing during school exams became increasingly painful, and she was constantly exhausted. But despite visits to specialists, her symptoms were repeatedly treated with painkillers and she was asked to rest. “I knew I was in pain, but people did not believe me,” Ms Shanavas, now 26, said. “My mother took me to orthopaedic and neurological specialists, and the answer was always painkillers. “Because I was doing well in academics and sports, one doctor suggested I was under too much pressure and that my parents were expecting too much from me.” “I was even referred to a psychologist because doctors thought the pain was psychosomatic.” Ms Shanavas, a psychologist, has now finally been diagnosed with inflammatory polyarthropathy and ankylosing spondylitis, two conditions that can cause chronic pain and inflammation. At 17, while in Grade 12, she had experienced a severe episode in which her neck seized up. She was admitted to hospital for emergency treatment amid concerns that she might be having a stroke. Doctors later ruled out a stroke. While recovering in intensive care, Ms Shanavas decided to pursue a career in psychology, hoping to better understand the relationship between the brain and physical health. The cause of her symptoms remained elusive despite consultations with doctors in the UAE and India. However, a minor cut to a finger that refused to heal led to rheumatology tests in Sharjah. “I had never even heard of a rheumatologist , who did an antinuclear antibody test, which helps guide investigations to understand why my finger cut was not healing,” said Ms Shanavas. The ANA test was positive, although several other markers were negative. Ms Shanavas subsequently became pregnant and postponed further investigations. After her pregnancy, her symptoms worsened. It was only then that she underwent further investigations and was diagnosed with inflammatory polyarthropathy and ankylosing spondylitis Inflammatory polyarthropathy, or polyarthritis, is an autoimmune condition that causes inflammation in five or more joints. As a type of arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis usually affects the spine and pelvis, reducing flexibility and leading to a stiff, hunched-over posture. “It was a huge surprise as I thought this was a disease for the elderly,” she said. The conditions are usually only diagnosed in people under 45 following three months of chronic pain and an in-depth evaluation of medical history, a physical examination, internal imaging and blood tests. Ms Shanavas is now urging people to recognise that arthritis can affect young people , too. Ms Shanavas, now head of inclusion and well-being at The Oxford School in Dubai, takes several medications to manage her symptoms. Her treatment schedule includes a biological injection every two weeks that slows down her overactive immune system, as well as multiple probiotics, supplements and corticosteroid creams to manage her flare-ups. She has kept a journal documenting her experiences over the past decade, which she hopes to publish. One of the most difficult aspects of living with the condition, she said, is that its effects are not always visible to others. “The hardest part is that I can look completely fine on the outside,” she said. “People don’t always understand why I need a day off. They cannot see the pain or fatigue. “I have often felt misunderstood because of this.” Arthritis in young people remains relatively rare. It is an umbrella term for more than 100 conditions affecting the joints and surrounding tissues. Symptoms and causes vary, and some forms can begin in childhood or early adulthood. Rheumatoid arthritis is an inflammatory condition that commonly develops in adulthood, while osteoarthritis is associated with changes in the joint's structure and becomes more common with age. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis refers to a group of inflammatory conditions that begin before the age of 16. Dr Humeira Badsha, a rheumatologist in Dubai, said arthritis care was moving away from general pain relief towards precision medicine and individualised therapy. “Treatment is increasingly targeted at the specific inflammatory pathways driving each patient's disease,” she said. “Anyone on chronic, long-term medication needs a thorough baseline medication review before a new drug is started, and regular monitoring afterwards. “Arthritis can appear at any age, depending entirely on the underlying classification.” GLP-1 weight-loss therapies can help arthritis by reducing wear and tear on overstressed joints. Dr Usama Hassan Saleh, a consultant in orthopaedic surgery at the Medcare Orthopaedics and Spine Hospital in Dubai, said genetics can also play a role. “Some forms of arthritis, including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis, have a hereditary component, meaning that having a close relative with the condition may increase a person's risk,” he said. “However, family history does not mean that someone will inevitably develop arthritis, as other lifestyle and environmental factors can also contribute.” Early symptoms include joint pain, stiffness, swelling and difficulty moving the affected area. “Seeking medical advice early can help establish the type of arthritis and ensure that appropriate treatment begins promptly,” said Dr Saleh. “With the right combination of medical care and lifestyle measures, many people can manage their symptoms, remain active and maintain a good quality of life.”

title: UAE confirms oil spill off coast causing strong fuel smell
description: Beaches closed in Umm Al Quwain as authorities seek to stem slick
content: UAE authorities are working to tackle an oil spill from a supertanker in the Arabian Gulf. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirmed the incident early on Friday morning. The spill is the cause of a strong smell that residents of Dubai and the northern emirates have reported in recent days, it said. The ministry did not name the vessel, but international maritime agencies say the Gem No.2 was struck in a suspected Iranian drone attack on October 9 to 10. Twenty-two Indian sailors were rescued from the 330-metre vessel at the time. The extent of the oil slick is unclear, but confirmation of the incident came amid growing concerns about the environmental impact of the Iran war on the Gulf and the Arabian Sea. People in the UAE have in recent days reported an acrid and strong fuel smell in the air. The ministry said there was no health risk from the odour, but advised the public to stay away from any oil that washes ashore. "The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirms the UAE’s technical monitoring and environmental assessment system detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain’s beaches," it said in a statement. "Odours noticed in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain pose no health risks to residents. "Teams immediately began containment, cordoning, clean-up and remediation with local and federal authorities to limit environmental impacts. Precautionary coastal surveys, monitoring and assessments continue to gauge impacts and protect the marine environment. "With relevant authorities, the ministry has temporarily closed all Umm Al Quwain beaches and coastal areas until technical teams complete assessments and identify safety and marine protection measures. Fishermen and sea users are urged to follow authorities’ instructions and avoid fishing in affected areas." Dr Diana Francis, an associate professor and head of the Environmental and Geophysical Sciences Lab at Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi, said oil spills caused by the regional conflict could create odours. “When an oil spill happens, it continues to move with the currents unless it is removed and cleaned completely,” she told The National before the ministry confirmed the oil slick incident. “Several spills can also move with the currents and accumulate in favourable gyre [rotating ocean current] areas. Then with time, heat and winds, they evaporate into the air and give off fuel-like odours. “Oil doesn't mix with water. It continues to float until it is removed or evaporate with time.” Prashant Kumar, professor of air quality and health at the University of Surrey in the UK, said air pollution – and the smells that it brings with it – can travel over long distances. “The smell can travel tens of kilometres,” he said, in comments also made before the ministry's statement on Friday. “It depends on the meteorological conditions, it depends on the wind speed and the wind direction. You can easily have the longer-range transport of pollutants from one place to another.” Additional reporting by Daniel Bardsley

title: Will the Iran war resume before the US and Israeli elections?
description: Recent developments have left the Gulf on edge and increased concerns that the US and Israeli could resume strikes
content: Two US aircraft carrier strike groups are in the region, and another is on the way. Families of US government personnel have been ordered to leave Saudi Arabia. And Israel has reportedly conducted a military sortie near the Iranian border. Recent developments have left the Gulf on edge and have increased concerns that the US and Israeli could resume strikes against Iran, perhaps even before Israel's general election on October 27 and the US midterms on November 3. US President Donald Trump said on October 8 that he would not renew attacks against Iran before the midterms. But reports that Washington and Israel are preparing for renewed military operations have raised questions about whether the conflict could escalate before then. On Wednesday, the US State Department ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. Some interpreted this to mean an attack against Iran was coming, especially amid reports that personnel could be withdrawn from other countries. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the order applies only to Saudi Arabia and was prompted by the threat from Yemen's Houthis, who have attacked Saudi airports and other critical sites. But another State Department representative said that "the hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly, including beyond that immediate area”. Alex Vatanka, director of the Iran programme at the Middle East Institute in Washington, said Iranian officials appeared to view a renewed conflict as a real possibility and he warned that the political thinking around both elections could influence decisions about whether to escalate. “It’s not so much the logic of the war that might be in the driver’s seat; it’s the logic of the politics, particularly in Israel, that might be in the driver’s seat,” Mr Vatanka said. Quoting senior Iranian officials and a US official, Drop Site News reported that Washington and Israel believe large-scale bombing could begin before Israel's election. An unidentified senior Iranian official told the outlet that Tehran's intelligence assessment indicated a high likelihood of an attack before October 27, with Israel potentially striking Iranian air defences first to clear the way for US bombers.
