Iran's national security chief, Mohsen Rezaei , has repeatedly said that Iran can continue missile and drone attacks against US assets across the region if fighting resumes. He has also warned that Tehran could widen its targets to include data centres, artificial intelligence sites and undersea cables, he warned. Mr Vatanka said he did not think the strike would come before the US and Israeli elections. "If I had to had to gamble, I'll say it's unlikely to happen," he said. "Any new round [of fighting] is just going to be that much more devastating for the region. And when the region is devastated, US interests are also going to suffer massively. I do suspect that's going to be one of those areas where Trump might be sensitive to pressure." Quoting US officials and other sources, The New York Times reported on Wednesday that the US and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the midterms. The proposed campaign could attack Iranian energy and nuclear sites, and missile and drone arsenals, with the aim of forcing Tehran to make diplomatic concessions. The report said a strike before the midterms had not been entirely ruled out, however, and that Mr Trump could ultimately decide against further military action. Still, he has hinted at renewed strikes after the midterms. At last month's UN General Assembly, he said he was deciding whether to annihilate Iran. And in a Newsmax interview on October 15, he spoke about the Mother of All Bombs, the largest non-nuclear device in the Pentagon's arsenal, but he did not say if he would use it against Iran. Mr Trump and Mr Netanyahu launched the Iran conflict on February 28. The Trump administration initially projected the war would only last a few weeks but it has been unable to topple the regime in Tehran, strike a durable deal or completely defeat Iran militarily. If Mr Trump and Mr Netanyahu do resume the war, the consequences could be devastating for the region, Mr Vatanka said, with Iran threatening to retaliate against Israel and Gulf states, as well as US interests. Axios on Wednesday reported that dozens of Israeli Air Force fighter jets conducted a "power projection" sortie this week, close to the Iranian border.

title: Aipac ends US candidate endorsements as backlash over Israel grows
description: Powerful pro-Israel lobby will continue spending on campaign adverts through its super Pac amid tension in Michigan Senate race
content: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee, the most powerful pro-Israel lobby in the US, said it would no longer endorse candidates or make direct campaign contributions, as debate intensifies over American aid to Israel, the Gaza war and the influence of outside money in elections. Instead, the group will continue operating through its United Democracy Project committee, known as a super Pac, which is allowed to raise unlimited amounts for campaign advertising but is not allowed to co-ordinate with candidates, Jewish Insider first reported. The development comes amid growing criticism of Aipac , particularly within the Democratic Party, and declining support for Israel among Americans after the war in Gaza. Aipac began contributing directly to politicians in 2022. Polls show a substantial shift in American public opinion on Israel and US policy towards the country, particularly among Democrats and independents. Jim Manley, a Democratic strategist, said Aipac had become “radioactive” for many candidates. “I was surprised that Aipac did that,” Mr Manley said. “Aipac typically signifies a very aggressive posture towards politics. They're not in the habit of backing away from a fight.” He said the move could become a “major headache” for Democratic leaders, including House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries and Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer, who have received contributions from Aipac's political network. Aipac did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It told NPR that its strategy remained unchanged despite the decision to end direct campaign contributions and candidate endorsements. "Our goal is to build support for the US-Israel relationship,” spokeswoman Deryn Sousa told NPR, adding that Aipac members had given more than $90 million directly to candidates during the current election cycle and that such giving would “continue and increase”. But Trita Parsi, a political analyst in Washington, said it was "hard to overstate" the significance of the development. "Historically, Aipac sustained an aura of invincibility that ensured it won most battles by walkover. If you are perceived as invincible, the other side doesn't even bother to fight you," Mr Parsi said on X. "Rather than invincibility, Aipac's name now carries such toxicity that the group doesn't want its own name on its political donations." The decision, observers say, changes how Aipac channels political money, rather than its political involvement. Ending formal endorsements and direct contributions could help candidates avoid the political fallout of receiving the group's explicit backing. The move is likely to have an almost immediate impact in Michigan , a battleground state where the Senate race is being closely watched and Aipac spending and US policy towards Israel have become major campaign issues. Aipac's involvement in the race has been particularly contentious. Its super Pac spent more than $30 million seeking to defeat Abdul El-Sayed in the Democratic primary and backing Representative Haley Stevens, a staunch supporter of Israel. It was the organisation’s largest single investment in a single contest. Mr El-Sayed, an Egyptian-American physician and a progressive candidate, won the nomination in August, in a major setback for the pro-Israel lobby. The group later continued its involvement in the race with advertising opposing Mr El-Sayed as he faces Republican Mike Rogers, an ally of President Donald Trump, in the November 3 midterm elections. Mr Rogers was initially wary of Aipac's involvement, concerned that the group's unpopularity could hurt his campaign amid declining support for Israel among some Republicans. He later publicly welcomed support from the group. Mr El-Sayed, who is endorsed by Senator Bernie Sanders, has called for an end to US military aid to Israel and described Israel's war in Gaza as a genocide. If he wins he would become the first Muslim US senator. "Aipac is now spending as much as $9 million against Abdul El-Sayed," Mr Sanders wrote on X. "Aipac is why we’re at war in Iran. Aipac is why the US has supported genocide in Gaza. We must say no to Aipac." This week, Aipac directed about $9 million to a group supporting Mr Rogers, according to The Washington Post . The money was reported as independent political spending, rather than a direct contribution to his campaign.

title: Dubai Municipality reveals plan to keep city safe from impact of heavy rain
description: 10 temporary water collection lakes prepared to help offer respite from flooding
content: Dubai Municipality has unveiled its new strategy to keep the emirate safe from heavy flooding caused by excessive rainfall . The authority has prepared 10 temporary water collection lakes in "strategic locations to accommodate rainwater runoff in the event of heavy rainfall and reduce pressure on the main drainage networks", Dubai Media Office reported on Thursday. A response team of 675 people, including engineers, supervisors, administrative staff, drivers and field workers will be available round the clock to deal with any emergencies, according to the statement. "Dubai Municipality has established an integrated and proactive response system that brings together specialised teams, advanced equipment and flexible operational plans to strengthen our preparedness for the rainy season," said Eng Adel Mohammed Al Marzouqi, chief executive of the Waste and Sewerage Agency at Dubai Municipality, head of the Municipality's Emergency, Crisis and Disaster Management Team, and head of the Rainwater Drainage Team. "Our priority is to ensure that infrastructure and emergency resources are ready to respond effectively to changing weather conditions, manage rainwater accumulation and address reports according to their urgency and the requirements of each location. "These preparations are supported by continuous monitoring, preventive maintenance and close coordination with our strategic partners. Through this approach, we aim to safeguard people and property, maintain the continuity of services and minimise disruption to everyday life across Dubai." Earlier this month, The National reported how Dubai’s rainwater drainage capacity is set to increase sevenfold under a Dh30 billion infrastructure project designed to protect the emirate from extreme weather and serve its growing population for the next century.

title: Can Netanyahu bomb Iran as a caretaker PM? How US and Israeli elections could affect war
description: US and Israel both head to polls as leaders hint at new military action against Iran
content: The US and Israel are hinting at new military action against Iran as both countries are preparing to vote in elections that could affect the course of the war. The Israeli general election on October 27 and the US midterms on November 3, are the biggest tests of public opinion for either country's leaders since they began the conflict in February. In Israel, polls suggest stalemate in which neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main opponent Gadi Eisenkot have a majority – although this would not prevent Mr Netanyahu ordering strikes while coalition talks take place. US President Donald Trump largely has a free hand constitutionally but a heavy midterm defeat could increase domestic friction over the war. Here is what to know about the elections and the war: Once Israel elects a new parliament, it could be weeks or months before a coalition is formed. Mr Netanyahu would remain in office as a caretaker, with no formal limits on his powers – meaning he could still order military action against Iran. There is no firm rule against caretaker governments embarking on major ventures, as is the norm in some countries. Still, opposition leader Yair Lapid was quoted by Israeli media as saying they should not act to “fundamentally change reality”. In August 2022, Mr Lapid was caretaker prime minister – although before an election rather than after – when Israel launched three days of strikes on Gaza . It has also been speculated that Mr Netanyahu could exploit a crisis to form a wartime unity government, bringing in members of the opposition. Mr Netanyahu is promising to maintain his hardline doctrine if he wins another term. Most opposition leaders also favour attacking Iran and oppose Palestinian statehood. Americans are electing a new Congress as well as choosing governors in many states. Mr Trump is in office until 2029 and his authority as commander-in-chief of the military is independent of majorities in Congress. That means Mr Trump could order a new assault on Iran at any time. Early this month he said the US would not attack Iran “at any time prior to the midterm elections” but did not rule out strikes after that. Still, defeat for Mr Trump's Republicans could narrow his options politically. With high energy prices likely to be blamed, causing further disruption to the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf energy exports would risk deepening his unpopularity. A Democratic-controlled Congress could also launch investigations into the war, potentially embarrass the administration. US military assistance to Israel, sanctions on Iran and Washington's relationships with governments across the Gulf could all become subjects of deeper scrutiny.

title: Turkey and Canada launch strategic partnership
description: Erdogan and Carney pledge to forge closer ties in energy and defence
content: Turkey and Canada launched a strategic partnership on Thursday, pledging to forge closer ties in energy and defence as global instability prompts nations around the world to reinforce their militaries and energy supply chains. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara as part of a two-day trip to Turkey, the first official visit by a Canadian premier to the country. The two Nato members signed agreements on defence co-operation and energy, and agreed to increase flights to boost trade and travel, Mr Erdogan and Mr Carney said in a press conference. Buffeted by energy price shocks from the US-Iran war, Turkey has had to revise its inflation targets and is keen to secure energy and fuel imports, including from Canada, as well as supplies of critical raw minerals. “From mining to LNG [liquefied natural gas], from critical minerals to nuclear energy, a broad area of co-operation exists,” Mr Erdogan said. The strategic partnership was not merely a symbolic move that would “remain on paper”, he added. After mounting tension with the US had prompted Canada to develop other relationships, the new partnership with Turkey is backed up by a three-year action plan focusing on trade and investment, defence and security, energy and “people-to-people ties”, Mr Carney said. On Friday he will meet Turkish business leaders in Istanbul before free-trade agreement talks start next month. The two countries aim to increase trade volume from its current level of $3 billion to $10 billion, Mr Erdogan said, without providing a time frame. “Our objectives are clear: more trade between businesses to build more prosperity between our peoples,” Mr Carney said. Turkey is aiming to cement its role as a key “middle-power” player of the sort that Canada wants to forge closer relationships with, according to Sinan Ulgen, a former Turkish diplomat. “On a more strategic level, this visit emphasises Turkey's foreign policy orientation, which is to diversify its traditional foreign policy by way of strengthening its ties with what Carney has called this universe of middle powers,” Mr Ulgen, who now runs the Edam think tank in Istanbul, told The National. “Within that universe, Turkey aspires to play a major role,” As Mr Carney arrived in Turkey, human rights groups encouraged him to raise concerns about what they describe as increasing authoritarianism in the country. Amnesty International called on Mr Carney to raise concerns with Mr Erdogan about curbs on democratic freedom, following recent arrests of activists, journalists and opposition politicians. “Prime Minister Carney can and must demand the protection of those most at risk,” said Ketty Nivyabandi, secretary general of Amnesty International Canada’s English-speaking section.

title: France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda after patient dies
description: Man had been admitted to hospital in Lyon with an unrelated serious disease
content: France reported the first human case ⁠of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock on Thursday in a hospital patient who died, though authorities said there was no risk to the general population. It is suspected that the victim was bitten ⁠by a midge carrying the virus in eastern France where it had circulated among animals this spring ​and ⁠summer, the government said in ‌a statement. The man has been admitted to hospital in Lyon with an unrelated serious disease, a French Health Ministry ​official said. The victim was in his 60s and lived in the Lyon area, the newspaper Le Progres reported. The UN's World Health Organisation said it was in contact with French authorities about the outbreak. “Based on current information and knowledge of the transmission of closely related viruses, this is an isolated human case and it is unlikely to lead to wider spread at this time,” said the Geneva-based WHO , which co-ordinates responses to international public health issues and emergencies. Gregory Emery, head of France's health directorate, told reporters: “We are clearly dealing with a case that is unprecedented from a scientific and virological point of view. It is linked to this man's severely weakened immune system. From a medical and public health point of view, there is no alert and no crisis.” Shamonda is transmitted by biting midges and most ‌commonly found in cattle, though it has ⁠also been found in horses, alpaca, sheep and ​goats, according to the World Organisation for Animal Health. There has been no report ​of cattle-to-human ‌or human-to-human transmission, Mr Emery said. The virus is not classified as a disease under the EU Animal Health Law and ⁠not subject to official surveillance or control measures. Identified in Nigeria in the mid-1960s, Shamonda ⁠was first confirmed in Europe in late July after genomic tests on sick cattle in southern Germany, Switzerland and eastern France. France's weekly animal health surveillance bulletin said it had also been detected in Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain and Jersey. The virus has several ​effects on animals, with infected cattle showing diarrhoea, weakness, loss of appetite and, less often, fever, French animal health authorities said. A study of nine French dairy farms found milk production fell by up to 75 per cent.

title: UAE regulator reviews AIX Financial Consultations amid investor claims and payment concerns
description: CMA says it is conducting inquiry under its regulatory mandate and legal procedures
content: The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said it is reviewing AIX Financial Consultations' activities after receiving information that the company had delayed or even missed payouts. Without disclosing the details of the information it received or the nature of the review, the CMA said it would keep the matter confidential to ensure a thorough, fair and impartial assessment. A case has been filed with the Dubai International Financial Centre ( DIFC ) Courts against AIX Financial Group's Cayman Islands affiliate, AIX Secure SPV Ltd. Carl Marcus Detloff issued the claim in August concerning nine note subscription agreements entered into between June 2023 and August 2025. Mr Detloff alleges that AIX Secure SPV failed to make interest payments when due and contends this entitled him to terminate their agreement. He seeks repayment of invested capital of £925,000, €240,000, and $309,692, along with unpaid interest payments and an additional $900,000 he claims is owed under the agreements. AIX Secure SPV, represented by Pinsent Masons, has not yet stated its position publicly. In a statement published on AIX Investment Group's website, AIX Secure SPV said “geopolitical uncertainty and significant volatility across global financial markets has affected valuations and investment realisation cycles within a limited part of AIX's product offering”. The majority of AIX's products and their underlying investments have not been affected, it added, and AIX continues to meet its obligations to investors under those products and investments. AIX Financial Consultation is regulated by the CMA and specialises in wealth management, retirement planning and portfolio diversification. The statement said it had appointed leading international law firms, and financial and restructuring advisers to provide support, including in its communications with the relevant authorities. “Following a comprehensive review, measures relating to the restructuring of the affected investments are now being taken forward under the direct oversight of management and subject to the applicable approvals. The aim is to protect value, maintain stability and determine the most appropriate path forward for affected investors.” According to the Financial Times , investors have filed claims seeking to recover about $10 million, including two individual claims for $2 million and $8 million. Dubai-based AIX Investment Group, an international investment advisory firm, reportedly suspended payments to thousands of investors after promising annual returns of up to 30 per cent. The CMA said it is conducting the review under its regulatory mandate and legal procedures. It will provide updates through official channels and will urge the public and market participants to rely on authorised sources for verified information.

title: Sheikh Abdullah discusses regional security with Cypriot Foreign Minister
description: UAE and Cyprus discuss bilateral ties and Middle East stability in high-level call
content: Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, spoke with his Cypriot counterpart on Thursday to discuss bilateral relations and the deteriorating security situation across the Middle East. Sheikh Abdullah held the phone call with Dr Constantinos Kombos, Cyprus's Minister of Foreign Affairs, covering issues affecting both nations and the wider region, state news agency Wam reported. The two ministers reviewed the current state of strategic relations between the UAE and Cyprus, exploring avenues to strengthen co-operation in ways that would serve the mutual interests of both countries. The discussion underscored the importance of both nations deepening their bilateral ties.

title: Palisades recovers damaged nuclear fuel assembly, but critics of restart escalate concerns
description: Nuclear regulator recently warned reactor operator over 'chilled work environment' impacting safety
content: A nuclear fuel assembly that had tipped over was successfully retrieved from the soon-to-be-restarted Palisades nuclear reactor in Michigan but controversy over the restart has been escalated to Congress. On Wednesday, owners of the Holtec International reactor said “technical ingenuity” would allow efforts to resume operations at the plant to continue. “When we encounter a challenge, what matters is how we respond,” said Fadi Diya, Holtec's chief nuclear officer. “Our team approached this recovery with the same commitment to safety, technical rigour, and teamwork that has guided our work throughout the restart.” The Palisades reactor, bought by Holtec after being decommissioned in 2022, has become synonymous with a US nuclear energy renaissance induced by the significant energy needs of artificial intelligence data centres. Efforts to restart the reactor in Covert, Michigan, hit a snag in August, when, according to the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), one of the fuel assemblies tipped over during fuelling. The NRC said no radiation was released. However, it was another controversy linked to the Palisades reactor, which first went online in 1971. In 2012, an NRC report warned about the work culture at the plant, where it said safety concerns were routinely dismissed. In 2016, security staff were placed on leave, which was then owned by Entergy, for failing to properly follow fire prevention protocol. And in October 2025, a worker at Palisades fell off a refuelling bridge into a pool of water, though was not seriously injured. Most recently, the NRC sent a letter to Holtec following an inspection that determined that although Palisades maintained a safety-conscious work environment overall, “a chilled work environment” existed in the supply chain and quality assurance departments. “Employees in these two work departments are hesitant to raise safety concerns using all available avenues without fear of retaliation,” the NRC said. Last week, Patrick O’Brien, Holtec's director of government affairs and communications, told The National that Holtec was “taking actions to address these issues and will continue our work to maintain and strengthen a healthy safety-conscious work environment”. Arnie Gundersen, a nuclear engineer and expert adviser for the environmental advocacy group Don't Waste Michigan, has criticised how the Palisades restart is being handled. “In the last four weeks, Palisades lost control and tipped a nuclear fuel bundle and couldn’t get it out, nine out of 15 licensed reactor operators failed their exam, and more than half of the people in their quality assurance and procurement departments feel they will be fired by management if they bring concerns forward,” he said, and yet “ironically … the NRC just gave them permission to begin loading fuel again!” Mr Gundersen recently told The National he has escalated his concerns about the Palisades nuclear restart to US Democratic Senator Edward Markey, a long-time critic of the nuclear industry. “The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has either ignored or rebuffed my safety concerns as an expert witness for the last three years,” Mr Gundersen's letter to Mr Markey reads. “Simply put, restarting the 55-year-old Palisades reactor is unsafe. Holtec is a rookie with no nuclear operating experience and has been entrusted with an incredibly complex, never-before-attempted undertaking.” Michigan's Democratic Governor Gretchen Whitmer has previously praised the Palisades restart efforts, however, and has shown no sign of reversing course. Meanwhile, Holtec on Wednesday insisted that safety is a priority. “Palisades will resume operations when all required work is complete and all applicable federal requirements and industry standards are met,” a press release from the company said. Yet despite taking a victory lap after the company retrieved the tipped nuclear fuel assembly, woes continue to darken the doorstep of Holtec. On Wednesday, according to Law360, a jury in New Jersey found that the company had violated whistleblower laws by firing it's former chief financial officer who said that he refused to make statements about Holtec that he thought were misleading. Holtec told Law360 that it didn't agree with the jury and planned to appeal.

title: Saudi-led coalition denies Houthi claims Riyadh threatened to attack tribal and civilian gatherings
description: Yemeni government and US official accuse Iran-backed group of using public events to recruit children as fighters
content: Saudi-led coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki Al Malki denied claims by the Houthis that Riyadh was to launch attacks on tribal and civilian gatherings in Yemen. “Both the content and timing of these claims reflect ongoing attempts to mislead public opinion, divert attention from the militia’s own crises and practices, and draw members of authentic Yemeni tribes into its conflicts,” he said. Yemeni tribes are an integral part of Yemen's social fabric, Maj Gen Al Malki said. “These bonds are far too deep to be undermined by disinformation campaigns or attempts to sow division and hostility,” he added. Yemen 's internationally recognised government said late on Thursday that a warning issued from its Ministry of Defence had been an "erroneous and unacceptable statement". Defence Minister Taher Al Aqili apologised in a post on X and said an investigation was under way. "We further affirm that our authentic Yemeni Arab tribes are the primary bearers of the project to restore the state, and under no circumstances can we ever stand against them," he said. In a now deleted statement, the government warned residents of Houthi -controlled areas against attending gatherings organised by the Iran-backed group, saying the events were being used to recruit children and young people as fighters. “Any gatherings of this kind will be considered legitimate military targets,” the Defence Ministry said in the deleted post. Neil Hop, US charge d’affaires in Yemen, also accused the Houthis of recruiting children and forcing them to fight on the front lines. “Children everywhere deserve a real childhood, not brainwashing into the Houthi cult of death,” he said in a video published on X by the US embassy in Yemen. He added that reports and videos documented the recruitment of children, putting them at risk of being killed or suffering lasting psychological trauma. He also accused Houthi leaders of taking children from ordinary Yemeni families rather than their own. “It is wrong and it has to end,” Mr Hop said. “Tell the little ayatollah to stop recruiting Yemen’s children for his war,” he added, referring to Houthi leader Abdul-Malik Al Houthi. The remarks came amid escalating hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia , which leads the coalition supporting Yemen's government. The Iran-backed group on Thursday claimed to have attacked the Saudi Defence Ministry in Riyadh, King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, an Aramco site in Yanbu and Abha International Airport in the previous 48 hours. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the attacks were carried out using ballistic missiles and drones. Saudi Arabia said two people were killed in an attack on the airport in Dammam. Another two people were killed and two injured after debris from a drone intercepted by Saudi air defences fell near a processing plant at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, in the Eastern Province. The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday it intercepted and destroyed five drones in the Riyadh and Madinah regions. Mr Saree also claimed that any Saudi threat to strike Yemeni tribes could lead the group to resort to “major options” it had previously avoided. “If it carries out this threat, the consequences will be catastrophic and unforeseen,” he said. It is not clear whether he was referring to the Yemeni Defence Ministry's initial message about tribal gatherings organised by the Houthis.

title: Teenager accused of planning assassination of Texas congressman in name of ISIS
description: Target was Representative Keith Self, who has called for confronting the spread of radical Islam
content: A 17-year-old boy from McKinney, Texas, has been arrested on suspicion of planning to assassinate a Republican congressman and carry out an attack in the name of ISIS . Representative Keith Self , who is a staunch supporter of President Donald Trump and has called for confronting the spread of radical Islam in the US, was claimed to be the intended target of the assassination. Dallas media outlet WFAA reported, quoting law enforcement sources, that the suspect was arrested on October 5 after acquiring a firearm and that the boy had been recently radicalised. Mr Self thanked the FBI and law enforcement. "Preserving our constitutional republic from radical Islam means accepting the costs that come with it – name-calling, threats and worse," he said in a post on X on Wednesday. "This only strengthens my resolve. I will not back down." The suspect's name has not been released. It is unclear how he came to the attention of law enforcement and for how long he had been monitored. The FBI declined to comment. Mr Self has been at the forefront of a Republican effort to oppose the perceived incursion of radical Islam in the US. He, along with fellow Texas representative Chip Roy, launched the Sharia-Free America Caucus this year. “If we do not fight back, Sharia will dominate our culture and America will no longer be America,” Mr Self said at the time. Critics say the intensified scrutiny of the Muslim community by him and others is Islamophobic and part of a tactic to stir up the Republican base before major elections. There has been a rise in political violence in the US since Mr Trump returned to office last year. He has been a target of at least two earlier assassination attempts. The Democratic Speaker of the Minnesota House of Representatives, Melissa Hortman, and her husband Mark were killed last year.

title: President Sheikh Mohamed congratulates jiu-jitsu team after Asian Games medal haul in Japan
description: Sheikh Mohamed meets UAE medallists, coaches and support staff
content: President Sheikh Mohamed has received members of the UAE jiu-jitsu team after their medal-winning performances at the 20th Asian Games in Japan. Sheikh Mohamed met the athletes, along with their coaches and administrative staff, at a reception in Abu Dhabi on Thursday to mark the team's achievements at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Games, state news agency Wam reported. He congratulated the team on their performance, calling the results a reflection of the collective efforts of players, coaches and support staff. Sheikh Mohamed commended the determination shown by the UAE's athletes in representing the country on the international stage.

title: European Parliament asks EU to list Houthis as terror group
description: Backers show 'full solidarity' with the people of Yemen and Gulf countries that have come under attack
content: Members of the European Parliament on Thursday called on the European Union to list Yemen's Houthis as a terror group, citing destruction caused in Gulf states. Lead negotiator Hana Jalloul , from the group of socialists and democrats, said she extended her “full solidarity with the people of Yemen and Gulf countries”. “We did it!” Ms Jalloul wrote on X, after the motion for a resolution on the implication of Houthi attacks for regional security was adopted in parliament after weeks of negotiations. EU sanctions include an asset freeze and a travel ban. They must be approved by the European Council, the Brussels body in which representatives of the EU's 27 governments sit. The parliament called on the council to “put the Houthi movement, including its military and political wings, leadership and military and security apparatus, on the EU list of terrorist organisations”, it said in a statement. MEPs said they “strongly condemn the unprecedented missile and drone attacks by the Houthis against Saudi Arabia , and their military offensive in Yemen”. “MEPs describe these attacks as flagrant violations of international law and international humanitarian law, stressing that large numbers of Yemeni civilians have been killed and displaced, while the humanitarian crisis in the country has worsened,” the parliament statement said. The parliament also condemned Iran's support to the Houthis and called on the disarmament of all Tehran-backed groups in the Middle East, such as Hezbollah in Lebanon. Speaking at a debate on Tuesday, Ms Jalloul said Europe “cannot stand idly by”. While recognising that EU nations were already invested in defending Gulf states, including with the defensive maritime operation Aspides , Ms Jalloul called on “broader sanctions and for the Houthis to be included in the EU terrorist list”. She said measures should address the Houthi blockade of the Bab Al Mandeb strait, the gateway to Red Sea shipping, which alongside the Strait of Hormuz closure has disrupted the global food supply. Ms Jalloul also called for “political and financial support for the victims” of the Houthis’ actions. MEP Antonio Lopez-Isturiz White, from the conservative European People's Party, said Europe's “credibility is on the line”. He added: “The EPP demands clearly and without ambiguity that the Houthis belong and have to be on the European list of terror now.” Speaking alongside the MEPs, Kaja Kallas , the EU's foreign affairs and security policy chief, spoke of the need to get the EU's 27 states on board to designate the Houthis a terrorist organisation. “I agree with those who said that the Houthis are not operating alone. They are being financed, equipped and trained by Iran, and the playbook is exactly the same,” she said. Ms Kallas said she regretted that Houthi attacks had forced the postponement of a summit of EU and Gulf Co-operation Council leaders that had been scheduled to take place in Riyadh this month. “The Gulf is where Europe’s best hopes are for diversifying trade supplies,” Ms Kallas said. “Around a fifth of the EU’s trade already passes through the Red Sea. The security of the region is in our core interest.” The European Parliament's position on the Houthis comes a few weeks after it also called on the European Commission, the bloc's legislative arm, to take tougher measures against the Muslim Brotherhood . The 10-page resolution called on the commission to provide a “comprehensive overview” of all EU funds delivered to entities suspected of links with the Muslim Brotherhood. In a statement sent to The National , a commission representative confirmed receiving the resolution, to which they said they would respond in due course. “When it comes to the use of funds, the commission remains committed to not allowing any public money to be used for the promotion of extremism and terrorism,” they said. “This reflects a shared priority of the EU.” They highlighted an already existing “robust legal framework” to protect the EU's financial interests against people or organisations involved in terrorist activities or in violation of the bloc's values. In a counterterrorism agenda adopted this year, the European Commission reinforced measures designed to prevent the misuse of EU funds. They include a new financial data retrieval system for the purpose of tracking terrorist financing.

title: Health plan aims to counter effects of climate change
description: Ministry of Health and Prevention releases blueprint for future planning of services
content: Health care should evolve to accommodate a changing climate and an increased risk of associated diseases, officials said as they laid out a blueprint for future services. The Ministry of Health and Prevention has identified six areas of climate-related concern as priorities in future planning for health services. They include heat-related illnesses, heart and respiratory diseases and vector-borne diseases such as dengue fever and malaria. Planning will also expand to include waterborne and foodborne diseases, such as cholera, typhoid and norovirus, as well as mental health concerns related to climate. Scientists recorded 2024 as the hottest year on record, with global temperatures temporarily pushing past 1.5ºC above pre-industrial levels and more humid, hotter days increasing the risk of heat exhaustion and strain on the heart and lungs. Plans developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment and health authorities aim to strengthen integration between health and environmental policies. “As our climate changes, the risks to our health change with it,” said Ahmed Al Sayegh, Minister of Health and Prevention. “Heat, dust and extreme weather affect people’s health in very real ways. Our responsibility is to anticipate these risks and protect our communities before people fall ill.” The plan brings together data, expertise and institutions to build early warning systems and prepare health services for the effects of climate-related events. Planning is heavily focused on preventing climate-related diseases before they occur. Early heat and air-quality warnings will encourage people to take protective action before exposure leads to illness. Meanwhile, healthcare centres will be provided with resilient sources of medical goods and co-ordinated emergency plans, so essential care can continue during disruptions. The Earth is warming at a rate of about 0.35°C to 0.4°C a decade. That is almost double the average rate of around 0.2°C a decade recorded between 1970 and 2015. Poor air quality is a considerable risk factor for asthma and other respiratory conditions. Under the proposals, healthcare professionals will also be trained in preparation for more climate-related illnesses. “This plan includes developing the skills of healthcare professionals, expanding specialised research, improving emergency preparedness and increasing the resilience of healthcare facilities,” said Dr Hussain Al Rand, assistant undersecretary for public health at the Ministry of Health and Prevention. According to the Institute for Global Health, an estimated 62,775 heat-related deaths occurred across 32 European countries in 2024. In North America, there were more than 1,161 deaths related to record temperatures. As the world warms, more vector-borne diseases transmitted by mosquitoes and other insects could place health systems under pressure, as hospitals respond to increased illness and hospital admissions. In 2025, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control recorded 4,000 deaths related to dengue and more than five million cases across more than 90 countries. Meanwhile, the World Health Organisation said deaths related to malaria increased from about 598,000 in 2023 to 610,000 in 2024. Dr Gopal Chawla, a consultant pulmonologist at NMC Royal Hospital DIP, Dubai, said the government plan showed climate change was an increasingly important public health challenge. “I regularly see patients with asthma, COPD and other respiratory conditions whose symptoms worsen during dust storms, poor air quality and extreme weather,” he said. “Beyond respiratory illnesses, changing temperatures and rainfall patterns can influence mosquito populations and the spread of vector-borne diseases. Predictive surveillance could help identify emerging hotspots, enabling earlier public health interventions.” Dr Chawla said that by integrating environmental data, weather patterns, disease surveillance and individual clinical records, AI-driven models could help to identify vulnerable populations to anticipate health risks. For hospitals, that could mean better forecasts of patient admissions, resource allocation and emergency preparedness. Dr Muhammed Aslam, a pulmonologist at the International Modern Hospital in Dubai, said healthcare professionals should give priority to prevention, early detection and public awareness alongside treatment. “In respiratory care, that includes optimising asthma and COPD management, promoting vaccinations, educating patients about air-quality alerts and protecting vulnerable groups,” he said. “Strengthening disease surveillance, emergency preparedness and healthcare infrastructure will help reduce preventable illnesses and ensure continuity of care during climate-related emergencies.”

title: UAE announces plan to invest €15 billion into Greece
description: Announcement made on sidelines of Sheikh Khaled's official visit to Greece
content: The UAE is to invest a further €15 billion ($16.8 billion) into Greece as part of a joint initiative between the nations The plan was unveiled on the sidelines of an official visit to the European country by Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed , Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, on Thursday. It builds on the joint investment initiative, which was launched in May 2022 with a value of €4 billion, Abu Dhabi Media Office reported. The scheme has provided an important framework for developing and implementing strategic investments across sectors of mutual interest, the media office said. The move has resulted in “the completion of significant transactions in strategic sectors such as energy and health care”. The investment reflects the mutual trust between the UAE and Greece, and an opportunity to explore new opportunities in vital and future-focused sectors, supporting sustainable economic growth and enhancing the competitiveness of both economies, the media office said. The announcement “reflected the UAE's confidence in Greece's economic and investment strengths its strategic location and its role in connecting European markets with regional and international markets, alongside the promising opportunities it offers to develop major projects and long-term partnerships”. Sheikh Khaled met Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis on Thursday. Discussions at the Prime Minister's Office focused on efforts to bolster collaboration across a range of key sectors, including energy, infrastructure, health care, advanced technology and health care. During the meeting, Sheikh Khaled and Mr Mitsotakis also reflected on regional and international developments, stressing the importance of reinforcing security, peace and stability. Sheikh Khaled was greeted on arrival at Athens International Airport by George Gerapetritis, the Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs, state news agency Wam reported early on Thursday.

title: Sharjah tests AI-powered fire-detection system using thermal cameras and drones
description: New technology can verify reported incident before emergency team is sent
content: Sharjah is testing an AI-powered system that uses thermal cameras and drones to verify whether a fire has triggered an alarm before emergency crews are sent to the scene. The aim of the Aman system, developed by facility management company Saned in collaboration with Sharjah Civil Defence Authority, is to reduce unnecessary call-outs and speed up responses to industrial fires. The technology is being tested in open areas and warehouses, with plans to extend its use once trials are complete. During a demonstration attended by The National at Al Sajaa Industrial Area, teams set fire to a container and a damaged car before a drone flew over to verify the incident and relay information to the command centre. Hamid Al Zarouni, director of Saned, told The National that the system has been developed to report fires in commercial and industrial areas, aiming to detect incidents more quickly, speed up response times and improve warehouse safety. “Previously the system only reported incidents but now it can also verify whether there is a fire, using AI-powered technology, cameras and drones,” he said. Thermal cameras can detect flames, smoke and unusual increases in temperature, while drones can be sent to areas without camera coverage to investigate potential incidents and relay information. The drone's battery lasts up to one hour, covers distances of up to 20km and transmits data using 5G connectivity, enabling operators to assess incidents remotely. Mr Al Zarouni said Aman has been operating since 2018 and that Saned developed the technology, which the relevant authority owns. A presentation during Thursday’s demonstration outlined the system’s capabilities and results. The presentation said about 13,700 buildings are connected to the technology and monitored around the clock, and that 500 fire incidents have been detected and reported to the authority after verification. Brig Khalid Al Sharji of the Sharjah Civil Defence Authority said the latest tests aimed to use advanced technology to improve responses to fire reports, particularly in industrial areas. “Sometimes the alarm is not clear and we send firefighters with fire engines, but there is no fire. It wastes time and effort,” he said. Using drones to capture images and transmit them to the command centre would allow officials to verify reports before sending emergency teams, he added. The technology is useful in warehouses and industrial sites where large quantities of stored goods, including flammable materials, can increase the risk of fire. Brig Al Sharji said Aman already provided monitoring and coverage in residential areas. The trials will help assess how effectively the technology can detect and verify fires in complex industrial environments, where early identification can be critical to limiting damage and protecting workers.

title: UAE ranks third globally for quality of life satisfaction among the affluent
description: Nearly 90% are confident about their financial future, HSBC study shows
content: The UAE has been ranked among the top three nations in which investors are satisfied with the quality of life, prompting them to be confident about their financial future , a study from HSBC has found. About 83 per cent of more than 700 high-net-worth individuals surveyed in the Emirates said they were satisfied, placing the country below only Mexico and India, the London-based bank said in the report released at the UAE Wealth Investment Summit in Dubai on Thursday. The study, conducted by French research firm Ipsos, covered nearly 10,000 HNWIs across 10 markets. The UAE's satisfaction is markedly higher than the overall average of 75 per cent, as more than a quarter gave quality of life a perfect score, which was the joint-highest share of any market and well above the global average of 15 per cent, the report said. Nearly 90 per cent of those are also more confident about their financial future, it said. Those in the UAE are also more active when it comes to business plans, with more than a fifth claiming they are launching, acquiring or investing in a new venture, compared with the general average of 17 per cent, HSBC said. “The UAE has built an environment where people and their wealth can thrive, and this research shows it,” said Sami Abouzahr, HSBC’s head of international wealth and premier banking for the Middle East and UAE. “Investors here are confident, ambitious and internationally connected, and they are planning for the long term.” The HSBC study also suggested half of UAE investors expect to receive a significant financial inheritance, compared to 43 per cent globally, while about 58 per cent expect to leave a significant financial legacy to their heirs or other causes. Among those who expect to inherit and were able to estimate its value, the average expected inheritance is around Dh2 million ($545,000), about twice the global figure, with recipients typically expecting to receive it around the age of 52, HSBC said. “A significant transfer of wealth between generations is under way in the UAE and families want to get it right,” said Craig Worobec, HSBC’s head of wealth and premier solutions for the Middle East and UAE. “That means planning early, having open conversations about what wealth is for, and preparing the next generation with the skills and networks to use it well.” Despite the geopolitical uncertainty and economic headwinds, wealth generation and the flow of new money to the UAE continues. The country is a magnet for the ultra-wealthy , as well as global wealth managers and trillion-dollar asset managers. Abu Dhabi and Dubai have been ranked among the top 10 destinations for next-generation wealth, despite the fallout from geopolitical tension and hostility, London-based consultancy Savills said in a report last week . Also last week, a study from Boston Consulting Group showed that net wealth in the UAE is set to jump to $6 trillion by the end of this decade, despite the short-term volatility caused by conflict in the Middle East . “With a highly international population and wealth that spans several countries, the UAE has become a base from which investors manage and grow their wealth around the world,” HSBC said.

title: Syria sends troops to Sweida front line as Israel moves hardware into area
description: Tensions rising over southern province that is home to Druze minority
content: Syria has deployed troops to reinforce the southern province of Sweida amid Israeli military activity that could be aimed at setting up a base in the area, security sources said. The troops have been sent to a front line in Sweida near where members of the Druze minority have mobilised militias with Israeli backing. Sweida, the Druze heartland, is one of several issues standing in the way of a US drive for peace between Syria and Israel . Tensions rose after an inconclusive US-backed meeting in Jordan in August, with Israel expanding its military presence on Syrian territory in provinces to the east of Sweida. Increased Israeli involvement in the province could boost the Sweida National Guard, an amalgamation of Druze militias supported by Israel and allied to Hikmat Al Hijri, the main Druze spiritual leader in Syria. Mr Al Hijri has condemned Syria's post- Bashar Al Assad government as extremist and called for a new constitution. Over the past two weeks, around 1,000 Syrian soldiers, mostly from rural Damascus, have arrived in batches on pick-up trucks in western Sweida, the sources said, raising the total number of government troops to 3,000. A Syrian security official confirmed that reinforcements have been sent. Israel has been airlifting equipment into the interior of the province, in what could be preparation to build a base, the sources said. Government forces, mainly the Syrian Army Fourth Corps, have been surrounding the city of Sweida since last year. One of the sources said the Sweida National Guard militias had cordoned off 10 hills around the provincial capital. Israeli helicopters have been dropping off surveillance, radar and other hardware into some of these locations. “Securing the hills would protect any base that they could be planning. It would also increase Israel’s warning capabilities against Iranian attacks,” said the source, who is in contact with National Guard members. Last year Israel built positions inside Quneitra and Deraa governorates as a precursor to lengthening a military line parallel to the occupied Golan Heights. “Israel has been raising the capabilities of the National Guard, so the Syrian army has to factor in the possibility of a Druze offensive,” the source said. Syrian reinforcements have been quiet to avoid attracting the fury of Israel, which last year conducted major air attacks against government forces to halt attacks against Syria’s Druze. In July 2025, Israeli air strikes stopped a government offensive to subdue Sweida, which is majority Druze. The Druze forces remained in control of Sweida city, the provincial capital. However, government forces captured more than 30 Druze villages west and north of Sweida city. Around 1,700 people, mostly Druze, were killed. Damascus “cannot appear to be standing still” while Israel expands its military presence in the country, the source said. For the past 22 months, Syria's central government has been run by members of Hayat Tahrir Al Sham, a former Al Qaeda affiliate, after they toppled Bashar Al Assad in December 2024. However, neither the Sweida Druze nor the authorities want hostilities to resume, the source said. The army does not want to invite an Israeli response, while Mr Al Hijri realises that hostilities would make the Druze outside Sweida, particularly in Damascus, more vulnerable to sectarian attacks, according to the source. In March 2025, the Israeli air force struck targets near Damascus to stop attacks by pro government gunmen on Druze neighbourhoods near the capital, which left dozens killed. US envoy Tom Barrack discussed Sweida with President Ahmad Al Shara during a brief visit to Damascus on Wednesday, according to a western diplomat who requested anonymity. In September last year, Mr Barrack brokered an unrealised deal between Syria, Washington and Jordan to solve the Sweida issue. Syria‘s role is “pivotal” for a lasting peace, Mr Barrack said, without elaborating. The Druze are one of three minorities in Syria whose ties with the new government have been marred by violence. In March last year, the authorities sent regular forces and militias to control Alawite coastal areas, which underpinned the old system. In the east, a government campaign in January brought the Syrian Democratic Forces, a mostly Kurdish armed group, under government control after the US abandoned its support for the group. There are several hundred thousand Druze in Syria, out of one million worldwide. The sect is also present in Jordan, Israel, Lebanon, as well as a diaspora community mainly in Latin America. However, its heartland comprise the Chouf Mountains in Lebanon and Sweida. A source in neighbouring Deraa said that Israeli commanders and personnel had been travelling back and forth by helicopter between Israel and Sweida. “They also have taken men from Sweida for drone training in Israel,” the source said. Israeli helicopters can be seen flying over the Yarmouk River basin and villages in Deraa on the way to Sweida. Supplies communication devices, night-vision systems and sniper rifles have reached the Sweida National Guard, the source said.

title: The movies, the media and the messy truth
description: As Hollywood captures the changing face of the media, the industry finds itself at a crossroads
content: It’s been a decade since Spotlight won Oscars for best picture and best screenplay at the 2016 Academy Awards, with the film recognised for its heroic portrayal of journalism. This newspaper described it as the “best film about journalism since All the President’s Men ”, which was quite the compliment, for its dramatisation of the Boston Globe ’s journalists working to expose historic child abuse cases within the Catholic church. Ten years later, Spotlight remains one of the great industry movies, and presents a powerful case for investing time, patience and teamwork into the stories that matter. The Social Reckoning , released earlier this month, attempts to cover some of the same ground, unravelling a time-hopping dialogue between an investigative journalist at The Wall Street Journal and a marginalised Facebook team member-turned reluctant whistleblower, as the two work together to explain the algorithmic harm that social media is known to be capable of. Like Spotlight , The Social Reckoning is an advert for slow-burn reporting work, although journalism is very much the side order to the main-course dissection of the mores of digital platforms where billions of people spend good chunks of their daily lives. The contrast between those two worlds and the articulation of processes at work in their respective silos are everything you’d expect from a film by Aaron Sorkin, although it appears global audiences have not been especially convinced. The movie has to date underperformed its predecessor, The Social Network , as well as its reported pre-release revenue estimates. The Abu Dhabi cinema I saw the film in had few patrons in attendance on a recent weekend afternoon screening. One wonders if audiences genuinely want to sit and be instructed on the ills of social media in a darkened cinema when most will already instinctively recognise on some level that these digital platforms have a level of user-induced toxicity about them. Even armed with that knowledge, we remain broadly happy to scroll passively through our feeds morning, noon and night. And those who paid to watch the movie might have been absentmindedly flipping through their feeds right up until the point the opening credits rolled, an unintentionally amusing state of affairs given the film’s central argument. Media industry practitioners may still nod sagely at the love-letterish portrayal of investigative reporting, however. Time magazine called it a “brisk, old-school journalism thriller”, which in itself is an energetic hat-tip to a film that celebrates what is described in one scene as “the last two minutes of print journalism”. The Wall Street Journal ’s review, the title at the core of some of the film, describes it as a sequel that “no one saw coming and no one asked for”, in part, it says, because our societal concerns have shifted towards artificial intelligence in recent years. By comparison, social media might occupy the same place as the legal vices of society, such as excessive use of tobacco or alcohol or overconsumption of processed foods. Most would recognise the ability of these substances to do harm to the individual, but seem to have made an uneasy peace with their own habits. Given the above, The Social Reckoning seems unlikely to claim a spot on those “best films about journalism” lists that regularly circulate, which usually push the aforementioned Spotlight and All the President’s Men to the upper reaches of their rankings. Who knows if the film will be remembered affectionately a decade from now or even if it will be talked about at all? Anyone seeking a less glorious portrayal of the industry could do worse than seek out Devil Wears Prada 2 , a box-office high-performer earlier in the year that can now be found on streaming platforms. It offers a surprisingly accurate portrayal of journalism in its post-imperial years, although most people will have been attracted to it for its all-star cast and affection for the 2006 original. The 2026 comedy drama begins with layoffs at Anne Hathaway’s fictional newspaper and quickly progresses to the story at the centre of the film’s light plot being broken all over Instagram and the mea culpa that follows it through push notifications and alerts. The death of print is very much to the fore, too. The fictional fashion title at the centre of the film “stopped being a magazine years ago … we are digital, downloadable, we are in the ether … [we are] content that people scroll past while they eat”, which is quite the stinging epithet. In this world, digital stories are judged on optics and cut-through to a niche audience by one part of the organisation and on clicks and hard numbers by others. “Did anyone read the piece?” asks Meryl Streep’s Miranda early in the film at an editorial meeting. It is a question that sits at the heart of audience-behaviour discussions in every newsroom, because on many occasions, what is perceived as good work does not line up with genuine high performance. It is always a wonderful day in a newsroom when they do. As such, DWP2 probably captures the moment better than Sorkin’s admirable film. Process, production and dissemination of information at speed, as well as the definitive shift of print to being one form of story presentation rather than the only form, are to the fore. Outsiders may still wonder which is the more accurate portrayal? Insiders, meanwhile, may be locked in to interrogating what their audience wants, in what format and where.

title: Harry Brook smashes fastest ODI double century but England still lose to Sri Lanka in run fest
description: Captain reaches landmark in just 114 deliveries in Rawalpindi but still sees team beaten in format's second-highest chase
content: Harry Brook broke a number of records as he smashed a double century in a high-scoring tri-series match against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi. Brook hit 202 off just 116 balls to help England post a mammoth 429-4. It was the first time an England batter had hit an ODI double century. Not just that, Brook's maiden ODI double century was also the fastest 200 in the format's history – from 114 balls – breaking record of India captain Shubman Gill who had scored one off 127 balls last month against the West Indies. On Thursday, Brook cracked 21 fours and 10 sixes to reach the milestone in the final over of the innings. The England captain also became only the second batter in history, after Caribbean great Chris Gayle, to hit a Test triple century, ODI double ton and T20 hundred. Brook also eclipsed England's highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes. Brook's scintillating knock ended with the final ball of England's innings when he ​was caught by ‌Sahan Arachchige off ⁠the bowling of ​Janith Liyanage. Joe Root provided good support with 69 from 66 balls, ​finishing as England's second-highest scorer of the day. Will Jacks finished unbeaten on 66 off just 30 deliveries. It was the highest score ever conceded by Sri Lanka and the biggest total scored in Pakistan. Brook is already among top five Test and T20 batters and should now find himself in the top 10 in ODIs as well. The right handed batter has emerged as one of the best batters in the world, and among the few all-format players. Incredibly, Sri Lanka would chase down the total in thrilling fashion with Janith Liyanage hitting a six with the second last ball to snatch a two-wicket win in what became an unforgettable 859-run shootout. It was the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, after South Africa's famous one-wicket win over Australia in Johannesburg in 2006 when the Proteas scored 438-9, also achieved with one ball to spare. Pavan Rathnayake top scored with 130 runs off 106 balls - snatching the player of the match award out of Brooks' hands - while Avishka Fernando (97 off 83) and Dasun Shanaka (97 off 50) battering the England attack all around the ground. It would be Liyanage's unbeaten 61 off 27 that would guide Sri Lanka over the line, although Josh Tongue's final over two wickets in two balls almost swung the game back in England's favour. It was a chastening finish for Brook's side in which Sam Curran became the first England bowler to concede a century of runs in ODIs, having seen his nine overs go for 2-103. "It was an incredible game of cricket, both teams were exceptional," said Brook. "Sri Lanka just outplayed us. They played exceptional cricket to knock off 400. "It was a nice innings but being on the losing side it has no value whatsoever in my eyes. We got to get back to the drawing board a little bit, and we have an opportunity in the next couple of games to nail down a place in the final." Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis said: "We chased very well today, I enjoyed it as captain ... everybody showed their character. "Everyone believed we can do it. Everyday we talk about showing the character in team meetings, and it's about showing we can get any score." Defeat leaves winless England bottom of the tr-series table after two games with Pakistan top after victories in both of their matches so far.

title: UFC 333 predictions: Volkanovski and Dvalishvili to leave Abu Dhabi as champions
description: Etihad Arena to host two world title fights on Saturday
content: Abu Dhabi will host two title fights as the UFC returns to the UAE this weekend. Alexander Volkanovski puts his featherweight championship on the line while Petr Yan makes his first title defence as bantamweight champion. There are nine fights on the card at Etihad Arena. Below are our predictions for UFC 333. Alexander Volkanovski v Movsar Evloev Alexander “The Great” looks back to his brilliant best following two polished wins over Diego Lopes. He will need to be on top form against the unbeaten Russian. Evloev boasts a perfect 20-0 record in pro MMA. Volkanovski (28-4) has the edge in experience. Saturday will be his 12th successive title fight and the sixth time he has defended the UFC featherweight title. He is in the conversation as the greatest 145-pounder of all time and is looking to add to his legend against Evloev. If Volkanovski has the advantage in striking, Evloev has it in grappling. The Russian is a master wrestler; the way he dominated Aljamain Sterling is a testament to that. He tried to venture away a little in his win over Lerone Murphy, before reverting to type to secure the victory. Volkanovski warned Evloev to “not try to be exciting” and to “bring your best game”, saying he didn't want to hear any excuses if things don't go the Russian's way on the mat. “People want to see how I handle that wrestling anyway. I think that's a part of the story,” he told The National . Prediction: Volkanovski to win on the judges' scorecards. Petr Yan v Merab Dvalishvili Yan fought the perfect fight to end Dvalishvili's three-fight run as bantamweight king. Ripping body shots took the wind out of the Georgian's sails when they met last December. Yan's takedown defence was textbook too. It was Dvalishvili's fourth fight of 2025 and, by his own admission, accepting the Yan fight was a mistake, coming only two months after his victory over Corey Sandhagen. “I'm not blaming that because of my loss, but I know why I lost,” Dvalishvili told The National . His loss to Yan ended a 14-fight win streak and necessitated a long-overdue break for Dvalishvili. Neither has fought since their last meeting. UFC 333 will be the third time they have met, with Dvalishvili taking the first fight on the judges' scorecards. Many admire Yan's skill set, not least because he is an underrated ground technician too. But with Dvalishvili well rested, “The Machine” should be too much for his Russian opponent this time around. Prediction: Dvalishvili to reclaim the title. Lone'er Kavanagh v Ramazan Temirov Flyweight prospect Lone’er Kavanagh will look to protect his top-six ranking and potentially move into the title conversation when he faces Ramazan Temirov. A win over former champion Brandon Moreno put the rest of the division on notice, but a late submission at the hands of Brandon Royval has some questioning whether the likeable Londoner has the all-round game to challenge for championship gold. In Temirov, he faces a fearsome puncher, one who separated Steve Erceg from his consciousness the last time he was in Abu Dhabi in July . It was his 13th first-round knockout. Prediction: Temirov by KO. Alexander Volkov v Rizvan Kuniev Alexander Volkov's victory over Jailton Almeida in Abu Dhabi 12 months ago put him next in line for a shot at the heavyweight title. By the end of UFC 321, those hopes lay in tatters. Ciryl Gane’s wayward fingers changed the heavyweight landscape. Tom Aspinall is still recovering from his injuries. Gane, meanwhile, has been promoted to undisputed king of the division. Volkov, a fighter more methodical than mesmerising, needs to put on a show against Rizvan Kuniev if he is to convince his UFC bosses he deserves a crack at Gane. Prediction: Volkov by decision. Aaron Pico v Losene Keita Losene Keita was drafted in at short notice following an injury to Arnold Allen. The Belgian featherweight became a viral sensation following his spectacular walk-off KO over Muhammad Naimov at UFC Paris in September. The celebration will take some topping, too. After being stopped by Lerone Murphy, Pico returned with a flawless performance over Patricio Pitbull, taking a unanimous decision over the feared Brazilian. Prediction: Keita to deliver another highlight reel KO.

title: Dubai Design Week announces five new commissions for Abwab 2026
description: Arabic lettering, handmade paper and Kashmiri weaving traditions inform  exhibition opening on November 3
content: A seven-metre installation featuring red light and a structure inspired by the coded instructions used by Kashmiri weavers are among five new commissions announced for Dubai Design Week’s Abwab programme. Abwab , which means doors in Arabic, commissions new work by practitioners from across Asia and Africa. Dalia Rafeh, Grace Shieh, Kanaka Raghavan, Ubik and architecture and research practice Varussi have been selected to create this year’s commissions, under the theme In Other Words. The exhibition will run from November 3 to 8 at Dubai Design District. It forms part of the festival’s 12th iteration , with Abwab bringing the commissions together in an indoor group exhibition for the first time, moving away from the individual pavilions of previous years. Established in 2015, Abwab has supported more than 180 designers. This year’s works explore communication through lettering, textiles, paper and architecture, considering how meaning is conveyed through the materials and forms people encounter. Rafeh’s Shhhhhhhh takes the Arabic letter sheen – ش – and its association with the call for quiet as its starting point. The letter is repeated in a seven-metre installation using red light, which draws on the visual language of public and commercial signage. The work explores how the same call for quiet can suggest an order to remain silent, a pause for reflection or an invitation to listen. Dubai-based architecture and research practice Varussi, founded by Owais Asif Khan and Samreen Junaid Wani, draws on Kashmiri weaving traditions in Taleem . The installation takes its name from the traditional coding system used to design Kashmiri carpets and kani shawls. Varussi will translate that system into an architectural structure visitors can enter, exploring how craft knowledge is recorded and passed between generations. Dubai-based designer, educator and researcher Kanaka Raghavan turns to the construction of written language in Cheent Devanagari . Her work challenges the treatment of Latin typography as a universal starting point for design, drawing instead on Devanagari’s own structural and material traditions. Using block printing, ornament and layers of translucent textiles, Raghavan creates letterforms that separate and come back together as visitors move around them. Their changing appearance allows viewers to examine how the script is constructed. Writer and visual artist Grace Shieh explores the material qualities of paper in A Library of Paper Memories . Combining papermaking, poetry and experimental writing, the installation considers how fibres, textures and forms can carry memories and meaning alongside written words. India-based conceptual artist Vivek Premachandran, who works under the name Ubik, examines the interpretation of language in Non/Sense , a floor-based installation inspired by science-fiction writer Philip K Dick’s How to Build a Universe That Doesn’t Fall Apart Two Days Later . The installation uses translation, mistranslation, abbreviation and lorem ipsum – the placeholder text used in graphic design – to turn text fragments into patterns and spatial structures. The exhibition’s layout will allow visitors to move around, between and through the commissions, as well as view them from above. Entry is free. Three free curator-led walkthroughs with Alexie Glass-Kantor, Caoimhe CJ Reynolds and the participating practitioners will explore the research, materials and processes behind the works.

title: IMI Media Academy and Abdulla Al Ghurair Foundation to prepare 29,000 young people for careers
description: Five-year partnership to create professional pathways for young Arabs
content: IMI Media Academy and the Abdulla Al Ghurair Foundation have announced a five-year partnership to develop Arab media talent, aiming to reach 29,000 young people and train them for careers in the field. Under Al Ghurair Voice Lab, the partnership will connect education and skills development with practical experience and professional opportunities. It will also help create pathways into the media sector by offering access to internships, placements, employment opportunities and other forms of professional development. Seven connected programmes will cover the foundational media skills, advanced professional upskilling, university curriculum integration, storytelling for school pupils, national youth initiatives and regional programming across the Arab region. These will provide young people with technical and professional skills, practical learning, mentorship and direct exposure to media professionals and workplaces. The agreement was signed by Ali Al Hammadi, chief operating officer at IMI, and Dr Sonia Ben Jaafar, chief executive of AGF, in the presence of Dr Sultan Ahmed Al Jaber, Minister of Industry and Advanced Technology and chairman of IMI, and Abdul Aziz Al Ghurair, chairman of AGF’s board. The partnership comes as rapid changes in technology, audience behaviour and media production reshape the skills required across the industry. It brings together IMI Media Academy’s industry expertise, professional training capabilities and access to a media ecosystem with AGF’s regional experience in education and youth empowerment and its learning-to-earning approach, connecting skills development with pathways to meaningful professional opportunities. The partnership builds on the organisations’ existing collaboration through the Nomu Al Ghurair Siraj programme, which has equipped 450 graduates with future-ready media skills and provided opportunities to engage directly with the media industry. The five-year plan expands that work in scale and ambition, with a greater focus on connecting learning to tangible professional opportunities. “Media has an important role in how our region sees itself and how others see us. That makes investing in the people who will shape its future especially important,” Dr Ben Jaafar said. “Young people will have the chance to learn within a real media environment, develop their skills alongside professionals and see a clearer route into the industry. We want young people across the Arab region to have the skills, the access and the space to contribute their perspectives and tell the stories of their communities.” Khalid Al Hosani, director of operations at IMI Media Academy, said: “This partnership is about building a stronger pipeline of Arab media talent – not simply delivering training. By connecting education directly with practical experience, mentorship and professional opportunities, we will help thousands of young people move from learning about the media industry to actively contributing to it. Our ambition is to create a model that delivers measurable outcomes in the UAE and can be expanded across the region.” Chantal Saliba, director of media and training at IMI Media Academy, said: “Media cannot be learnt from a classroom alone. Young people need the opportunity to work with experienced professionals, understand how newsrooms and creative teams operate, and develop their own voices through practice. This partnership will give them that exposure – helping them build not only the technical skills required by today’s industry, but also the judgment, confidence and curiosity needed to shape its future.” The partnership will launch in the UAE and is expected to expand across the region over the five-year period. AGF and IMI Media Academy aim to strengthen the pipeline of skilled Arab media professionals and create clearer pathways for young people to move from education and training into the industry.

title: London’s prime properties take a 10% hit but new super homes emerge
description: Activity in £5m+ housing market picked up compared with the summer, but remains sluggish
content: Sellers of properties in prime London postcodes were forced to accept discounts of 10.1 per cent in September, as overall sale prices fell by 7.1 per cent compared with a year earlier. The number of sales was the lowest in any September since 2016, according to property analysts LonRes, with 16.8 per cent fewer transactions than September 2025 and 13.9 per cent fewer than the 2017-20129 pre-pandemic average. There was slightly better news for properties worth more than £5 million , with transactions falling 12.5 per cent but new instructions increasing by 32.5 per cent. Buyers continued to pay well below asking price. Compared with pre-pandemic levels, prices were 8.2 per cent lower in September. For homes above £5 million, there was 0.8 per cent more discounting, but 88.8 per cent above the levels from 2015-24. The founder of London taxi company Addison Lee sold a mansion overlooking London’s Regent’s Park for little more than half the price he paid 13 years ago. John Griffin, who sold his business to the Carlyle Group for about £300 million ($464 million) in 2013, offloaded the property on the park’s western perimeter for £11.5 million at the beginning of October, down from his purchase price of £20.7 million. It had been discounted a number of times over recent years but failed to sell. LonRes said that, in the context of a weaker market, it was important to set a competitive initial asking price “as the longer a home is on the market, the bigger the discount needs to secure a sale”. Between July and September, the average discount for homes selling in under three months was 3.8 per cent, but increased to 11.1 per cent for homes taking six to 12 months to sell. There appears to be movement at the top end of the market, with 32.5 per cent more new £5 million-plus instructions compared with the same month last year, and 63.6 per cent higher than the 2017-2019 average. LonRes said super prime sales continue to be “impacted by news and speculation, resulting in a stop-start market”. Nick Gregori, head of research at LonRes, said: “September typically sees the market pick up after the summer lull, and this year this was partly true. Activity across prime London – from both buyers and sellers – improved relative to the summer but remained sluggish for the time of year. Achieved prices continued to slide downwards, reflecting buyer hesitancy.” He said borrowing costs and a perceived lack of future growth were the two factors driving lower demand, combined with global uncertainty and fears of inflation. He believes there are unlikely to be any giveaways for prime property buyers in Chancellor John Healey’s budget on October 28, “so the best that can be hoped for is no further damaging changes”.
