The retreat will close after breakfast at Tocha accompanied by a series of giveaways. All proceeds will be donated to Al Jalila Foundation to support awareness campaigns. For those who can't make the event, the collaboration extends across the month with a "pink" spa package – any 90-minute treatment with 10 per cent of the proceeds donated. October 24; from 8.30am; Dh270; Bluewaters Island The Los Angeles-founded athleisure brand has built a UAE following over the years, which it cemented with the opening of its first shop in the Dubai Mall in early 2024, followed by one at The Galleria Al Maryah Island in Abu Dhabi a few months later. This year marks an expansion of its physical presence in Dubai with a shop that opened in Dubai Hills Mall in August, followed by the largest flagship store in the UAE – spanning an impressive 950 square metres – in the Mall of the Emirates in September. Head there for your next matching gym set or cosy daywear. Sign up for the final few sessions of the Breasy Floating Immersive Breathwork series, which has been held monthly at Mandarin Oriental Downtown throughout the summer. The collaboration between wellness community Breasy and the hotel takes place under the new moon at Noia by the Pool, the rooftop pool and restaurant space. Guests take to the water on an airbed, adding a sense of weightlessness to the 60-minute sound and breath experience. The guided experience aims to aid rest and recovery for attendees. October 8 and November 5, 8pm-9pm; Dh325 plus VAT After a successful launch this year, Charge Circle is back from a summer break. Led by Silvina Joseph, a hypnotherapist and founder of Charge Hypnosis & Wellness, the 60-minute session takes participants through a guided visualisation complemented by immersive audio that further promotes a relaxed nervous system. Step inside the Arte Museum in Dubai Mall, and make your way to a corner of the museum where walls appear as soothing rolling waves; take a seat on one of the airbeds, put on your headphones and an eye mask, and kick back. Each session has a different theme, but follows the same immersive set-up. October 22; 7pm-8pm; Dh320 Leadership coach and speaker Noona Nafousi will head to the Theatre of Digital Arts at Souk Madinat Jumeirah for a live recording of Limitless , her 2026-launched podcast spotlighting founders and chief executives. In October, Nafousi will be joined by special guest, her sister Roxie Nafousi, to talk about self-confidence, identity, mindset and more. Roxie rose to prominence as the author of Manifest: 7 Steps to Living Your Best Life and for her work as a self-development coach. October 26; 6.30pm; from Dh280 The Pink Ladies Games return to Dubai for its fifth iteration, bringing women together for a morning of fitness challenges while raising awareness of cancer and healthy lifestyles. Held at the Sevens Stadium as part of day one of the Dubai Fitness Challenge, the event has teams of four to five women take on six 15-minute challenges that combine strength, speed, teamwork, creativity and problem-solving. The event is open to women of all ages and fitness levels, and participants can enter alongside friends, colleagues or members of sports and social clubs. October 31; 7am-10am; from Dh200 Real Pilates, which has branches in JLT, Jumeirah and Meydan, has teamed up with fellow Dubai brand Activeist to create a limited collection signalling their shared community values. The Rooted capsule features T-shirts, grip socks, caps, leggings and accessories, with prices from Dh65. Dania Istaitie, founder of Activeist, hailed the collaboration, saying she's “incredibly proud” of what has been created. Female-founded and Palestinian-owned, Activeist launched in 2023 with a mission to create community-focused and environmentally conscious clothes and accessories for comfortable movement. The Pink Caravan community event is returning to Aljada, Sharjah, in collaboration with Arada. The festival will combine health and community engagement, with free breast examinations and mammograms available through mobile clinics. The three-day programme will also feature community activities, educational workshops, gaming zones and children’s entertainment. October 2 to 4; 5pm-11pm; free

title: WETEX 2026: Powering the UAE's energy future from day one
description: The Water, Energy, Technology and Environment Exhibition gathers thousands of energy industry professionals under one roof at Dubai World Trade Centre
content: Thousands of energy industry professionals gathered at Dubai World Trade Centre on Tuesday for the opening day of WETEX 2026, with companies across the UAE's power, construction and technology sectors using the exhibition to set out their responses to surging electricity demand that existing infrastructure was not built to meet. The Water, Energy, Technology and Environment Exhibition, organised annually by Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA), drew cable manufacturers, EPC (engineering, procurement and construction) contractors, property developers and enterprise technology companies under one roof, across several halls of the sprawling convention centre. The conversations on the floor spanned the rising demand for more renewables and more data centres and an increasingly urgent need for the tools to manage it. Innovative solutions to meet these challenges, however, were not in short supply. "This event is extremely significant in terms of presenting our capabilities to the utilities here," said Ranjod Singh, whose company Aasa Power has been working across the UAE’s power infrastructure for 30 years. "It provides a great platform for all the EPC contractors, the clients, the consultants and DEWA itself to come together. There is a lot of technological exchange, a lot of development happening." The development happening outside the exhibition halls is relentless as the country continues to grow. Data centres are multiplying, residential masterplans are expanding into previously undeveloped areas, industrial zones are drawing new investment. And all of it needs power. "The power requirement will definitely outcast current capacity,” said Mr Singh. “We have to be ready." His answer – and one of Aasa Power's headline showcases at this year's WETEX – is a containerised, mobile solar unit designed to serve construction sites without the need for diesel generators. The system deploys foldable solar panels from a transportable container, expanding remotely to generate clean electricity for site offices and equipment. The unit can shift from site to site and be reused indefinitely, addressing not just carbon emissions but the noise and power-quality problems diesel generation brings. As the demand for power surges, as does the need for cables. Charles Mellagui, chief executive of the Cable Business Unit at DUCAB, laid out critical infrastructure requirements: "Some estimates say we need 80 million kilometres of transmission cable by 2040," he told The National . "Simply because of electrification and renewables, creating this need for cable." To deliver at that scale, raw materials are the biggest challenge, he added. Copper demand is expected to nearly double globally in the years ahead, while a new copper mine requires a decade to reach full production. "We are in 2026," Mellagui said, "so the output will come fully by 2036, meaning there is a constraint on the supply chain." DUCAB's response includes a push to increase its use of recycled copper – currently at 12 to 13 percent – to more than 25 percent by 2040, alongside the development of cables using polypropylene, a greener and fully recyclable alternative to conventional materials. This is why DUCAB, which counts DEWA, TAQA and Sharjah Electricity and Water Authority (SEWA) among its strategic partners, has been a fixture at WETEX for several years. "WETEX has grown year after year in terms of reputation and also in terms of international connection," Mr Mellagui said. "WETEX brings a lot of players in energy transition, in sustainability, in electrification together – they are bringing innovation, they are sharing solutions." In the built environment, DAMAC Properties is showcasing at WETEX the shift in design and construction across its developments. Mohammed Tahaineh, chief projects officer at DAMAC, pointed to the recently completed DAMAC Lagoon as a marker of that shift. "It is the first master plan to get a Platinum Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) certificate in the UAE," he said. "This required a lot of detail, studying a lot of design, using a lot of technologies that enhance the lifestyle of residents." DAMAC has invested close to $50 million in its own offsite manufacturing facilities, producing bathrooms, kitchens, precast components and tiling systems under factory conditions. Around 80 per cent of its villas are now assembled from factory-made components, with composite construction technologies reportedly cutting concrete consumption by up to 30 to 40 per cent in some applications, with corresponding reductions in water and energy use through the build process. "Today we are not considering sustainability or green building as a choice," Mr Tahaineh said. "It is a responsibility of us, as a leading development company in the region, to educate the people, to give them a sustainable lifestyle." Mr Tahaineh has high expectations for WETEX this year. “I am expecting a lot from this,” he said. “I feel that our presence here is to know what else we can give our customers.” At the same time, there is knowledge exchange. “We are visiting companies, and a lot of companies are visiting us, to know what is new in sustainability and how we can save power and save water for the future generation.” Unsurprisingly, artificial intelligence was another recurring theme across the exhibition floor. For SAP, which has been a technology partner to DEWA and related organisations for more than 15 years, WETEX 2026 is an opportunity to take that conversation forward with major energy clients. "The importance of this event for us is mainly two things," said Marwan Zeineddine, managing director of SAP UAE. "The networking with all our partners, and it's a big opportunity for us to showcase our latest innovations – especially around the autonomous enterprise and agentic AI." SAP's vision is of an enterprise that runs finance, procurement, human resources, logistics and operations end-to-end through AI agents, governed, secure and drawing on an organisation's own data for accuracy. The company is in active conversations with DEWA about implementing these capabilities. It has also developed what it calls a green ledger – a control tower that tracks carbon emissions across all operations – a tool already deployed with major UAE industrial clients. The fundamental challenge, Mr Zeineddine argued, is not ambition but pace. "The main challenge for all technology companies like SAP is speed – how quickly you can develop, especially in the AI era. You have to be very quick in developing and making sure your solutions work with the latest innovations. If you are late, someone else will be doing it.” This is how events like WETEX become a platform for these innovative – and necessary – solutions. And this year it’s more important than ever, added Mr Zeineddine, as organisations respond to regional turbulence alongside global technological shifts. “The investments should be very smart.” This page was produced by The National in partnership with WETEX and WGES.

title: Apple iPhone Duo hands-on: Your productivity will hinge on this
description: John Ternus and Co unfold new tricks with debut device in growing category
content: Apple , this had better be good; you made us wait more than seven years for this to unfold. At long last, the company has introduced the iPhone Duo , its first entry into the foldable device category, and first major hardware release under new boss John Ternus. And, on a personal note, I've never seen my peers this hyped for a device. The National gave the device a spin and ran through its features. Here are our initial thoughts. The passport-sized iPhone Duo, when folded, gives you a 13.7cm (5.4-inch) display. Open it up and that digital real estate stretches to 19.3cm (7.6 inches). And it's now Apple's thinnest smartphone, at only 5.2mm when open. The power and camera control buttons remain in their usual slots on the right while it's closed or open in landscape mode. But from here, things get shaken up quite a bit. The volume buttons are now on top, and switching to portrait mode while unfolded brings them to the left for more familiar control. Meanwhile, the USB-C charging port, while still at the bottom when folded, switches to the left side when unfolded, which is a little odd as we're used to that on the right. But there are two notable omissions: there is no Action Button, which is customisable and (probably) most commonly used as the silent toggle Face ID – repeat, no Face ID. Instead, a Touch ID, nestled on the power button, makes its return. Skipping the Action Button and Face ID will need some getting used to, particularly the latter, but Apple says key stuff like transactions and verifying your identity will still be seamless – you'll just need your fingers instead of your eyes. Also, battery percentage and carrier details won't be readily visible on the homescreens. Instead, you have to swipe down from the top-right, like the iPhone X. The latest, smaller version of Dynamic Island is also present, but now it now appears on the top right. As for the crease, it is virtually invisible. Apple hasn't released a figure for fold-unfold durability, though the Duo has ceramic shield protection for scratchproofing and is rated IP68 for dust and waterproofing. There are four cameras – the main 48MP Dual Fusion system, the 12MP Centre Stage camera on the cover and the under-display camera on the inner display. You can choose from two colours, night sky and star white, with the former our winner. (It would've been better if there was a defining option like lavender or our all-time favourite, cosmic orange.) By now we know that the Duo's prices in the UAE range from Dh8,499 to Dh13,599, and there are extended shipping times due to overwhelming demand. The iPhone Duo has a clean feel: opening and closing feels reliable, and the sturdy hinge ensures it will stay in place without any wobble or movement. Multitasking is a key feature that allows you to do more with fewer swipes and taps. For example, you can have your email on one side and photos on the other, and you can just drag an image as an attachment. Let the Duo sit L-shaped and you'll be able to do some easy stuff. If you're in the camera app or a streaming service like Netflix, controls will be on screen below for easier navigation. The camera also has a new feature that automatically takes pictures without having to control it; trigger the function, let the main cameras face you and it will track subjects and take pictures from time to time, which you will know when the torch briefly lights up. It also acts as a good teleprompter, which creators and on-camera people will find useful. Apple says apps have been and are being optimised to work with the Duo, and a sign that an app has been updated is when you see controls on the right side. It's also optimised for popular apps such as WhatsApp, Instagram and Slack, to make work, play and creation easier. While we don't have the full list, updates for popular apps are expected to be rolled out on Friday, when the device finally becomes available in stores. While we haven't fully tested it, Apple guarantees battery life on a par with the iPhone 18 Pro, meaning it should, according to our own tests , make it through more than a day and a half. There are two batteries in the Duo, although according to Apple, they work as one, discharge as one and do all things together. The Duo is compatible with the USB-C version of the Apple Pencil. At this point, it is unclear if and when other models of the company's stylus will follow the same path. We're still not sure how much of the iPhone Duo's bigger display we'll be using, considering it has specific purposes and the front screen is big enough to perform most of our tasks. We're foreseeing we'll be using the front display for work and communication, and the bigger one for entertainment and gaming. If the overwhelming orders are any indication, Apple's iPhone Duo is poised to do well. The device feels refined, but its biggest draw may be its seamless integration into Apple's ecosystem. That's a compelling selling point for those who usually find foldables cumbersome or complicated, if they're willing to splash the cash.

title: Halo Trust demining workers still trapped by Houthi siege in Taiz
description: Staff have been separated from families as blockade of city continues to deplete supplies
content: About 30 deminers from the Halo Trust remain among hundreds of thousands of civilians stuck in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz, the organisation said on Wednesday. Houthi rebels have encircled the government-held city as the two sides fight for control. The blockade has effectively severed the last route through the mountains connecting the city to the interim capital of Aden, the trust said. Taiz region is heavily contaminated by mines, it added. All supply routes in and out of the city are cut off. Humanitarian groups have been warning about the dwindling food, water, medicine and fuel supplies in the city. The organisation said one of its employees is stuck outside the city, unable to reunite with her children. “Behind this siege are real people facing impossible choices. Our staff are trapped in Taiz, separated from their families and uncertain when they’ll see their loved ones again,” the Halo Trust's Yemen programme manager Mara van der Kamp said. “The longer this siege continues, the greater the suffering for civilians who have nowhere safe to turn." On Wednesday, the Houthis claimed a ballistic missile attack on a Saudi operations room in Aden, Yemen's de facto capital. Saudi Arabia did not immediately confirm the strike. Last Thursday, Houthi missiles were fired at the Presidential Palace in Aden, killing five people. On Monday, the government confirmed the deaths of at least 73 people when the Houthis struck a military training camp in Shabwa. Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in ⁠support of the government in 2015, fearing the rise of Iranian influence and the prospect of chaos on its borders, after the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa. In 2022 the UN brokered a truce between the warring ⁠sides that kept a fragile peace in place until this year. Saudi Arabia resumed its military campaign in Yemen in support of the internationally recognised government in a bid to reverse the Houthis' sudden gains last month, when they swept along the Red Sea coast to the critical Bab Al Mandeb strait. The EU has urged the Houthis to lift their siege of Taiz, as the Yemeni government appealed to the UN for urgent action to avert a humanitarian catastrophe. At least 600,000 people in Taiz depend on aid, including more than 200,000 children. More ⁠than 200,000 people have been displaced from their homes since fighting began in ⁠recent weeks, the UN's International Organisation for Migration said.

title: Shuttle service to connect Yas Island attractions to Etihad Rail station in Abu Dhabi
description: Free service to create more options for rail passengers
content: Miral and Etihad Rail have agreed to partner on first-and-last-mile transport to connect Yas Island , Abu Dhabi's leisure and entertainment hub, with the city's railway station. The service will increase connectivity between Yas Island's theme parks and Etihad Rail's Mohamed bin Zayed City station in Abu Dhabi . Ferrari World, Yas Waterworld, Warner Bros World and SeaWorld are among the attractions operated by Miral, the company behind Yas Island, that are set to be connected by the free shuttle bus network. The key priority is to make the journey “as seamless as possible”, Miral said. “Our collaboration with Etihad Rail represents an important step towards creating a more integrated journey, connecting rail travel with the Yas Express network to enhance accessibility and convenience for our guests,” said Lisa Goswell, senior vice president of sales at Miral Destinations. “Together, we are helping to advance the UAE’s vision for smarter, more sustainable mobility while supporting the continued growth of the tourism sector.” The deal will add to the list of shuttle services operating to and from the station. Yas Express operates its fleet of shuttles around the city to bring tourists to theme parks, even extending to Dubai and the Northern Emirates. The Yas Express ER1 route currently connects the Abu Dhabi station with Yas Mall, picking up and dropping off passengers at the mall's north entrance. The free shuttle leaves the station at 7.40am, 1.05pm and 7.35pm, and the journey takes 30 minutes. The return shuttle leaves Yas Mall at 12.15pm and 4.15pm and takes 45 minutes. Etihad Rail has increased its first-mile and last-mile offerings since the passenger service between Abu Dhabi and Fujairah started on June 30. “We are focused on making passenger rail a practical and convenient part of how people move across the country,” said Adhraa Almansoori, executive director of commercial and support at Etihad Rail Mobility. For those heading towards central Abu Dhabi, AD Mobility has introduced two dedicated routes, MR1 and MR2, connecting the rail station with major bus hubs in the capital. MR1 links Mohamed bin Zayed City Station with Abu Dhabi's Main Bus Station, while MR2 connects it with Al Zahiyah Bus Station, in both directions. MR1's stops serve Al Jazeera Club, Al Mushrif Mall and Al Rawdah interchange, while MR2 connects through Al Rawdah and Mazyad Bus Interchange before reaching Al Zahiyah. Etihad Rail also operates shuttles to Reem Mall, Adnec and Adnoc HQ for Dh10 per journey, in addition to the train fare.

title: NBA targets 2027 Europe expansion as EuroLeague charts own path
description: American association promises faster growth and profits even as European body refuses merger and unveils 10-year business plan
content: The NBA are surging ahead with their plans for a new basketball league in Europe, which is set to roll out in 12 months’ time, despite the failed negotiations for a possible partnership with the EuroLeague, the continent’s current premier competition. NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said on Tuesday that the European venture, in collaboration with FIBA (basketball’s international governing body), will be “the largest investment in European basketball in its history”. Earlier this month, the EuroLeague, which currently features 20 teams, including Dubai Basketball , rejected an offer from the NBA to merge and form a single European operation. The EuroLeague then followed that up by unveiling a 10-year business plan last Friday that included a shift to a franchise-based model projected to lead to a three-fold increase in the collective value of the current licensed clubs, which would reach an amount of €5.4 billion over the next 10 years. Department of Culture and Tourism - Abu Dhabi (DTC Abu Dhabi) has made significant investments in basketball with multi-year deals in place with both the NBA and the EuroLeague. The agreement with the NBA, which was renewed early this year, includes staging NBA preseason games in Abu Dhabi, setting up development initiatives, and centralising the league’s global academies at one single location in the UAE capital. Meanwhile, the deal between DCT Abu Dhabi and the EuroLeague includes a sponsorship component and brought the Final Four to Etihad Arena in 2025, as well as the inaugural edition of the EuroLeague Super Cup to the same venue last month. Despite recent developments, Tatum assured that the NBA’s plans are full steam ahead, adding, “we continue to be hopeful that we'll reach an agreement, but we're prepared to proceed regardless.” Tatum did not commit to a specific timeline regarding the announcement of any team deals for the NBA Europe project but is confident things will be in place for the intended tip-off next year. “We continue to target October 2027. We target that to begin rolling out this project. And we believe that the timing is realistic here,” he said. “Remember, this is not just about a season and launching a new league, it's reimagining the entire European basketball ecosystem, built on that merit-based foundation that gives every fan and club in Europe the right to dream. “So, this is a historic moment, and we are going to take the time we need to get it right, but we definitely expect to begin announcing teams soon as agreements get finalised.” While Tatum refused to divulge details of any negotiations that have taken place with the EuroLeague , he did respond to questions posed about their 10-year business plan, and how the NBA’s proposal is expected to create “significantly more value” and bring a “much quicker pathway to profitability”. “We believe that we've developed a model here that combines the best elements of global sports, including the merit-based pathways that make European sport so special,” said Tatum, referring to the proposed model of promotion and relegation introduced by the NBA/FIBA venture. “As we thought about this European league, as we went into it, the passion is there. There's no doubt that the fans love the game of basketball. You see that in the arenas, in the experiences and we want to maintain that. We want to preserve that. But there's still a lot of confusion for fans of European basketball today. “What we believe is that our model is going to actually widen the opportunity for fans to actually understand the merit-based pathway of how their teams can play in the top-tier league. And so that's what we're focused on. “The 10-year business plan by the EuroLeague doesn't affect our plans. I will tell you that our model will provide clubs with a much quicker pathway to profitability. I saw some of the reports in terms of the teams that are not financially stable in the EuroLeague today. “The average permanent team in our league is projected to be profitable by year three. I saw the amount of investment that the EuroLeague is going to distribute back to its clubs. I will tell you that our projections show that we're going to triple those projections – billions and billions of dollars in distributions over 10 years that will go back to these clubs and make them financially stable. “Beyond team profitability, we're also focused on investment. This will be the largest investment in European basketball in its history. We'll invest in academies, grassroots development, league operations, marketing, and arena infrastructure, which is really needed. “We’ll leverage the NBA's global platform, our reach, and our expertise in premium IP to really unlock the full potential of European basketball and put the game on a stronger financial footing, which is going to be better for the clubs, which is going to be better for the players, which is going to be better for the fans. So, that's what we're really focused on and we're moving forward. So, we're excited about that.” Last year, NBA commissioner Adam Silver told The National that the intended 16-team Europe league is meant to be a hybrid of permanent franchises and teams that would go through promotion and relegation. “I think we want the best of both systems. I think from a financial standpoint, in terms of creating incentives to build arena infrastructures and invest in team organisations, having some permanence obviously helps from an investor standpoint,” Silver explained. “On the other hand, we do want to take advantage of great European traditions in sport and of course, promotion and relegation is part of that.” With negotiations stalling between the NBA/FIBA and the EuroLeague, the battle for Europe’s basketball riches could lead to a fragmented offering that could undervalue both operations. “To us, it's not about us or them, it's how can we collectively do a better job continuing to advance the game in Europe?” Silver had said in his interview with The National 12 months ago. At the moment, it’s definitely a case of ‘us versus them’. In his opening remarks with international reporters on Tuesday, Tatum noted how the last eight NBA MVPs were all born outside the United States. Tuesday’s opening night of the new NBA season featured rosters with 70 European players, marking the second consecutive season and second time ever with at least that many. France has a league-high 17 international players competing in the NBA for the 2026/27 campaign, marking the first time in 13 seasons that a country other than Canada has led the NBA in international players. “These players not only generate interest among fans from their respective countries and regions, but they're superstars who resonate with billions of NBA fans globally,” Tatum added. “There's never been a better time to be an international NBA fan, but even with everything that we're doing to engage the billions of passionate fans around the world, we still believe that we're just scratching the surface of how popular this game and this league can be on a global basis.” The new European league is meant to capitalise on the NBA’s global appeal, and expand it even further. The door for further negotiations with the EuroLeague remains open, according to Tatum. Time will tell if both sides will become partners or competitors moving forward.

title: Greece rejects Libya-Turkey maritime deal after eastern parliament approves pact
description: Athens says 2019 agreement breaches international law and infringes on sovereign rights of countries in eastern Mediterranean
content: Greece has rejected the approval by Libya’s eastern parliament of a maritime agreement with Turkey, saying the deal breaches international law and infringes on the sovereign rights of countries in the eastern Mediterranean. Libya is divided between two governments, one in the west, based in Tripoli and another in the east in Benghazi. The deal was originally agreed to by the government in the west. The eastern-based House of Representatives, aligned with military commander Field Marshal Khalifa Haftar , unanimously approved the 2019 agreement on Tuesday, reversing its previous opposition to the deal and its decision to sever political ties with Ankara. The agreement delineates maritime jurisdiction areas between the two countries in the Mediterranean, where competing territorial claims and offshore energy exploration have fuelled tension. Greece, Egypt and Cyprus have long been opposed to it, and they see it as infringing on their own maritime claims. The Greek Foreign Ministry said the parliamentary vote did not change what it described as the agreement’s “illegal, null and void” status. Athens said that Turkey and Libya did not have opposite or adjacent coastlines that would provide a legal basis for delimiting maritime zones. Greece said the agreement disregarded the maritime rights of its islands. "We call ​on the ⁠Libyan side to refrain from any ‌action that contravenes International Law and undermines stability in the Eastern Mediterranean," the statement read. It added that it had informed its partners and allies and would take appropriate measures to protect its sovereign rights. Following the ratification, Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis held phone calls with his Cypriot and Egyptian counterparts, according to readouts from the Greek Foreign Ministry. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU deeply regretted the Libyan parliament’s ratification of the agreement. She emphasised the bloc’s longstanding opposition to the deal and its support for Greece and Cyprus. “This agreement infringes upon the sovereign rights of third states, it does not comply with the Law of the Sea, and is null and void,” Ms von der Leyen said in a post on X. Turkey's Foreign Ministry welcomed the Libyan ​parliament's decision, saying the agreement respected the mutual rights and interests of both countries under international law and the principles of equity. "Turkey will continue its determination to work together with all partners to ensure security, stability and peace in the Mediterranean basin," the ministry said. Athens and Cairo signed an overlapping deal designating an exclusive economic zone in the eastern Mediterranean in 2020, which Turkey opposes. Libya broke apart into rival eastern and western administrations more than a decade ago during a civil war after longtime Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi was toppled by a Nato-backed uprising. The vote marks a shift in eastern Libya’s relations with Turkey, which intervened militarily in 2020 to support the Tripoli government against Haftar’s forces. Relations between Ankara and Haftar’s camp have since improved. Lt Gen Saddam Haftar , Field Marshal Haftar’s son who is also his deputy, welcomed the decision, describing the agreement as a means of protecting Libya’s economic interests in the Mediterranean. The decision could further complicate efforts to resolve competing maritime claims in the eastern Mediterranean, a strategically important region with significant natural gas resources.

title: Global private equity investor Advent opens ADGM office
description: Firm joins growing list of international financial institutions setting up in Abu Dhabi
content: Advent, a global private equity investor with more than $109 billion in assets under management, has opened an office in Abu Dhabi’s ADGM , joining the growing list of financial institutions with a presence in the UAE capital. The opening of the new office follows a series of openings by the company globally, including in Tokyo and Hong Kong, the company said in a statement on Wednesday. “The new presence builds on Advent’s long-standing relationships across the Middle East, giving Advent a local base from which to deepen its engagement with investors and support the firm’s existing portfolio companies and explore potential investment opportunities,” the company said. Set up in 1984, the company has made 460 investments in 45 countries. It has 18 offices globally, including in Abu Dhabi. The announcement comes as a growing number of global financial institutions launch their operations at ADGM, despite uncertainty arising from the Iran war. Earlier this month, New Mountain Capital, an alternative investment firm based in New York, said it was opening an office in ADGM to strengthen its presence in the Middle East, while Capital Group, which manages $3.6 trillion in assets, has secured a licence from the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Abu Dhabi's ADGM to operate as a regulated investment manager. The Paris-listed Eurazeo, a European asset manager with €40 billion ($45.2 billion) in assets under management, has also opened an office in the ADGM amid its expansion plans in the region. Other high-profile companies that the UAE capital has attracted in recent months include private credit lender Blue Owl Capital, the tech-focused US company Vista Equity Partners, the world’s largest listed hedge fund Man Group, Barings, Bain Capital, Cantor and the Swiss derivative investment company Adapt Investment Managers. “Advent’s decision to establish an office in ADGM reflects the strength of Abu Dhabi’s proposition as a leading destination for global investment firms,” Arvind Ramamurthy, chief market development officer at ADGM, said. Assets under management at ADGM grew 54 per cent annually in the first six months of 2026, with 49,027 professionals now based at Al Maryah Island and Al Reem Island, an increase of 34 per cent on the same period last year. Collectively, asset managers that established operations in ADGM in the first half of the year oversee more than $2.1 trillion in global assets under management.

title: Sultan Haitham mixes and matches with British style on state visit
description: Omani leader has a look to fit every occasion when he meets UK royals
content: Oman's Sultan Haitham entered St George’s Hall at Windsor Castle for a state banquet on Tuesday wearing a black velvet bisht with heavily embroidered golden borders at the collar, along the front buttons and at the seams. The striped purple and blue turban made of fine cashmere closely matched the attire worn by his predecessor, the late Sultan Qaboos on his own visit to the UK in 1982. It was a ceremonial outfit fitting for the state visit to the castle, hosted by King Charles III and Queen Camilla. The leader of Oman cuts a distinctive figure in the portals of power, with a variety of looks that are all tailored to the occasion. As he stepped down from the plane at Stansted airport on Monday, he was dressed in a simple blue suit, with a tunic jacket and a grey Karakul or Astrakhan hat. At the centre of the state banquet table was the St George and the Dragon candelabrum, surrounded by pomegranates grown on the East Terrace of the castle. The menu included Scottish langoustine and Cornish crab with avocado and tomato. The main course was pot-roasted Windsor pheasant with spiced quince. For dessert, guests enjoyed individual baked Alaska. After-dinner drinks included iced Earl Grey and date, iced mint and rose tea. World politics were at the heart of the invitation. King Charles praised Oman’s pivotal role in securing the passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz , which has been blockaded by Iran since March. He thanked Oman’s “noble efforts in trying to keep open one of the world's most important shipping routes”. He also announced that his son, Prince William , would soon launch a project with the Sultan’s son. Sultan Haitham ’s clothes choices can be as shape-shifting as the country’s politics. While Oman has emerged as a key mediator with Iran in the Gulf and the Houthis in the Red Sea, it is also fast-tracking reforms to supercharge investments and build new hubs and free zones. On Wednesday, Sultan Haitham will make his third visit to Downing Street – the Prime Minister’s residence – in three years. The two countries’ foreign, defence and trade ministers will also hold a separate meeting. Sultan Haitham met former prime minister Keir Starmer shortly before his departure from office in the summer. His outfit then was modern and businesslike: a blue tailored tunic and classic-fit trousers with the smart black hat. Andy Burnham – who succeeded Mr Starmer in July – is equally as open to working with Oman. This is largely over Oman’s plans for a growth hub at Al Batinah. It was inspired by a similar project established by Mr Burnham when he was Mayor on Manchester, and the pair spoke about it in July during their first phone call. “The UK and Oman have built a friendship which generates real benefits for people at home, and I look forward to shaping the next chapter of our relationship,” Mr Burnham said ahead of the meeting on Wednesday. The four-day trip has many nods to the long history of British-Omani relations, which date back to the founding of the sultanate and the routes of seaborne trade. The state visit in 1982 took place shortly after the UK and Oman had partnered in a counterinsurgency that began with a rebellion by Marxist groups in Dhofar in 1965. While Sultan Haitham‘s outfits for the state visit mimic those worn by his predecessor in 1982, they have more modern touches. Sultan Haitham met King Charles and Queen Camilla at Windsor Castle on Tuesday morning wearing a grey worsted wool open abaya with ornate golden embroidery at the seams. Beneath it was a grey tailored tunic and trousers of the same grey fabric, and black dress shoes. His headwear was a white turban. Sultan Haitham met the late Queen Elizabeth II soon after his accession to the throne, dropping by for tea in 2021. On that occasion he wore a three-piece suit in the British style. The Savile Row tailor Dege and Skinner, known for its long history of military and diplomatic uniforms, boasts a royal warrant from the Omani rulers. That relationship dates back to a “trunk show” in Oman by its fitters in the 1970s and the warrant was awarded in 1981.

title: Whoop sees Abu Dhabi as springboard for shift to predictive health, says chief executive
description: Wearable tech company launches clinical research partnership with Department of Health
content: Whoop is pushing deeper into the Gulf's longevity economy. The Boston-based human performance company this week announced a clinical research partnership with Abu Dhabi's Department of Health. The deal builds on a $75 million anchor investment from Mubadala Investment Company and a broader buildout that has made the GCC one of Whoop's fastest-growing markets . “This region has become one of the most important regions for Whoop,” its founder and chief executive Will Ahmed tells On the Record with Hadley Gamble . “We're growing extraordinarily fast here in the GCC. We're up about 15 times in the last three years. Our membership base here has grown over 85 per cent just in the past year.” The company has separately put GCC year-on-year growth at more than 75 per cent. Speaking on stage at the Abu Dhabi Future Health Summit , Mr Ahmed said the Department of Health agreement would fund “powerful clinical research to drive health outcomes” around prevention, sleep, cardiovascular health and ageing. The announcement is the latest layer in a multiyear capital and operational push by Abu Dhabi entities into Whoop, which produces wearable health trackers. On May 7, Whoop and Mubadala said they had formed a strategic partnership “to advance proactive health, performance science and preventative healthcare innovation in the UAE”, anchored by the $75 million investment. That investment was made as part of Whoop's $575 million Series G, which valued the company at $10.1 billion. The round was led by Collaborative Fund and, according to the company, included Mubadala and Abu Dhabi-based 2PointZero Group. Under terms disclosed by both sides, Whoop would establish a dedicated office in Abu Dhabi , expand its Advanced Labs blood-testing product, introduce full Arabic localisation across its platform – launched this month with a GCC-wide campaign – and launch the Whoop-Mubadala Health Research Initiative, a longitudinal research programme aimed at strengthening the UAE's health value chain from diagnostics and genomics to prevention and behavioural optimisation. Mr Ahmed has cast the UAE capital as a proving ground for a shift from reactive to predictive care. “The power of continuous health monitoring is that it can really understand signals in your body that you may not be able to feel,” he says. “We believe those insights can actually drive health outcomes, which is to say it can make you lower your weight, it can make you decrease your blood pressure.” He says the company's thesis since its launch 14 years ago – to validate continuous monitoring with elite athletes and then move into the mainstream – is now playing out in the Gulf. He acknowledges the timing, closing a large Gulf investment shortly after the Iran war began, reflects a long-term commitment. “The timing of some of that partnership was complicated with the wars in this region. But to me, it was obvious to show up because I'd been showing up for the last decade,” he says. For Abu Dhabi, the Whoop partnership is one piece of a broader longevity infrastructure play. An EY survey cited by Abu Dhabi officials found only 43 per cent of respondents follow a structured fitness plan, even as 61 per cent had used a wearable in the past year and 87 per cent reported a positive experience using AI for health decisions – a gap officials believe wearables plus clinical integration can close. Whoop, which has now raised about $1 billion in total capital, said the Gulf expansion would be paired with retail distribution, sponsorships with the UAE Team Emirates-XRG cyclists and Al Nassr football team, and, through Whoop Qatar, its first performance research and developement lab outside Boston, later in 2026. “There are many countries in the world that are excited about wearable technology,” Mr Ahmed says. “When you can remove bureaucracy and you can say, look, no, we want health care not to be reactive but actually proactive, then a lot of things fall in suit.”

title: Mysterious recurring stench adds to Gaza's misery
description: Residents across the territory report waking up to a powerful smell of sewage several times in recent weeks
content: Saber Zaquot awoke early one morning recently to find a foul, sewage-like smell filling the house in Nuseirat camp, central Gaza , where his family lives. At first, the family checked for the most likely sources. “We became anxious and thought the smell might be coming from the bathroom, or even from the children while they were asleep,” Mr Zaqout told The National . “We checked everything several times but could not find the source.” Later that morning, Mr Zaqout saw on social media that people across Gaza were reporting a similar experience. “Residents across the Gaza Strip complained about the smell, both in the south and the north,” he said. Civil defence teams have noted the foul smell repeatedly in recent weeks, spokesman Mahmoud Basal said. The odour had caused confusion and anxiety, with people unsure where it was coming from, he said. “Many residents have complained about these foul odours, particularly children, the elderly and the sick,” Mr Basal told The National . He said the civil defence believed Israeli forces were responsible and claimed that aircraft had been used to disperse the odour. He said Israel had in the past used a foul-smelling liquid to disperse Palestinian protesters, including during the Great March of Return demonstrations along the Gaza border in 2018, and during protests in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood of East Jerusalem. The liquid, developed by an Israeli company, is known as “The Skunk” and its odour has been described as a mixture of sewage and decomposing flesh. Moamen Abu Jayyab, 30, who lives in a camp for displaced people in Al Tawam area of northern Gaza, said he first noticed the foul smell about a month to six weeks ago. “Every now and then, we wake up in the morning to an extremely foul smell, similar to the smell of toilets and sewage,” he told The National . Mr Abu Jayyab said the first time it happened, his family and other residents suspected the camp’s toilets. They inspected them but found nothing unusual. They then checked the sewerage system but could not identify a problem there either. An hour or two later, Mr Abu Jayyab left the camp for the market. “The smell was there too,” he said. “People were talking about how it had spread since dawn across all areas of northern Gaza and was still lingering.” Rumours soon circulated that the Israeli military had released a foul-smelling substance into the air. Mr Abu Jayyab said he initially did not know whether the claims were true, but later saw social media posts and statements from the Gaza civil defence attributing the odour to the Israelis. Gazan authorities have not been able to identify the substance causing the odour because they lack the equipment needed to capture and analyse samples, said Ayman Al Ramlawi, director of the Environment Health and Occupational Safety Department at the Ministry of Health. “We can’t reach a definitive conclusion about the substance without laboratory analysis,” he said. Mr Al Ramlawi warned that exposure to unidentified gases or airborne substances could affect the environment and public health. “The use of such substances and gases undoubtedly has an impact on the environment in the Gaza Strip and on the health of residents, particularly those with weakened immune systems and those suffering from respiratory illnesses,” he said. Mr Abu Jayyab said the smell added another source of distress for families already struggling with displacement and insecurity after two years of war between Israel and Hamas that left Gaza in ruins. “The smell is extremely distressing and the worst thing is waking up to find it in the air,” he said.

title: Dubai Fashion Week returns with Ludovic de Saint Sernin, Tarun Tahiliani and regional talent
description: Spring/summer 2027 edition will bring five days of runway shows and presentations to Dubai Design District, with designers from Lebanon, Kuwait, Bahrain, India and beyond
content: Dubai Fashion Week returns on Thursday, bringing five days of runway shows and presentations, with a line-up spanning established international names, emerging regional talent and designers making their debuts. The spring/summer 2027 edition will open in Dubai Design District with Paris-based designer Ludovic de Saint Sernin, whose shimmering, often provocative creations have attracted celebrity fans including Kim Kardashian and Miley Cyrus. Indian designer Tarun Tahiliani will close the event on October 26, before opening a boutique in Dubai's Jumeirah district, his first outside India. Designers from Kuwait, Lebanon, Bahrain, Egypt, Palestine, Greece, Colombia and the UAE will present their collections, reflecting Dubai's ambition to connect regional talent with the wider international fashion industry. One of the biggest draws this season is de Saint Sernin, whose designs have become synonymous with a sensual, body-conscious approach to fashion. Also showing on the opening day is Kuwaiti designer Yousef Al Jasmi, whose elaborate, crystal-embellished evening wear has become a signature of his label. Tahiliani, who closes the event, is one of India's most established fashion designers. Known for blending traditional Indian craftsmanship with western tailoring, he has built a reputation for elaborate occasion wear, particularly his fluid, intricately draped gowns inspired by the sari. His UAE boutique will further strengthen his ties to the region. While international names provide some of the biggest draws, Dubai Fashion Week continues to offer a platform for designers from the Middle East and showcases the UAE's developing fashion industry. Palestinian-Greek designer Nafsika Skourti will present her latest collection on Friday. Known for combining contemporary tailoring with crystal embellishments, her designs bring a distinctive approach to womenswear. Sunday will see the return of Lebanese label Lili Blanc, alongside the Dubai Fashion Week debuts of Emirati brands Onori and Kuni. The programme extends beyond traditional ready-to-wear collections. On Friday, Bahraini label Touchless will present its 3D-printed bags, bringing technology and experimental design into the spotlight. Egyptian eyewear brand Amr Saad will follow with a presentation of its accessories. Saturday brings a Latin American perspective, with collections from Colombian designers Laura Aparicio, Adriana Capasso and Oda. The day will also feature a runway show by graduates of FADS Dubai fashion school, offering emerging designers an opportunity to present their work as part of the official programme. Away from the runway, Harvey Nichols Dubai at Mall of the Emirates is hosting a pop-up featuring a selection of designers participating in Dubai Fashion Week, connecting the collections on show with the city's retail audience. The first Dubai Fashion Week took place in March 2023. A collaboration between the Arab Fashion Council and Dubai Design District, it evolved from Arab Fashion Week, which began in 2015. It also follows in the footsteps of Fashion Forward, which ran in Dubai from 2013 until 2020, as part of the city's broader efforts to establish itself as a destination for regional and international fashion. This season's programme reflects that international outlook, bringing together designers from Europe, the Middle East, South Asia and Latin America. Dubai Fashion Week spring/summer 2027 takes place from October 22 to October 2 at Dubai Design District. Guests are advised to check official Dubai Fashion Week channels for attendance information and the latest schedule.

title: Russia frees US citizen Stephen Hubbard
description: President Vladimir Putin makes announcement as he hosts Trump envoy for new Ukraine peace talks
content: Russia on Wednesday freed Stephen Hubbard, ⁠a 74-year-old American citizen who had been held in custody since 2022, after a visit by US President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff. In a post on Truth Social, Mr Trump said that he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin during a phone call last week to free Mr Hubbard, and that, unlike previous releases, the US did not have to give up anyone in return. “Welcome home, Stephen, it’s great to have you back,” Mr Trump wrote. Later on Wednesday, during an event at the White House, he said Mr Hubbard was on a flight headed to the US with his family and Mr Witkoff. "I spoke to him this morning. He is the happiest man around," Mr Trump said. Mr Hubbard had been serving a nearly seven-year prison sentence in Russia after being convicted of mercenary activity in a closed-door trial. Mr Trump called him a "wonderful" and a "very high-quality, innocent man". Mr Putin said ​Mr Hubbard, who was detained in Ukraine and sent to Russia, had been freed and was at ⁠St Petersburg's Pulkovo airport. The ⁠announcement came during a ‌meeting with Mr Witkoff ​in a grand imperial palace ​in St Petersburg. The meeting was focused on reviewing new ideas on ending the war ⁠in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since the Second World War. "You talk so much about my President, President Trump, being a humanitarian," Mr Witkoff told the Russian leader in a video circulating on social media. "You are a humanitarian, also, sir, and I salute that." A State Department representative said the Russian government had unilaterally decided to release Mr Hubbard. His "release was not part of an exchange, and no other concessions were provided", the official said in a statement, adding that the Trump administration would continue to work for the release of all Americans unjustly detained in Russia. Mr Witkoff's meeting with Mr Trump comes amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the US is backing ⁠away from Ukraine , at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications . Mr Putin also proposed ⁠meeting ​Mr Trump ⁠in China, ​Russian state TV said. The Kremlin has previously raised the possibility that Mr Putin, Mr Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping could hold three-way talks during ​an ‌Apec ⁠summit in ​China next ​month. Mr Putin ‌also offered ⁠to talk about ⁠restoring economic co-operation between Moscow and Washington, state TV said. Mr Hubbard was arrested in April 2022 in the eastern Ukrainian city of Izyum, where Russian prosecutors alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military ​checkpoint. Prosecutors said Mr Hubbard had joined a ​Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a ‌month. Russian state media reported ‌he pleaded ⁠guilty to the charges. But ​his US-based lawyer, Martin ​De ‌Luca, previously said Mr Hubbard had told him ⁠the charges against him were false ⁠and that he was not in any combat or military unit. At the time of his release, he was ​the only US prisoner held by Russia who was designated by Washington as “wrongfully detained”. Mr Hubbard had served in the US Air Force and National Guard, according to military records quoted by The New ⁠York Times . He earned a master’s degree in English and lived in Japan for 25 years where he taught English before moving to Cyprus and then, in 2014, to Izyum with a Ukrainian partner, according ⁠to his sister.

title: President Sheikh Mohamed holds talks with Prime Minister of Singapore in Abu Dhabi as key deals agreed
description: Lawrence Wong is on a working visit to the Emirates aimed at further bolstering ties
content: President Sheikh Mohamed on Wednesday held high-level talks in Abu Dhabi with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong aimed at advancing long-standing ties. The two leaders explored ways to expand partnership across key sectors such as the economy, investment, advanced technology and artificial intelligence. A number of deals were struck on the second day of Mr Wong's working visit to the Emirates, including plans for a joint energy task force and agreements on higher education and health. Sheikh Mohamed underlined the strength of UAE-Singapore relations and reflected on the similarities of the allies, including successful development models, their shared commitment to championing peace and focus on education and investment in people. Sheikh Mohamed had earlier hosted a welcoming ceremony for Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to mark his working visit to the UAE. Mr Wong received a guard of honour as the national anthems of both the UAE and Singapore were played at the official reception in Abu Dhabi. He thanked Sheikh Mohamed for the warm reception he received and noted the continued growth of UAE-Singapore relations. A high-level welcoming party included Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi; Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs; Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs; Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohamed, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Special Affairs; and Sheikh Mohammed bin Hamad, Adviser to the UAE President; along with a number of ministers and officials. Mr Wong had held talks with the Abu Dhabi Crown Prince after beginning his visit to the Emirates on Tuesday. The two men reflected on long-standing bilateral ties before enjoying a tour of the landmark Zayed National Museum, in Saadiyat Cultural District. The UAE and Singapore formally established diplomatic ties in 1985 and relations have grown steadily across a number of key sectors in the decades since. In February 2019, the two governments signed the Singapore-UAE Comprehensive Partnership, a framework aimed at advancing co-operation across trade, investment, defence, security and sustainable development. More than 600 Singaporean companies operate in the Emirates, in key areas such as fintech, health care, infrastructure and education. In October 2024, Sheikh Khaled made an official visit to the city-state during which he held talks with Mr Wong and witnessed the signing of a host of agreements to strengthen links across artificial intelligence, education and renewable energy. They also held high-level talks at the Singapore Parliament House aimed at cementing long-standing ties. During the meeting, Sheikh Khaled reaffirmed the importance of promoting UAE-Singapore collaboration, with a focus on advanced technology, clean energy and urban planning.

title: Dubai records strong sales for homes valued at over $10m as it attracts wealthy despite Iran war
description: Volumes for the quarter down about 17 per cent annually, Knight Frank report finds
content: Dubai recorded 86 residential transactions valued at $10 million or more during the third quarter this year, down 17 per cent annually, as wealthy investors continued to invest in the emirate despite the Iran war. Among the deals, 13 were for homes valued at more than $25 million, property consultancy Knight Frank said in its latest report on Wednesday. Of the total, the 73 that were in the $10 million to $25 million bracket had a combined value of Dh3.93 billion ($1.07 billion), with the remaining 13 transactions generating Dh1.84 billion. The highest-value transactions accounted for about 15 per cent of sales for more than $10 million by number, but nearly 32 per cent of their total value. “Despite the exceptional geopolitical backdrop across the region, Dubai’s luxury homes market has continued to record high volumes of sales during Q3, albeit these are lower than this time last year,” said Faisal Durrani, partner and head of research, Mena at Knight Frank. Prices across the city’s 10 prime neighbourhoods have dipped for the first time since 2020, declining by 5 per cent between the second and third quarters, he said. In total, prime transaction volumes are 29.4 per cent lower than this time last year. “The biggest drag at the moment on overall market activity is the ongoing regional conflict . The somewhat ‘stop-start’ nature of the hostilities is predictably a confidence dampener,” Mr Durrani said. Dubai and Abu Dhabi continue to attract wealthy individuals on the back of government initiatives that support economic growth, including favourable tax environments, business-friendly policies and significant infrastructure investment. Net wealth in the UAE is set to jump to $6 trillion by the end of this decade despite the short-term volatility caused by the Middle East conflict , a report this month by Boston Consulting Group found. In the five years to the end of 2030, net wealth in the Emirates is set to increase by more than $2.3 trillion, at an annual growth rate of 10.6 per cent, the report said. Dubai and Abu Dhabi have also been ranked among the top 10 destinations for next-generation wealth despite current war-related concerns, Savills said in a report this week. Dubai was ranked eighth and the capital 10th among favoured cities for the $84 trillion of wealth expected to be transferred between generations over the next two decades, it said. In the first nine months of the year, a total of 412 transactions worth $10 million or more were recorded in Dubai, up 15 per cent on an annual basis, Knight Frank's latest report found. The combined value of the deals this year stood at about $6.67 billion, the report said. On a quarterly basis, transaction volumes in the third quarter were down about 34 per cent from the previous period, the report said. In terms of areas of Dubai, Palm Jumeirah recorded the most residential sales worth $10 million or more in the third quarter, with 27 transactions worth Dh2.01 billion, Knight Frank found. The community accounted for approximately 31 per cent of luxury homes sold between July and September and 35 per cent of their total value. “The easing of prices by 9.1 per cent over the last 12-months means the island is increasingly offering ‘good value’ at Dh4,083 per square foot,” said Louis Harding, partner and head of UAE residential at Knight Frank. “Buyer interest here continues to largely stem from those seeking a permanent or holiday home, rather than buy-to-flip investors.” Jumeirah ranked second by transaction volume, followed by Emirates Hills, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Golf Estates.

title: Non-Iran Middle East oil exports recover to prewar levels with Hormuz alternatives
description: Oil flow averages more than 24.5 million barrels a day for week ended October 18
content: Non-Iran Middle East oil exports have surpassed prewar levels as ships continued to transit through the Strait of Hormuz , a key route for global oil supplies, despite rise in attacks on vessels. The total oil flows, including shipments through Hormuz and alternative routes across the region, averaged more than 24.5 million barrels per day for the week ended October 18, surpassing the 24.4 million bpd for the week ending February 22, just before the Iran war broke out, according to preliminary data from Kpler. The total volumes recorded include Hormuz transits, Gulf of Oman ship to ship net exports, Gulf of Oman terminal loadings from Fujairah and Oman ports and Red Sea exports. The data excludes Iranian exports. The data is an estimate which is subject to change depending on ship crossings across the strait at a given time. The conflict began on February 28 with the US and Israel attacking Iran. Tehran retaliated with attack s on its Gulf neighbours and ships carrying oil through the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow water channel in the Arabian Gulf. The strait has been subject to an Iranian blockade since the start of the conflict, but ships are continuing to transit make it through, with about 19 commodity vessels crossing on a daily basis in the last 10 days, the data shows. More than 100 ships a day used to cross the strait before the war, carrying oil, fertilisers and refined products to global markets. But Iranian attacks have resulted in ship owners avoiding the channel. According to International Maritime Organisation data, there have been 116 attacks on ships up to October 20, with 24 deaths since the conflict began. Attacks have increased recently. The US also plans to allow ships that are under sanctions to sail through the channel that is expected to help increase flows to global markets. The dark fleet, sometimes referred to as the shadow fleet, refers to a group of ships that sail outside conventional shipping regulations. These vessels use deceptive shipping practices to transport cargo that is under sanctions or at high risk, deliberately concealing it to avoid detection. The US administration's plan would involve investors buying and refurbishing the idle vessels before using them to transport legitimate oil. Oil continues to trade higher amid the Middle East conflict, with Brent, the benchmark for two thirds of the world's oil, trading above $110 a barrel at 1.16pm UAE time on Wednesday. West Texas Intermediate, the gauge that tracks US crude, was nearing $100 per barrel.

title: Sheikh Tahnoon holds talks with US venture capitalist David Fialkow
description: Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi and founder of General Catalyst discuss opportunities for collaboration
content: Opportunities for business and technology partnerships were at the centre of talks as Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed , Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi and National Security Adviser, met US billionaire businessman David Fialkow. Sheikh Tahnoon and Mr Fialkow, co-founder of venture capitalist firm General Catalyst, discussed advances in the technology sector and their impact on investment trends. They emphasised the importance of harnessing expertise and investment capabilities towards spurring economic growth. Sheikh Tahnoon said they "exchanged perspectives on shared areas of interest and potential avenues for collaboration," in a post on X on Wednesday. Mr Fialkow established General Catalyst in 2000, which now handles billions of dollars worth of assets and has invested in more than 800 companies, with its portfolio including varied interests such as Airbnb to Anthropic. On Tuesday, AI-powered voice transcription tool Otter announced it had raised $320 million from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund. The cutting-edge company will use the financial backing to support international expansion and product innovation. Sheikh Tahnoon, who is also Chairman of the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council, plays a central role in Abu Dhabi's growing global investment strategy and its sharp focus on advanced technologies. He regularly meets prominent business and technology leaders to promote investment opportunities and collaboration. He has previously held talks with G42 chief executive Peng Xiao and Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella, as well as high-ranking US officials from the current administration. In February, he met former British prime minister Tony Blair to discuss the growing significance of AI and government efficiency.

title: Sultan's state visit: King Charles praises Oman's 'noble efforts' to keep Strait of Hormuz open
description: UK and Oman to announce major investments during Sultan Haitham's visit
content: Britain's King Charles III praised Oman’s “noble efforts” to keep the Strait of Hormuz open in a speech at a state banquet at Windsor Castle. Speaking at times in Arabic, the king told Sultan Haitham he recognised “Oman’s enduring commitment as a trusted interlocutor to all parties” at a time when conflict has returned “so painfully to the region”. At the end of the first day of Sultan Haitham's state visit to Britain, he thanked Oman for its “noble efforts in trying to keep open one of the world's most important shipping routes”, saying it had been of “great service to the whole international community, and particularly to the most vulnerable of those affected”. The king added: “Oman’s role across the Gulf and her ‘constructive neutrality’ … matters far beyond Hormuz, and is worthy of our utmost respect.” He described Oman as “one of Britain’s oldest allies” and “closest friends”, saying he was especially delighted that his son Prince William, the Prince of Wales, and Sultan Haitham's son the Crown Prince, Theyazin bin Haitham, had worked together as joint patrons of the Jewel of Arabia expedition across Oman. It retraced the 1928 coastal route of British explorer Bertram Thomas last year. “There can be fewer happier symbols of success than a living relationship being passed from one generation to the next,” he said. The king, who has been taking Arabic lessons, quoted poetry and praised Oman’s “breathtaking landscape” which he has seen on many visits. The state banquet, for 160 guests, was the culmination of the first day of the sultan’s three-day state visit to the UK. It began with a horse-drawn procession to Windsor Castle, where he spent time with the UK royals. Sultan Haitham presented the king with the Order of Al Said, which the king later wore to the banquet. Across London at the Guildhall, business leaders discussed opportunities following the UK-GCC trade agreement signed earlier this year. A “major mandate” of Sultan Haitham’s visit is to facilitate investment between the UK and Oman, Haitham Al Salmi, chief executive of Muscat Stock Exchange, told The National . Omani and British officials are due to sign a series of deals on Wednesday as Sultan Haitham meets Prime Minister Andy Burnham, including participation in a $1 billion data centre in Salalah. Mr Burnham attended the banquet last night, his first as prime minister, and was seated next to Jokha Alharthi, the Man Booker prize-winning writer, and General Sultan bin Mohammed al Nu’amani, Minister of the Royal Office. The UK and Oman will commit to closer co-operation across security, defence and trade “as the countries take their centuries old partnership to a new level”, a Downing Street statement said. Boosting the UK-Oman Sovereign Investment Partnership means increased investment across a number of key sectors, including in renewable energy, technology, critical minerals, space, health care and financial services. The UK Export Finance credit agency will increase its financing capacity up to £7 billion for British exports to Oman. While Oman has emerged as a key mediator with Iran in the Gulf and the Houthis in the Red Sea, it is also fast-tracking reforms to supercharge investments and build hubs and free zones. The two countries are also expected to sign an agreement to secure maritime co-operation through strengthened information-sharing with the Omani Maritime Security Centre. The UK will announce the return of the Chevening Educational Scholarship Programme to Oman, offering access to British education institutions. Wednesday will see Sultan Haitham's third visit in three years to the Prime Minister’s residence in Downing Street. The two countries’ foreign, defence and trade ministers will also hold a separate meeting. Sultan Haitham was the first overseas leader to meet former prime minister Keir Starmer after the general election in 2024 and also met him just days before Mr Starmer stood down from the role. The sultan has already found common ground with Mr Burnham, who succeeded Mr Starmer in July. This is largely over Oman’s plans for a growth hub at Al Batinah. It was inspired by a similar project established by Mr Burnham when he was Mayor of Manchester, and the pair spoke about it in July during their first phone call. “The UK and Oman have built a friendship which generates real benefits for people at home, and I look forward to shaping the next chapter of our relationship,” Mr Burnham said before the meeting on Wednesday. “Economic growth, security, defence, education: these are just some of the priorities we share as we plot a course through an increasingly complex world. “Working together, we are leading with our values and creating opportunities for people in both our countries.”

title: France's Macron secures gas from Qatar during Gulf trip
description: French President wraps up three-day tour as his government seeks to bolster energy security amid domestic unrest over soaring fuel prices
content: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Wednesday that he had secured gas supply guarantees from Qatar during his Gulf tour, as he seeks to stabilise energy prices in his country after violent protests sparked by the rising cost of living. "We secured during the winter period the equivalent of two terawatt-hours per month of LNG, which was important for us and which will allow us to move forward," he told reporters in Doha. Qatar was the last scheduled stop of Mr Macron ’s three-day Gulf trip, which also took him to Kuwait, the UAE and Bahrain, as France looks to strengthen ties with regional partners amid heightened tension and concerns over energy security. However, the French President made an announced stop in Saudi Arabia later on Wednesday, where he held talks in Riyadh with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The French presidency said Mr Macron's visit, the first by a western leader since Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militia intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia this month, was “to ​demonstrate France's solidarity with the kingdom in the face of attacks launched by the Houthis against its territory, and to continue efforts aimed at securing and diversifying ​hydrocarbon ‌supplies”. France is bracing for renewed protests on Saturday, after a weekend of demonstrations that descended into rioting and looting. Authorities have introduced curfews in response to the unrest. Mr Macron met Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim on Tuesday at Lusail Palace. They spoke about bilateral relations, as well as ways to strengthen and develop ties across various fields, particularly the economic, investment, security and defence sectors, the state-run Qatar News Agency reported. Qatar, one of the world’s leading liquefied natural gas exporters, has extensive energy and investment ties with France. French energy company TotalEnergies is a partner in Qatar’s North Field East LNG expansion project, one of the world’s largest gas developments. Iran ’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz after the US and Israel launched strikes against the Islamic republic in February disrupted global energy supplies, sending oil prices higher and intensifying inflationary pressures. With Saudi Arabia diverting oil exports to Red Sea ports to bypass Hormuz, a vital artery for global energy shipments, Houthi threats to shipping through the Bab El Mandeb strait have opened a second potential chokepoint, further jeopardising energy flows and adding to economic pressures in Europe. The Houthi rebels are fighting against Yemen’s internationally recognised government and its Saudi allies. This month, they carried out attacks on Riyadh’s main airport , killing 17 people, injuring more than 300 and forcing a complete shutdown of operations. There have been 20 strikes on the airport since the start of October. Responding to a question from The National before leaving Doha, Mr Macron said talks with the Houthis should resume for tension to ease. He added that French personnel and capabilities had been sent to support the kingdom. "We stand alongside Saudi Arabia in ensuring its security and defence," said Mr Macron. “We have offered to help rehabilitate the site and, above all, secure it,” he said, referring to Saudi Arabia ’s oil pipeline linking the Arabian Gulf to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. “For the past eight days, we have had personnel and capabilities deployed there,” he added. The war between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is a spillover from the wider, nearly eight-month war with Iran . Washington and Tehran have not yet reached a lasting peace agreement . In recent weeks, they have exchanged proposals to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but negotiations have not resumed. Mr Macron said France had maintained contact with Washington and Tehran, urged calm and de-escalation, and put forward proposals to reopen the Strait of Hormuz through international and Omani waters. “Our proposal remains on the table. It is still valid, and we discussed it at length,” he said. "I think the coming hours and days will allow us to receive a response, particularly from Iran. It is on the basis of that response that we will be able to assess the situation," he added. Before arriving in Qatar, Mr Macron visited Bahrain , where he met King Hamad. Their discussions focused on bilateral relations, energy security and regional developments. France has secured commitments from Bahrain and the UAE to each supply an additional 100,000 tonnes of diesel a month. Together with additional supplies from Saudi Arabia, the commitments amount to about 295,000 tonnes a month, equivalent to slightly more than 10 per cent of France’s usual diesel consumption. Rising diesel prices have added to the cost-of-living pressures facing households in France and elsewhere. The International Energy Agency earlier this month urged member countries to accelerate pledged diesel releases and consider supplying additional volumes as global markets tightened. European diesel is trading at almost $200 a barrel amid the Iran war and Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries. In Abu Dhabi, Mr Macron met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed . The two countries exchanged a strategic defence partnership framework and signed agreements covering energy, artificial intelligence and advanced technology. Defence co-operation featured prominently in the visit, with France and the UAE signing an intergovernmental agreement on co-operation on the Dassault Rafale F5 standard within their respective Rafale programmes, reflecting efforts to deepen military ties amid geopolitical uncertainty stemming from the regional war. Mr Macron began his tour in Kuwait on Monday, where agreements, memorandums of understanding and declarations of intent covering defence, civil aviation, artificial intelligence, investment, health and academic co-operation were signed.

title: Australian MP has both legs amputated after ramming 'attack'
description: Police charge Brendan Nugent, 43, after Helen Haines critically injured outside her office
content: An Australian MP has had both legs amputated after she was rammed by a car in the street outside her office earlier this week. Independent Helen Haines was critically injured as she retrieved an item from her car in the rural town of Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday. Another vehicle made a U-turn and struck Mrs Haines, before reversing and driving into her a second time, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said on Tuesday. Doctors amputated one of her legs on Monday and then her other leg on Wednesday, her husband Phil Haines said at the Melbourne hospital where she is being treated. “The good news in all this is Helen is alive and she’s stable,” he said. “This is the most important thing for our family.” Australian police have charged Brendan Nugent, 43, over the alleged attack on the MP, according to an official. He was charged with causing harm to a Commonwealth public official, intentionally causing serious harm and dangerous driving, according to a statement from police on Tuesday. Mr Nugent appeared briefly in Wangaratta Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday and was remanded in custody until his next hearing in February.
