title: Syria and World Bank to set up recovery and rebuilding fund
description: Finance Minister says agreement helps new phase of co-operation with international partners
content: Syria and the World Bank have agreed to set up a multi-donor trust fund for the country's recovery and reconstruction, the two sides announced in a joint statement on Sunday. Damascus is continuing to rebuild after a civil war that lasted for more than a decade and had destroyed the country's infrastructure. The Syria Recovery and Reconstruction Trust Fund – or “Start” – is a multi-donor fund that aims to provide concessional financing, investment guarantees and technical assistance, and build trust, the statement said. The agreement comes after Syria took part in the International and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. The gatherings were the latest to be attended by Syrian officials since the fall of president Bashar Al Assad's regime in December 2024. Syrian Finance Minister Yisr Barnieh said the agreement helps to set the foundation for a new phase of co-operation with Damascus's international partners. Partners in the US, Europe and Middle East expressed their support for the initiative, the statement said. “An important milestone in Syria’s recovery and reconstruction journey,” Mr Barnieh wrote in a post on X. The World Bank in 2025 estimated Syria's reconstruction would cost about $216 billion , making it one of the most expensive rebuilding efforts in history. The World Bank classified this as its best “conservative” estimate. The World Bank said infrastructure accounted for 48 per cent, or $52 billion, of total damage from the civil war, followed by residential buildings at $33 billion and non-residential buildings at $33 billion. It said the multi-donor trust fund will help to support the delivery of basic services, strengthen institutional capacities and expand economic opportunities. “We look forward to working with all partners to support a comprehensive and sustainable recovery path,” said Ousmane Dione, World Bank vice president for the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan. Syria's transitional government has been racing to secure investment commitments to help rebuild the country's infrastructure. Some of those pledges have recently gone to the implementation phase, including DP World's $800 million towards Tartus Port . The country has secured deals with its other Gulf partners, including a $2 billion Saudi Arabian investment package to develop two airports in Aleppo, as well as other projects involving energy, real estate and telecommunications. At this week's gatherings in Thailand, Mr Barnieh also held discussions with Qatari Finance Minister Ali Al Kuwari on supporting recovery and development work, the state-run news agency Sana reported. Norway also expressed interest in contributing to the trust fund, Sana reported. Qatar has also offered financing for projects to rehabilitate Syria's electricity grids, water networks, public services and the Damascus International Airport. Baker Hughes, Caterpillar and Visa were among a delegation of about 50 US companies that visited Syria last month to explore and deepen economic ties, which came weeks after the US delisted Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism. Syria will also return to the Arab group at the International Monetary Fund beginning on November 1, leaving the Russian-led group it joined in 2012, the Finance Ministry said in a post on Telegram. The IMF restarted communications with Syria in 2025. The fund said in August it had agreed on a technical assistance programme for the country after a staff-level visit in July. The IMF has not had an Article IV consultation with Syria since 2009.

title: Iraq renews calls for pact with Gulf and says security 'cannot be brought from abroad'
description: Baghdad hosts major conference of Islamic countries for first time in 45 years
content: Iraq ’s Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said on Sunday that stability in the Middle East must come from within the region itself, not from external powers, renewing calls for a security dialogue with Gulf states. Speaking after the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation (OIC) held a council of foreign ministers in Baghdad, Mr Hussein described the security situation as critical. “The security situation in the region is complex and the region, in fact, as a whole is under fire, so the first priority we need is stability and security,” Mr Hussein said at a joint press conference with the OIC's Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed. “We cannot buy security from abroad, we need internal security, and that internal security is the co-operation between the countries of the region,” he added. The high-level OIC meeting was first of its kind in the Iraqi capital in 45 years, and is seen as part of Iraq's broader effort to reassert itself as a regional mediator. Iraq has in recent years positioned itself as a rare interlocutor able to talk to all sides – maintaining close ties with Gulf Co-operation Council states, a strategic partnership with Iran and a security relationship with the US. The call for a home-grown security architecture is not new for Baghdad. Three years ago, Iraq had proposed a formula bringing together the six GCC states plus Iraq and Iran, but “due to certain circumstances there was no response to this initiative”, Mr Hussein said. The initiative, which he referred to as 6+2, was revisited after the Iran war broke out in February. The current push comes amid a renewed wave of instability across the region, from the war in Gaza and escalations in Lebanon and the Red Sea to continued tensions with Iran and threats to shipping in the Gulf. “Recently there have been important contacts between the concerned countries, especially between Gulf states, Iraq and Iran, to activate this initiative,” he added. The minister said that “we will work to hold a meeting in this regard and we look forward to being in Baghdad.” However, the initiative still needs “intensive contacts”, he added. “If a meeting is held between these countries, the issue of security will be raised, the issue of stopping the war will be raised, and initiatives to start peace and stability will be raised,” he said. The 6+2 concept has been touted by Baghdad as a pragmatic framework that acknowledges geographic reality. The idea is that the eight coastal states of the Gulf share inseparable security and economic interests, from oil exports and freedom of navigation to climate change and water scarcity, regardless of political rivalries. The economic argument is central to Baghdad’s pitch. Iraq is pursuing its ambitious Development Road project linking the Gulf to Turkey and Europe, and Gulf states are looking to invest in Iraqi gas, electricity and infrastructure. Officials in Baghdad argue that such projects cannot move forward while the region remains locked in a cycle of confrontation and external security dependency. Without stability, the minister continued, “we cannot move towards economic development, we cannot move towards building the economy, nor towards investment, so we need security and stability”. He added that regional countries, not foreign powers, should lead peace initiatives. “The priority is about security and stability, and I believe it is incumbent upon our countries, the countries of the region, to put forward initiatives on how to achieve security and peace, not foreign countries,” he said. Foreign countries “come but only think of their own interests, while the countries of the region and the people of the region are the stakeholders, therefore we seek to achieve stability in the region”. Iraq will continue to communicate with these countries with the help of the Secretary General of the OIC “until we reach this outcome”, he said.

title: Arsenal show 'champion's spirit' to edge out Nottingham Forest thanks to Noni Madueke late show
description: Gunners need deflected to strike to break deadlock at City Ground and keep within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City
content: Arsenal left it late before snatching a late Premier League victory at Nottingham Forest on Sunday, courtesy of a deflected Noni Madueke strike. The Gunners had been misfiring in front of goal at the City Ground having failed to register a shot on target for 79 minutes. But then Declan Rice, who had been guilty of a glaring miss seven minutes earlier when he swept a glorious chance to break the deadlock over the bar, had slipped the ball into the feet of Madueke. The former Chelsea winger then cut inside Daniel Munoz with a couple of stopovers before firing off a shot that clipped off Jair Cunha then flew into the back of the net. There would still be time for Forest to nearly snatch a leveller, though. First, a brilliant solo run by Murillo ended with the Brazilian curling an effort over the bar, while Liam Delap was then denied a shot on goal by a superbly-timed Ezri Konsa tackle. It was a far from scintillating performance from Mikel Arteta's side but the champions have that enviable habit of being able to eke out three points when it matters. “This place is so hard to come to, everybody knows it,” said Match-winner Madueke.” They make it so difficult for you. It was a really tough game but we are really happy as we did it all together. We showed grit and determination and a champion's spirit. “The first half is usually cagey here, in the last few years it has been 0-0. The manager told us to stick in there and stick with the game plan. To me he just told me to go out there and try to attacking the opposition, be dangerous and be myself.” With Manchester City beating Ipswich Town 3-2 on Saturday, maintaining their perfect start of seven wins from seven games, Arenal could have ended the weekend in third place, with Brighton second on goal difference after the Seagulls trounced Crystal Palace 5-0 earlier on Sunday. But the late intervention of half-time substitute Madueke meant the North London club head into the midweek Uefa Champions League clash with Harry Kane's Bayern Munich one place and three points behind Man City in the domestic standings. Arsenal's only defeat this season remains last month's 3-0 loss at Brighton ands they have won nine out of 10 matches across all competitions with three of those being 1-0 victories. Forest, meanwhile, remain third from bottom after what was their third successive defeat with Oliver Glasner's team having registered just one point from four home matches without scoring a single goal. “I had already beaten a couple of times on the outside so I thought I would come inside and let rip. Thank god it went in,” added Madueke. “At times last year this game wouldn’t have gone as it did in the end. We have that extra belief and extra mentality now. We are Champions and we can pull it out the bag wherever we go. “The Premier League can shock you, and we had that shock against Brighton. It is up to us to regroup and show why we are Champions. “If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it's absurd so we know that we're going to start some and finish some and for me it's the same mentality every time I just want to create or score. “We have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. Great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench you're ready to have an impact.”

title: Trump defends Russia sanctions waiver as Zelenskyy rift deepens
description: Treasury Secretary Bessent says Ukraine leader should be 'very careful' about Starlink claims
content: US President Donald Trump on Sunday defended a recent decision to waive sanctions on Russian diesel , as relations between Washington and Ukraine soured further. Mr Trump on Friday waived key provisions of a recent package of sanctions against Russia , saying in an executive order that “such a waiver is in the national interests” of the US. The order waived a requirement by him to raise duties on Russian goods imported into the US by up to 500 per cent, and a separate requirement to place tariffs of up to 100 per cent on China, India and other top buyers of Russian energy. The order was signed two days before the law's implementation deadline and came a week after Mr Trump's surprising decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel, a move that drew opposition from Europe and his Republican party. Mr Trump said the decision rested on him refraining from doing "anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table", as a resolution to end the four-and-a-half year war remains out of reach. "Perhaps more importantly, Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way, and will, unless stupid people get in the way," he wrote in a post on Truth Social. Mr Trump also criticised President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Ukrainian drones struck a major oil terminal and other targets in St Petersburg after a so-called energy ceasefire between Kyiv and Moscow collapsed last week. Mr Zelenskyy said Russia has continued attacks on his country's energy infrastructure despite Mr Trump's energy ceasefire announcement last week. The US leader said Mr Zelenskyy is continuing the attacks on Russian diesel refineries "knowing that these attacks are seriously hurting the world diesel markets". He also said Mr Zelenskyy "doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did". Earlier, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration invoked the law's 60-day pause “so we can see what's going on”. “The only thing that has been lifted is the diesel embargo,” he said. As part of the diesel deal , Mr Trump last week said Russia would immediately send 300,000 tonnes of diesel to US and global markets, with another 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”. The move was quickly condemned by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said it would help to support Russia's war machine. The Kremlin on Thursday said Russian diesel had begun to reach global markets after its agreement with Mr Trump. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told ABC the waiver does not hand Russia an “economic lifeline”. He also dismissed the backlash. “They are all wrong,” Mr Wright said. “They don’t understand what President Trump’s doing.” “This is an incentive to Russia that if they can reduce the conflict with Ukraine , they can get an energy ceasefire or reduce the conflict such that they have diesel to export will allow it to flow to world markets. This is a carrot to try to end a war.” The Trump administration is seeking to lower US diesel prices – which have surged past $6 a gallon ($1.59 a litre) in recent weeks – before the country's midterm elections on November 3. “Does it come with some short-term political pain? It does. But that's called leadership. President Trump wants to bring peace to the world and drive energy prices down,” Mr Wright said. But Mr Zelenskyy called the diesel deals “dangerous”, adding it does not have any meaningful influence on US energy prices. He said the Strait of Hormuz's prolonged closure was the driver behind this year's energy price shock. He also told NBC he believed the US government was responsible for a recent slowdown in US-provided Starlink internet. He said he believed the decision to limit the internet speed was “the message from [the] American government”. He said Ukraine was “blocked” from US intelligence “for some period of time, and then it was deblocked by the American side”. The Ukrainian leader said during this time his country did not see Russian attacks. The US has denied it has ordered restrictions on Starlink satellite internet services to Ukraine. “President Zelenskyy should be very careful about making statements like this that aren't true,” Mr Bessent said. He also appeared to dodge the question of whether Ukraine was still a US ally. “President Trump has made it clear that he wants to end this war; that it must stop. And President Zelenskyy presented a false binary this morning that Ukraine must win,” Mr Bessent said. “The war must end, and that will be with some kind of a negotiated settlement. And President Trump is working on that every day.” He also said the US supports Ukraine through providing intelligence, the Starlink service, and allowing Nato to buy US arms and resell them to Ukraine. “We're not providing those to Russia,” he said. When asked a third time if Ukraine is still a US ally, Mr Bessent said: “I'm not the Secretary of State. I'm not the President.”

title: Five gangsters killed in $3 million drugs and weapons raid in Egypt
description: Authorities seize weapons and tablets in move against 'criminal hotbed'
content: Five people were killed in a police raid on “highly dangerous criminal elements” in Egypt in which more than 250kg of drugs were seized, authorities said. Egypt's Interior Ministry said the drugs haul included 42,000 tablets and was worth 155 million Egyptian pounds ($2.9 million). It said the five people killed in the operation had previously been sentenced to prison on charges including murder, attempted murder, drug trafficking, armed robbery and firearms offences. The raid against “criminal hotbeds” took place in three areas and led to several other suspects being arrested, the ministry said. Investigations had revealed groups smuggling drugs, tablets and weapons in several parts of Egypt. The haul also included 76 parts of weapons. Authorities released images of three cars and two motorbikes that appeared to be part of the seizure. Authorities did not identify the drugs that were seized. Egypt, like other Middle East countries, has previously sought to clamp down on the trade in Captagon, a highly addictive methamphetamine. Last month, Egyptian TV presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 other defendants were sentenced to death after being convicted of belonging to an organised criminal group involved in manufacturing and trafficking synthetic drugs. Egypt imposes the death penalty for serious offences including drug trafficking, although executions are subject to further judicial and legal procedures.

title: UAE sends 60 lorries of food and shelter aid to Gaza under Operation Gallant Knight 3
description: Five convoys carrying 789 tonnes of supplies entered Gaza this week as UAE humanitarian efforts continue
content: Five UAE aid convoys carrying 789 tonnes of food and shelter supplies have entered Gaza this week, continuing the country's relief efforts for Palestinians. The convoys, comprising 60 lorries, were dispatched as part of Operation G3, Gallant Knight 3, the UAE's continuing humanitarian initiative aimed at addressing the basic needs of Palestinians in the Gaza Strip. The latest deliveries bring the total number of lorries that have entered Gaza under the operation since its launch to 14,579, collectively transporting 138,030 tonnes of humanitarian aid to the territory. The supplies are intended to address food and shelter shortages among the Palestinian population, supporting the broader humanitarian response and easing the suffering of those affected by the conflict in Gaza. The Operation Gallant Knight 3 team continues to co-ordinate aid shipments through the UAE Humanitarian Aid Logistics Centre in Al Arish, Egypt. The facility manages the full logistics pipeline, including receiving, sorting and preparing supplies before they are transported across the border into Gaza, ensuring a steady flow of assistance reaches those in need.

title: Egypt's Al Azhar calls for mediation committee to end fighting in Arab region
description: Intervention by Sunni Islamic authority comes as hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis intensify
content: Egypt's Al Azhar has called for the “urgent” formation of a mediation committee with representatives from Arab and Islamic countries to help end conflicts across the region. The call by Al Azhar, the world's top Sunni Islam institution, comes as hostilities worsen between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthi militia in a new round of Middle East conflict. In a statement on Sunday, Al Azhar's Grand Imam Dr Ahmed Al Tayeb urged Arab and Muslim leaders “to uphold the spirit of brotherhood and the bonds of religion, blood and language, give precedence to wisdom, and embrace reason and dialogue, while bringing about an immediate and comprehensive halt to all acts of war, fighting, destruction and sabotage that deplete peoples’ resources and claim innocent lives”. He warned that divisions and infighting were weakening the Arab and Muslim world, undermining its security and sovereignty, and depleting its resources and wealth at a time when unity was urgently needed. The 1,000-year-old Al Azhar carries considerable weight among the world's Sunni Muslims, with its current leader, Imam Ahmed Al Tayeb, enjoying wide popularity in the Arab and Islamic worlds. While the call for a mediation committee to end conflicts in the region is a rare foray by the revered institution into politics and diplomacy, it will probably be treated as a largely symbolic gesture. Al Azhar said the proposed committee should bring together wise and sincere figures from across Arab and Islamic countries to defuse escalating crises, bridge differences and resolve disputes. It said the initiative aimed to preserve the strength and sovereignty of Arab countries, protect lives and safeguard the resources and future of their people. The institution also expressed its readiness to provide the committee with all possible support. It expressed confidence that those involved could overcome their differences and turn the page on the past in the interests of peace and stability. Earlier in the day, Egypt 's top security body pledged “all necessary and possible forms of support” to Saudi Arabia . It met hours before parliament was due to vote on authorising President Abdel Fattah El Sisi to help defend the kingdom against attacks by the Houthi rebels. It later emerged that the parliament would reconvene for two further days to discuss the authorisation. On Sunday, six people were injured when a projectile launched by Yemen’s Houthi militia struck a residential site in the Saudi city of Najran, the civil defence said. The incident caused material damage to three houses and three vehicles, the civil defence spokesman said in a statement. The Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down two ballistic missiles fired at Khamis Mushait and three drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province. The Houthis have launched 20 attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport since October 1, coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said on Thursday. Attacks on Saudi airports have killed 19 people and wounded 364, he said. The deadliest, on October 10 in Riyadh, killed 13, including an Egyptian flight attendant.

title: Sheikh Abdullah holds calls with foreign ministers over regional security
description: Saudi Arabia has been attacked 20 times by Yemen's Houthi rebels since start of October
content: Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, held calls with regional foreign ministers on Sunday regarding security and stability. Saudi Arabia had been attacked by the Houthi rebels in Yemen since the beginning of October. The Houthis have launched 20 attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport since October 1. The deadliest, on October 10, killed 13 people and wounded 308. Sheikh Abdullah shared calls on Sunday with Nasser Bourita, Morocco's Minister of Foreign Affairs; Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Foreign Minister; Ayman Safadi, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs for Jordan; Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar; and Badr Al Busaidi, Foreign Minister of Oman, state news agency Wam reported.

title: Leeds v Man United ratings: Justin 6, Calvert-Lewin 8; Fernandes 5, Mbeumo 7
description: Premier League clash at Elland Road ends in 1-1 draw with Red Devils now having won just once in seven matches
content: A second-half finish from Dominic Calvert-Lewin earned Leeds United a well-deserved Premier League point against Manchester United at Elland Road on Sunday The Red Devils, who went into the match under a cloud following defender Lizandro Martinez's public criticism of the club after their Uefa Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid, took the lead in the 35th minute. Attacker Bryan Mbeumo, who should have put his team in front earlier when he sent a header wide of target when completely unmarked, made no mistake when he sild home a first-time finish from Youri Tieleman's perfect ball across the box. But former Everton striker Calvert-Lewin delighted the home crowd by firing home in the 51st minute, securing a point that would move Leeds up to seventh place on 10 points, six places and three points above Michael Carrick's side. For Manchester United, it was a frustrating end to a tough week and they have now gone six games without a win in all competitions, their worst run since the end of the 2019-20 season. They have also just one league win to their name so far. Leeds manager Daniel Farke: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt we should not be losing at half-time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on. “We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right. We were the dominant side but we couldn't capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box. “It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be. It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.” Man United manager Michael Carrick: “It was one of those challenging games. You could feel there was an edge to the game. Maybe if you talk about top quality, maybe it wasn't the top, top quality I think we are capable of playing. In little moments and spells we played some really good football. “It's a tough place to come. With the results we've had we weren't quite flowing but there's enough in there to take from it. I was proud of the boys for the way they went about it in difficult circumstances. A point is a point. It is a step forward for us. “The way that we went about it today gives me a lot of belief in us moving forward that we are a strong group and if we build on that with the quality we have got … we will win football matches.” James Trafford – 7/10: Former Manchester City keeper was beaten twice by Mbeumo efforts in first half – one header sent wide of target when completely free, one sliding finish that found back of net. Quiet game in general and not called upon for any big saves. James Justin – 6/10: Caught out of position then outmuscled by Mbeumo ahead of Cameroonian putting Man United in front. His lone error in solid performance was a costly one. Tarik Muharemovic – 7/10: Slovenian defender earned assist for heading ball to Calvert-Lewin for striker's leveller. Did well against United's expensively assembled attackers with Leeds now having lost just once in seven league games. Nico Elvedi – 7/10: Swiss defender almost grabbed first goal for club with game's first effort on target but saw header in 25th minute saved by Semmens. Helped side secure well-earned point with what was their fourth draw of season. Jayden Bogle – 8/10: A constant outlet down right for Leeds with steady stream or crosses into box and surging runs forward. One weak finish straight at keeper just before break. Gabriel Gudmundsson – 7/10: Rightly booked for naughty late tackle, raking studs down Santos's ankle. Provided plenty of energy down left. Ethan Ampadu – 7/10: Captain should have picked up early yellow card for late challenge on Mbeumo's ankle. Involved in some nice passing exchanges with teammates. Had one locking-of-horns with Fernandes in second half. Was booked in injury-time for blatant foul on Diallo. Ao Tanaka – 7/10: A real nuisance to play against, constantly closing down and snapping at heels of opponents. Hit shot immediately after Mbeumo's goal straight at keeper, volleyed wildly over bar not long after Leeds' leveller. Anton Stach – 6/10: Wasted good counter-attack chance in first half with final ball that was neither cross nor shot and easily dealt with by away defence. Had even better opportunity in 73rd minute but sent poor shot from inside penalty area over, then saw another goal-bound low shot blocked. Noah Okafor – 6/10: Swiss attacker's first attempt on goal was strike from tight angle just after hour mark sent very high and very wide. A few bright moments but not enough in areas that matter, unlike last season when his two goals earned Leeds a historic win at Old Trafford. Dominic Calvert-Lewin – 8/10: Striker had a couple of headers just before and after break that failed to trouble the keeper. Leeds' top-scorer was in right place to control then fire home from close range in 51st minute for fourth goal of season. Led line well again for Yorkshiremen. Lukas Nmecha (on for Okafor, 74') – 7/10: Handful after coming on offering Leeds something different in attack. Sean Longstaff (on for Tanaka, 81') – N/A: One superb block in injury-time. Senne Lammens – 7/10: Saved well from an Elvedi header in the first-half. Went long with almost every goal-kick, which was a change for him. He did OK at Leeds, but Manchester United have yet to keep a clean sheet in seven Premier League games. Leny Yoro – 7/10: Tough day for the Frenchman, but he cleared everything in the air and intercepted on the ground in a frantic opening. He’s playing out of position but playing well. Harry Maguire – 7/10: Up for it in an intense first half, especially against Calvert-Lewin. At the end of the game he was the only one of the four defenders playing in his usual position, which shows the extent of the defensive injuries and the cost of not bringing a left-back in. Lisandro Martinez – 6/10: Started after a controversial week, he stood up to Leeds pressure but looked to be carrying an injury from midway in the first-half. Came off at half-time. Diogo Dalot – 6/10: An attacking right-back playing at left-back, he crossed well just before half-hour mark. Counter-attacked well on 75 minutes, too. One very important challenge as Leeds attacked late on. Carlos Baleba – 7/10: Energetic in a very good first-half from the Cameroonian, where United were up for the fight. They ran more, physically up for it. Andrey Santos – 7/10: Physically strong in challenges – which was needed against Leeds – and did well in first-half. Brought down in a yellow card challenge by Gudmundson. Booked for showing his frustration at the referee in last minute. Youri Tielemans – 7/10: Played higher up with Baleba behind in a big tactical shift and his excellent cross provided assist United’s opener. Creative and worked well with Baleba and Santos. Less effective in second half. Amad Diallo – 6/10: Superb cross on half-hour and one of the best as United broke quickly, but he’s also struggling to beat a man. Lively towards the end but sent one shot miles wide, and was then fouled in a yellow card challenge in injury-time. Bruno Fernandes – 5/10: Playing in advanced position, he was booked in first half for challenge on Muharemovic. Shot wide on 65. He’s the main man and needs to get back to that level since his team haven’t won a game in six across all competitions. Bryan Mbeumo – 7/10: Started lively on the left. Headed wide when unmarked when he should have hit the target. Trundled a shot after a 33 rd minute break, then put his side ahead on 35, sliding in to guide a Tielemans cross in – a fine finish. Caught up in Leeds’ equaliser, but hardly at fault. Noussair Mazraoui (on for Martinez, 46') – 5/10: Gave away a soft corner which led to Leeds equaliser as they flew out of the blocks at the start of the second half. Stopped an injury-time Leeds shot which had beaten Lammens. Mason Mount (on for Beleba, 74') – 6/10: Slotted into central midfield. Skewed one shot from a well worked move. Matheus Cunha (on for Tielemens, 84') – N/A

title: President Sheikh Mohamed meets Saudi Arabia's Minister of Defence
description: Regional security discussed during meeting in Abu Dhabi
content: President Sheikh Mohamed met Prince Khalid bin Salman, the Saudi Minister of Defence, on Sunday. Saudi Arabia has faced attacks by the Houthi rebels in Yemen, who have carried out 20 strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport since October 1. The deadliest attack, on October 10, killed 13 people and wounded 308. Sheikh Mohamed and Prince Khalid exchanged views on regional developments with the aim of contributing to strengthening security and stability and achieving lasting peace in the region, state news agency Wam reported. Sheikh Mans our bin Zayed , Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Presidential Court, also attended the meeting on Sunday, as did Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi and National Security Adviser. They discussed their shared commitment to "further strengthening co-operation and co-ordination across various fields in a manner that serves their mutual interests and benefits their peoples". The meetings affirmed the depth and solidity of the Emirati-Saudi relations, said Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE President, in a post on X. "For our security and destiny are shared, and our partnership is one of the pillars of Gulf stability and prosperity, while the wisdom of the two leaderships and the sincerity of positions in times of adversity provide the most eloquent response to every bet against that," said Dr Gargash.

title: Donald Trump endorses Benjamin Netanyahu for Israeli election
description: US President says he might not have appetite to 'finish the job' in Iran alone if Israeli leader loses power
content: US President Donald Trump on Sunday gave his “complete and total endorsement” to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his re-election campaign. Writing in a post on Truth Social, Mr Trump praised Mr Netanyahu as a “great warrior prime minister, and an even greater partner for peace in combating the Islamic Republic of Iran ”. “This ‌is the kind of Partner that ​the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much,” Mr Trump wrote. The endorsement comes nine days before Israel 's parliamentary election on October 27, which could determine whether Mr Netanyahu remains in power. The vote is the first to be held since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, plunging the region into conflict as Israel responded by going to war in Gaza and Lebanon. In February, Israel joined the US in launching co-ordinated strikes against Iran, killing the supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by lashing out against its regional neighbours, damaging critical infrastructure and halting the flow of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Mr Trump said Iran's anti-Israel and anti-US rhetoric showed the threat the regime posed to the region. He also said the Iranian regime has been “systematically destroyed, both militarily and financially, and unless they change their ways, rapidly, we will soon finish the job”. Mr Netanyahu thanked Mr Trump in a post on X. “Thank you, President Trump, for the tremendous support and work together,” he wrote. "Together we will complete the mission!” The endorsement is seen as a major boost for Mr Netanyahu, who is in a close race to retain his position as the Iran war and conflicts in the West Bank and Gaza test his popularity. Mr Trump said Mr Netanyahu has been “brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself”. “Despite all ‌of that, he has endured and, ⁠in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted ⁠under the pressure – But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today,” Mr Trump wrote, referring to the Prime Minister by his nickname. And with the Iran war set to cross the eight-month mark later this month, Mr Trump suggested he might not have the appetite to “finish the job” alone if Mr Trump loses his re-election bid. “If Israel has the wrong leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Mr Trump wrote. Mr Trump and Mr Netanyahu have had close ties, although the Israeli leader's failure to toe his US counterpart's line on Gaza, Lebanon and Iran has caused friction. The President stopped short of offering an endorsement as recently as Thursday, saying he doesn't “trust anybody” in politics. In June, he called Mr Netanyahu “crazy” during a heated phone call, adding he was “a little bit perturbed” as Israel's fighting with Hezbollah in Lebanon was stalling peace talks with Iran.

title: Outrage over attacks on European diplomats and US journalist in West Bank
description: Concern is growing over violence in Israeli-occupied territory, where European diplomats were assaulted on Saturday
content: Anger was growing on Sunday at Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank after European diplomats and an American journalist were caught up in the unrest. Visitors from France, Belgium and Poland were among those targeted by masked settlers near the village of Taybeh on Saturday. It came a day after Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine suffered serious injuries when she was attacked by Israeli settlers. The EU on Sunday demanded “effective measures” from Israel to stop the unrest. Poland said the attack in Taybeh, a Christian village, was evidence of what Palestinians in the West Bank face on a daily basis. “The attack should be met with a firm response from the Israeli authorities,” the Polish Foreign Ministry said. US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee demanded arrests and the prosecution of those responsible after the attack on the journalist. “Attacking a female photographer is a despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards,” Mr Huckabee said in a post on X early on Sunday. “Dishonourable act of senseless violence.” The US envoy said Ms Levine had been clearly identified as a journalist and was unarmed. He called for those involved to spend years in prison and demanded prosecution “to the fullest extent of the law”. The Washington Post said Ms Levine was attacked when “dozens of masked settlers” set fire to shrubs and threw rocks in a “co-ordinated assault” on Palestinian olive harvesters. “She was knocked to the ground, kicked repeatedly and stripped of her cameras and phone,” the paper said. Ms Levine was later taken to hospital in Ramallah. Photos showed her lying on a trolley with a wound dressing on the left leg and a gash on her right knee, among other injuries. On Sunday, the Post welcomed the support of the US ambassador. “We appreciate the support we’ve gotten today for our photographer, Heidi Levine, after the brutal and unwarranted attack on her. We reiterate the call for action from the government. Press freedoms are a cornerstone for democracies,” editor Matt Murray wrote on X. The attack comes amid renewed international concern over Israeli settler violence in the West Bank, after European diplomats and a French mayor were assaulted by masked people in a separate incident on Saturday. Belgium criticised the attack on its consul general and the other diplomats and urged Israel to bring those responsible to justice. Poland’s Foreign Ministry said preliminary evidence indicated Israeli settlers were responsible for the assault. Polish diplomats travelling in the convoy were unharmed, the ministry said. “We expect the Israeli authorities to provide urgent and detailed explanations, identify those responsible and ensure that they are held accountable,” it added. “We also expect effective measures to be taken to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.” French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the mayor of a French town had also been assaulted by what he described as “extremist settlers” during Saturday’s incident. He called on Israeli authorities to stop the violence. Israeli President Isaac Herzog called Ms Levine to apologise for the attack and urged an investigation. The Israeli military described the violence as intolerable and said the incidents would be investigated. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said the circumstances remained unclear and more evidence was needed before responsibility could be established. It also noted that the diplomats’ visit had not been co-ordinated with Israeli security officials. Britain, France, Canada and other countries announced sanctions focused on Israeli settlements last month, while the US said it would not join those measures.

title: GCC urges Russia to press Iran to halt attacks as Lavrov proposes Gulf security framework
description: Russian Foreign Minister describes ties with Gulf as priority for Moscow
content: The Gulf Co-operation Council has urged Russia to use its position on the UN Security Council to press Iran to halt attacks on Gulf states, at a meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Bahrain. Speaking at a Gulf-Russia foreign ministers' meeting in Manama on Sunday, GCC Secretary General Jasem Al Budaiwi said member states faced unprecedented attacks as well as risks to shipping and energy supplies. The GCC called on Moscow to “play an active role in pressing Tehran” to comply with UN resolutions, cease its attacks and engage in “serious dialogue” with Gulf states. Mr Lavrov said Russia supports diplomatic efforts to prevent a return to full-scale war as he presented an updated Russian concept for collective security in the Gulf. On Ukraine , where Russia has waged war for almost five years, Mr Al Budaiwi said the bloc continues to support dialogue and diplomacy aimed at a peaceful, comprehensive political settlement. He said Iranian attacks on GCC states since February 28, when the US and Israel began their war against Iran, had involved more than 7,000 ballistic missiles and drones, striking airports, ports, power stations, water desalination plants and oil and gas facilities. Mr Al Budaiwi also condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia , singling out the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which killed 12 people and injured more than 300. He reaffirmed the GCC’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia, calling on the international community to adopt a firm stance against attacks on the kingdom. Mr Al Budaiwi said Iran’s disruption of maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and threats to shipping in the Red Sea and Bab Al Mandeb strait posed risks to global energy and food security and international supply chains. He called for maritime traffic through Hormuz to return to its status before February 28. The proposal envisages direct dialogue among the Gulf’s coastal states and neighbouring countries, including Iraq and Jordan, with possible support from the Arab League, the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation and permanent members of the UN Security Council. Mr Lavrov said the Gulf states themselves should have the decisive voice in determining the region’s security arrangements. “Our concept is specifically designed to foster conditions for direct dialogue among the Gulf’s coastal states and their neighbours, such as Iraq and Jordan,” he said. He also described ties with GCC states as a priority of Russia's foreign policy, noting that trade between Russia and the bloc’s member states rose by 45 per cent in 2025. He said the crisis in the region had been triggered by an “unprovoked act of aggression” by the US and Israel against Iran. The meeting, chaired by Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, also addressed the Palestinian cause, Syria and the Russia-Ukraine war. Mr Al Budaiwi reiterated the GCC’s support for an independent Palestinian state along the borders of 1967, with East Jerusalem as its capital. He called for the consolidation of the Gaza ceasefire and the enactment of its second phase, securing a full Israeli withdrawal and ensuring unhindered humanitarian aid. On Syria, he reaffirmed the GCC’s support for the country’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. The ministers also discussed expanding co-operation in trade, energy, education, health, agriculture and other sectors under the GCC-Russia Joint Action Plan for 2023-2028.

title: Abu Dhabi Police confiscate more than 9,000 e-scooters in last 10 months
description: Police warn of dangers of unsafe use of e-scooters in unauthorised areas
content: Police in Abu Dhabi have seized 9,237 e-scooters in the past 10 months across the emirate. The e-scooters were confiscated as part of a crackdown on breaches of the rules that govern their use on public roads, between vehicles, and in areas where they are forbidden. Police posted on Facebook that they had clamped down on “electric scooters violating traffic rules and regulations during 2026, as a result of their use on public roads, between vehicles, and on paths not designated for them, posing a danger to the safety of their users and road users”. “One of the most dangerous behaviours among electric scooter drivers is driving without paying attention to traffic, not wearing a helmet, and not wearing safety gear, which increases the likelihood of traffic accidents that may result in serious injuries or deaths,” police said on Sunday. Earlier this year, The National reported that data from the Ministry of Interior revealed a 97 per cent increase in major e-scooter accidents in 2025 compared with the previous year – a jump from 61 to 120. Alongside these figures, Al Wathba Insurance and RoadSafetyUAE conducted an e-scooter perception study and found that 93 per cent of UAE residents witness e-scooter riders behaving unsafely or recklessly, while 90 per cent personally feel unsafe because of the way e-scooters are used. title: Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial: Artists, locations, dates and what to know
description: Exhibition brings together 21 artists and collectives from the UAE and abroad
content: Art installations are set to take over public spaces across Abu Dhabi and Al Ain as the second Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial returns this month. Organised by the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi, the exhibition brings together 21 artists and collectives from the UAE and abroad, with monumental, interactive and multi-sensory works exploring home, collective memory and community. From the participating artists to where to find their work, here is what to know. The biennial opens in Al Ain on October 23, followed by Abu Dhabi on November 15. The exhibition runs across both cities until February 15, 2027. In Abu Dhabi, installations will be displayed at Mina Zayed (MiZa) , Souq Al Mina, Hidd Al Saadiyat and Saadiyat Cultural District , where works will occupy the park between Zayed National Museum and Louvre Abu Dhabi . The programme will also extend to selected locations across Al Ain, although specific sites have yet to be announced. Details of which artworks will appear at each location have also not been released. The line-up includes UAE artists Khalid Al Banna, Roudhah Al Mazrouei and Shama Al Hamed, alongside international names such as Ibrahim Mahama, Laure Prouvost, Yinka Shonibare and Akram Zaatari. Also participating are Asuncion Molinos Gordo, blaxTARLINES, Celeste Boursier-Mougenot, Elena del Rivero, Ivan Argote, Jean-Marie Appriou, Kapwani Kiwanga and Marinella Senatore. Completing the roster are M'barek Bouhchichi, Mercedes Azpilicueta, Nari Ward, Reena Saini Kallat, Serge Attukwei Clottey and Vica Pacheco. Artistic director Elvira Dyangani Ose leads the art event under the theme Home: A Glossary for a Communal Sense of Place. The exhibition approaches home as an evolving, shared human experience, exploring how people’s relationships with places are shaped by community, memory and everyday encounters. Artists will respond to the settings in which their works appear, drawing on research and engaging with surrounding communities. The biennial will bring contemporary art into public and cultural spaces, with installations exploring urban landscapes, material culture and civic participation. Visitors can expect a mix of large-scale, interactive and multisensory works designed to encourage engagement with both the art and its surroundings. Details of individual installations, visiting hours, ticketing and accompanying events are still to be announced.

title: Egypt pledges support for Saudi Arabia as Houthis warn Cairo against military intervention
description: Parliament set to vote on authorising President El Sisi to help defend  kingdom, as Sanaa's Houthi-run legislature says involvement could threaten national security
content: Egypt 's top security body on Sunday pledged “all necessary and possible forms of support” to Saudi Arabia . The National Defence Council, chaired by President Abdel Fatteh El Sisi at Al Ittihadiya Palace in Cairo, said Saudi Arabia's security was inextricably linked to Egypt's own and to wider Arab national security. The support would help the kingdom defend its security and territory, as well as the Islamic holy sites, the presidency said. It cited the “escalating unacceptable attacks” on the kingdom and called for more diplomacy to calm the region. The statement did not mention troops. But Mostafa Bakry, an MP and TV host close to the state, said on X that the council had approved sending forces to Saudi Arabia on “a defensive mission”. The Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, Speaker of Parliament Hisham Badawy, Defence Minister Lt Gen Ashraf Zaher and intelligence chiefs attended. Parliament had been due to vote after the council meeting on authorising President El Sisi to help defend the kingdom against attacks by the Houthi rebels in Yemen, but the session has been extended by two days. Under Article 152 of Egypt's constitution, the President cannot declare war or send the army on a combat mission abroad without consulting the council. He also needs the approval of two-thirds of MPs. Parliament's rules require the vote to take place in an urgent closed session. The legislature has a majority of pro-Sisi legislators who are widely expected to approve the request, as they have backed previous policies championed by the President. Mr El Sisi made the request on Saturday. “It is inconceivable that we would allow Saudi Arabia, its security or stability to be harmed,” he said. Egypt would act only if Riyadh asked, he said in a speech at the Military Academy. “We do not want to fight or attack anyone. We will only defend Saudi Arabia,” he added. The move drew a swift warning from Sanaa. Yahya Al Raei, speaker of the Houthi-run parliament there, wrote to Mr Badawi on Saturday. The Houthi-controlled body is not recognised internationally. “We categorically reject Egypt being dragged” into “the same trench as the takfiri forces and the Israeli occupation entity,” he wrote. Such a path “would pose a grave danger to its national security,” he said, urging Cairo to take a “courageous stance”. He accused Riyadh of waging “aggression and siege” against Yemen for more than 12 years. He said it had walked away from a peace road map and ended a period of calm by striking Sanaa airport. The letter was carried by the Houthis' Al Masirah TV. Early on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down two ballistic missiles fired at Khamis Mushait and three drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province. The Houthis have launched 20 attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport since October 1, coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said on Thursday. Attacks on Saudi airports have killed 19 people and wounded 364, he said. The deadliest, on October 10 in Riyadh, killed 13, including an Egyptian flight attendant. The coalition also said it intercepted a missile aimed at Madinah on Thursday. The Houthis denied firing it. The UN Security Council condemned the attacks as “escalatory” that same day and backed the kingdom's right to self-defence. Cairo's move also comes as a new alliance takes shape around Riyadh. Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7 . The pact provides that an attack on one member is treated as an attack on all. Riyadh activated it on October 5, and Pakistan said the partners would send the “agreed military forces” to the kingdom. While Egypt is not yet a member, Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said last week that joining was “under serious consideration”. Cairo has long been wary of binding pacts. Joining one could strain its ties with Iran and its peace treaty with Israel, while potentially drawing Egypt into a war with the Houthis. Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping have already caused heavy losses in Suez Canal revenue . Over the past week, many commentators have cited Egypt's costly intervention in Yemen in the 1960s as a reason not to rush into such an agreement. Instead, Cairo has taken smaller steps. On August 13, it joined a Saudi-led naval coalition set up after the Houthis declared a blockade on Saudi shipping. Egypt joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015. In July 2020, MPs voted unanimously in a closed session to allow combat missions abroad as fighting in Libya neared Egypt's western border. Approval of the request would not, in itself, mean that troops would be deployed.

title: UAE signs agreement to hold 2029 World Bank and IMF meetings in Abu Dhabi
description: Selection of UAE capital is mark of growing global confidence in country’s economy
content: The UAE has formally signed the agreement to host the 2029 annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Abu Dhabi. The deal, signed at the conclusion of the IMF and the World Bank 2026 annual meetings in Thailand, is a mark of growing international confidence in the UAE’s economic and financial ecosystem, the UAE Ministry of Finance said in a statement on Sunday. The formal pact to host the meetings also reinforces the status of the UAE – the Arab world’s second-largest economy – as a global financial hub that is helping to shape the stability and future of the global economic system. Mohamed bin Hadi Al Hussaini, Minister of State for Financial Affairs, and Khaled Balama, governor of the Central Bank of the UAE, signed the agreement in the Thai capital, Bangkok, with the World Bank president Ajay Banga and the IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva. “The signing of the agreement marks a significant milestone, reflecting … confidence in the UAE’s readiness, the efficiency of its infrastructure and financial system, and its ability to host major international events of strategic importance,” Mr Al Hussaini said. The hosting of the event in the UAE will provide global financial leaders and decision-makers with a platform to explore how to advance the financial and monetary stability agenda as well as build development finance, the minister added. The UAE’s selection to host the event builds on the country’s track record in hosting major economic events. Scheduled to be held in October 2029, the summit will return to the Emirates for the first time in more than a quarter of a century. Dubai hosted the meetings in 2003. Participation in the annual meetings has continued to grow over the years, with more than 10,000 in-person and virtual attendees welcomed at each event. Country group meetings, civil society forums and press conferences with the World Bank president and IMF managing director are also held. They are closely watched by financial experts and policymakers from around the world. The World Bank-IMF annual meetings are traditionally held at their headquarters in Washington DC, and every third year a member country is selected to host them. London was the first city outside the US to host the meetings in 1947, while the UAE and Turkey remain the only countries in the Middle East to have hosted them. “The UAE has built institutions and infrastructure with a spirit of bold ambition and partnership, cementing its role as a global hub for economic dialogue,” Mr Banga of the World Bank Group, said. “Abu Dhabi is a fitting host for the annual meetings where our focus is on development impact, and delivering jobs, growth, and financing at scale.” The meetings usually bring together finance ministers, central bank governors, policymakers and economic experts, private sector representatives, civil society, media, and academics from more than 190 countries to examine the challenges and opportunities facing the global economy. The IMF and World Bank also release their outlook for growth and financial stability, and discuss future policy direction that supports inclusive and sustainable development. “The UAE has become an important hub for ideas, finance, innovation and international co-operation,” Ms Georgieva said. The 2029 meeting in Abu Dhabi will provide an opportunity to discuss the “challenges and opportunities ahead and help shape a better future”, the IMF managing director added.

title: Iran names new defence minister as he warns US over ‘Mother of All Bombs’
description: Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi already under US and UN sanctions over Iran’s missile programme
content: Iran’s parliament has approved Mehrdad Ketabchi as Defence Minister, the government said. Mr Ketabchi gave Washington a warning that Tehran was prepared to respond to a possible US attack involving the “Mother of All Bombs”. He received 237 votes in favour and 15 against, with no abstentions, following a review of his credentials and proposed programme, said a government statement posted on X. President Masoud Pezeshkian nominated Mr Ketabchi on October 5 and submitted his name to parliament for a vote of confidence. He replaces Brig Gen Aziz Nasirzadeh, who was killed in a US-Israeli air strike at the start of the war in February. Mr Pezeshkian subsequently appointed Brig Gen Majid Ebn Al Reza as caretaker defence minister. Mr Ketabchi is a veteran defence industry official who has headed Iran’s Aerospace Industries Organisation and Defence Industries Organisation, overseeing sectors involved in missile technology and weapons production. The US and UN have imposed sanctions against Mr Ketabchi over his alleged involvement in Iran’s ballistic missile programme. The UN listed him in 2007 in connection with the Shahid Bagheri Industrial Group, which develops and produces solid-propellant ballistic missiles. In presenting his plans to parliament, Mr Ketabchi pledged to restructure the ministry, accelerate defence technology development and upgrade Iran’s military capabilities. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of an online parliamentary session on Sunday, he said Iran had taken the necessary measures to counter a possible US attack involving the “Mother of All Bombs”, the semi-official Isna news agency reported. “We have taken the necessary measures for this scenario, and we are at ease. We proceed with our work with full confidence,” he was quoted as saying. Addressing US President Donald Trump , Mr Ketabchi said Washington should focus on ensuring the safe withdrawal of its forces from the region. “He ought to be thinking about how to get his forces out of our region safely. If he drops a single bomb, he will have to consider how many of his troops will end up being carried out of the region in a horizontal position,” he said, in an apparent reference to US military casualties. He said the prospect of retaliation had so far deterred Washington from launching an attack. “Rest assured; it is precisely this fact that has deterred the US from taking such an action thus far,” he said. “Of course, should they move from mere rhetoric to actual threats, they will certainly see the consequences.” CNN reported this week that the US had developed strike plans that could include using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, also known as the Mother of All Bombs, against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if Mr Trump orders renewed combat operations. The weapon is the largest non-nuclear bomb in the US arsenal. Separately, Iranian Army deputy executive co-ordinator Brig Gen Alireza Sheikh said the military’s equipment had been upgraded and its forces were ready to respond to any threat. Speaking on Sunday in response to threats involving the possible use of the bomb against Iran, he said, “The fathers of bombs are the Iranian people, and they can certainly have a more destructive impact than what the enemy expects on its thoughts, psychology, mindset, and strategies.”

title: Sudan’s humanitarian crisis deepens as millions face displacement and aid funding shortages
description: Armed forces chief is accused of breaking promises and derailing peace initiatives
content: Millions of Sudanese displaced by the country’s war are struggling to rebuild their lives amid worsening humanitarian conditions and a severe shortfall in aid funding, as politicians urge greater international pressure to end the conflict. Mohamed Abdel Hakam, a leader of the Sumoud alliance, which advocates civilian rule in Sudan, described the crisis as one of the world’s largest humanitarian disasters and called for greater attention to the plight of millions seeking safety and a return to normal life. “I believe the catastrophe unfolding in Sudan, which is weighing on millions of Sudanese, is the largest humanitarian disaster in the world at this time,” he told Sky News Arabia. He said the crisis had been described by UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres and other officials of the world body as a “forgotten crisis”, leaving millions struggling to live with dignity amid displacement, harsh conditions in shelters and an uncertain future. “Millions of Sudanese are now living in a state of loss and uncertainty. They want nothing more than to return safely to their homes and places of residence and have normal life restored after enduring immense hardship as a result of this brutal war,” he said. Dr Salah Al Amin, a Sudanese expert in humanitarian affairs, said millions of people had been displaced within Sudan or fled abroad as refugees, many of whom were facing additional hardship because of funding shortages. “Funding has fallen this year compared with previous years, to the point that there is a shortfall of more than 47 per cent in the funding that should reach these refugees,” he told Sky News Arabia. He said international organisations assisting refugees were also struggling financially. “Even Unicef and the UN refugee agency, which is responsible for refugees around the world, are complaining about funding problems, to the extent that many employees who were working to provide services to refugees have been laid off,” he said. The conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces, led by Gen Abdel Fattah Al Burhan , and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has devastated the country of 50 million people and battered its economy. International efforts aimed at ending the war have struggled to secure a lasting ceasefire. The war, now well into its fourth year, has created one of ​the world's worst humanitarian crises, displacing about 14 million people. Mohamed Al Faky, a former civilian member of Sudan’s ruling Sovereignty Council, urged the international community to maintain pressure on army chief Gen Al Burhan to end the war, accusing him of breaking promises and derailing peace initiatives. “This man is, of course, a professional liar and has derailed a number of initiatives,” Mr Al Faky said in an interview with Sky News Arabia. “He had promised regional countries and the United States in September 2024 that he would go to Geneva [for peace talks] but then backed out at the last minute,” he said. “Therefore, the pressure must continue, and the siege must continue. I believe the international community has finally seen through this man’s lies and is now exerting sustained pressure on him.” Mr Al Faky also criticised what he described as attempts by Gen Al Burhan to portray popular support through public appearances, including videos showing him playing cards with soldiers and mingling with crowds. “These are desperate attempts that can only come from a desperate political mind that does not understand what is happening in Sudan or recognise the suffering that Sudanese people are enduring in exile and inside the country,” he said. “It is a mentality that mocks the suffering of Sudanese people and the major issues they face, including displacement, hunger, and the loss of their land, property and memories.” Mr Al Faky said the videos had become a source of ridicule in Sudanese media and on social media. He challenged the army chief to demonstrate his support by organising a public rally rather than appearing unannounced at markets and celebrations. “If you have popular support, organise an event in your own name and deliver a speech in one of the major squares, whether Freedom Square or Martyrs’ Square. Invite people,” Mr Al Faky said. “But showing up uninvited at markets and celebrations is not a measure of popular support. These people are simply walking along the streets and visiting markets to meet their daily needs, only for this man to suddenly confront them.” Mr Al Faky also claimed that Gen Al Burhan’s reported ambition to become president lacked support within the military establishment and the Islamic Movement. He said the three remaining military members of the Sovereignty Council – Shams Al Din Kabbashi, Yasser Al Atta and Ibrahim Jaber – opposed the idea, as did the Islamic Movement, which he said believed Gen Al Burhan could not assume the presidency without an agreement. “No such agreement has been reached,” Mr Al Faky said.

title: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid launches latest Arab Hope Makers initiative with Dh1 million prize
description: Philanthropists across the Arab world can apply for award
content: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai , has launched the seventh edition of the Arab Hope Makers initiative, celebrating philanthropists across the region who dedicate their efforts to improving communities. The initiative, the largest of its kind in the Arab world, recognises individuals, volunteer groups and non-profit organisations driving change through charitable, social and humanitarian work. Applications are open at arabhopemakers.com, with the winner receiving a prize of Dh1 million ($272,000). "Nurturing hope is a triumph for life itself," said Sheikh Mohammed . "The hope we cultivate today will yield prosperity, peace and safety in people's lives tomorrow." The UAE will "always remain a nation of good deeds and optimism, inspiring positive change across the region and the world", said Sheikh Mohammed. Mohammed Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs and Secretary General of Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives, said the initiative has contributed significantly to humanitarian action and volunteering across the Arab world since its launch in 2017. More than 335,000 participants have taken part in six iterations. "The initiative shines a light on the great aspects of our Arab societies and the potential and talents dedicated to sincerely improving people's lives," Mr Al Gergawi said. The most recent edition crowned Fouzia Mahmoudi from Morocco as the 2025 Arab Hope Maker after her foundation, Operation Smile, performed more than 19,000 surgeries on children born with cleft lips and palates. The two other finalists, Hend Alhajri from Kuwait and Abderrahmane Rais from Morocco, were also awarded Dh1 million each, bringing the total prize pool for the sixth edition to Dh3 million ($817,000). Ms Alhajri founded Fatima House, a refuge for orphaned children in Tanzania, while Mr Rais launched a humanitarian initiative supporting widows and women in need across Morocco. Operating under MBRGI, the initiative is open to applicants from across the Arab world and globally whose projects address community development, alleviate suffering or tackle local challenges on a voluntary, non-profit basis.

title: Three jailed over luxury watch robbery at knifepoint in London's Mayfair
description: Richard Mille watch worth £140,000 was seized in street attack
content: Three men who carried out a violent street robbery in one of London’s upmarket districts have been sentenced to prison. The trio held up a man at knifepoint to steal a £140,000 Richard Mille watch in Berkeley Square, Mayfair, one of the most upscale areas of the UK capital. It happened shortly before midnight on January 28 this year. Police in London have been trying to crack down on watch and phone robberies that have been described by politicians as an epidemic. The men have now been sentenced to a combined 14 years and nine months’ imprisonment after the Metropolitan Police investigation. CCTV videos showed the men arriving in a vehicle before committing the robbery. Footage then showed the group fleeing the scene and boarding a train to Slough, west of London, where they lived. Police were able to trace the vehicle, which led them to identify a suspect, Younes Djoudi, 34. He was arrested after a brief foot chase the day after the attack. Data from his phone led police to the other two suspects a week later. Djoudi was sentenced to five years and nine months’ in prison. Ali Eldahouzze, 22, was sentenced to three years and six months in prison, while Abdel El Habchi, 30, was given three years and six months. All three men later pleaded guilty to robbery at the Westminster Magistrates' Court. The Met says its campaign against violent crime is working and robberies in London have fallen by 12.8 per cent. This month, a man pleaded guilty to wounding with intent, attempted robbery and possession of a knife after an alleged attack on a Saudi visitor in Mayfair, which prompted the Saudi embassy to warn its citizens to guard their property and be vigilant when out in London . In March, two men who robbed a man of his Patek Philippe watch while he was out with his pregnant wife in Mayfair were jailed .

title: Al Ain stunned by Shabab Al Ahli as historic 38-game unbeaten run comes to an end
description: Coach Ivic critical of 'abnormal' defending after UAE champions lose a Pro League match for first time since March 2025
content: Vladimir Ivic said he was proud of Al Ain's record UAE Pro League 38-game unbeaten run but was highly critical of his side's defending after a 2-0 loss to title rivals Shabab Al Ahli saw them beaten for the first time in 19 months. Al Ain had not tasted a league defeat since a 3-2 loss to Dibba on March 29, 2025, some 567 days before Saturday's setback. In that time, Ivic had led the team through an unbeaten title-winning season . It was also the first time in 32 matches that Al Ain had failed to score. They sit fourth in the table as part of a four-way tie for the lead, although Al Jazira can go three points clear with victory at Kalba on Sunday. Shabab Al Ahli moved up to second after goals from in-form striker Sardar Azmoun and Kauan Santos gave them victory in Dubai. Ivic said his Al Ain side had been poor at both ends of the pitch but urged his players to get the defeat out of their systems quickly. They have an immediate opportunity to avenge the result when they face Shabab Al Ahli again in the last 16 of the President's Cup on Thursday. “It was a very strange match, but I congratulate Shabab Al Ahli on the win,” said Ivic. “They took their chances and scored two goals from four opportunities, while we created around 10 chances and failed to score a single goal. That was the difference between the two teams. “I don't remember us making these kinds of mistakes since I arrived at Al Ain. What happened was abnormal, especially the way we conceded the two goals. I cannot explain it before watching the match again. “For the first goal, a Shabab Al Ahli player got past two of our defenders easily, as if they were statues standing still on the pitch, before going through on goal and scoring. The second goal came from similar mistakes. These are things that cannot happen. “I am the team's coach and I take responsibility for the defeat. I do not blame the players, but we must return to the basics and correct our mistakes. Even the best teams in the world lose, and I am proud of what our players have delivered over the past period. “We must forget this match quickly because we will face Shabab Al Ahli again in four days, and our objective is to return to winning ways.” It was the biggest result so far for Andre Jardine, the Shabab Al Ahli manager, who took over from Paulo Sousa in the summer. He said his players had carried out his game plan to a tee but warned that they would need to maintain their level when they meet Al Ain again in the cup. “For us, beating Al Ain is worth six points because we are talking about a direct clash against a strong rival for the title,” he said. “Almost everything we planned before the match worked, but if I want to speak frankly, taking our chances was the decisive factor in achieving the victory. “Of course, the defeat will give Al Ain extra motivation to come back and win the next match, but our victory today will also give our players a big morale boost. We will face a new match between two teams that have the enthusiasm and desire to win.”

title: Saudi Arabia executes five over terrorism-related offences
description: They joined a foreign terrorist organisation and attacked security personnel, Interior Ministry says
content: Saudi Arabia has executed five men over terrorism-related offences. The executions were carried out in the Eastern Province on Saturday, the Interior Ministry was quoted by the Saudi Press Agency as saying. It named the five citizens as Mohammed Al Zaher, Ali Al Sheikh, Hassan Al Faraj, Reda Al Abu Abdullah and Ali Al Rabih. The ministry said they joined a foreign terrorist organisation, repeatedly opened fire on security personnel and vehicles with intent to kill, possessed weapons and live ammunition, and provided financial and other support for attacks inside the kingdom. A court found them guilty and sentenced them to death under tazir, a discretionary form of punishment that Saudi judges can impose under Islamic law for offences not carrying fixed penalties. The ministry said the sentences were upheld by the Supreme Court on appeal and a royal order was issued for them to be carried out. The executions reflected the government’s commitment to security, justice and the enforcement of Islamic law against those who threaten public safety, it added.

title: Daniel Dubois' five options after Fabio Wardley knockout - from Filip Hrgovic to Tyson Fury
description: British heavyweight eyes up unification bouts after second-round KO in London
content: Daniel Dubois ​retained his WBO heavyweight ​belt with a one-sided and devastating second-round stoppage of ⁠fellow Briton Fabio Wardley in their world title rematch on Saturday. The 29-year-old ⁠champion made a storming start at London's O2 Arena and ​Wardley's legs went from under him for a count within 17 seconds of the opening bell as Dubois floored him ⁠with a straight right. Wardley, 31, beat the count and could have been stopped at the end of the first round when he took a further brutal pounding on the ropes but was saved by the bell. There was no escape from the onslaught of ⁠blows in the second with Dubois picking up where he left off and Wardley taking punch after punch ​until the ⁠towel was thrown in and referee Steve ‌Gray brought the fight to a close. "Fabio is a great warrior, coming in for a second time, but it ​was my time and my era," said Dubois, never a man for long speeches. "I had my intentions, bad intentions, from the beginning. "Our back was against the wall the first time, this time we just had to go out there and show that we mean business and that's what we did tonight." Dubois dealt Wardley his first defeat as a professional when he came back from two knockdowns, the first after 16 seconds, to take the title in the 11th round of a thunderous and bloody clash in Manchester last May. Wardley, promoted to WBO champion last November after Ukraine's Oleksandr Usyk vacated the title, was acclaimed for his courage and refusal to give in first time around but on Saturday he looked a shell of the man seen in Manchester. He now has a 20-2-1 record with Dubois on 24 wins with three defeats. "I've always thrown myself in with the best competitors out there, ​the toughest, the biggest, hardest, meanest guys around. There's no shame in testing yourself ‌against the best," he said. "Daniel's a testament to ⁠coming up short and coming again, I'll be looking ​to do the exact same thing. "Boxing is a game of fine margins. It can be done ​and over in a ‌round or two or it can go into a big old war like it was last time." Here are five options for his Dubois's next opponent: The Croatian holds the IBF title after his win over Moses Itauma. In theory he must first defend it against Frank Sanchez, his mandatory challenger. Hrgovic lost to Dubois in 2024, but his appetite for a rematch was clear as he climbed into the ring at the O2 Arena on Saturday night. Kabayel holds the WBC title and is set to defend against Nelson Hysa next month. A unification against the Kurdish-German champion would make a lot of sense. Fury and Joshua will finally fight in December, with the WBA title reported to be on the line. Whether the winner would have the hunger to fight again and face Dubois is another question. Should the Cuban beat Hrgovic then there's a strong chance he'd be lined up for Dubois. The Ukrainian has beaten Dubois twice, but why not have another crack at the number one guy in the division?

title: Dubai's economy reaches Dh473 billion in first half of 2026 as key sectors expand
description: Economy shrinks 2.3% despite growth in finance and healthcare
content: Dubai's economy reached Dh473 billion in the first half of 2026, down 2.3 per cent from a year earlier, as growth in financial services, healthcare and construction helped offset weakness in other sectors. The emirate's real gross domestic product declined from Dh484 billion in the same period last year, according to figures released on Sunday by the Dubai Data and Statistics Establishment at Digital Dubai. The slowdown came as the Iran war, which began on February 28, disrupted regional travel and trade, weighing on Dubai's tourism and transport sectors and dampening economic activity during the first half of the year. GDP at current prices, however, increased by 0.2 per cent to Dh505 billion, reflecting growth across several key sectors. Helal Almarri, director general of the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism, said the figures demonstrated the emirate's ability to navigate global uncertainty. "Dubai’s H1 2026 GDP performance reflects the strength and adaptability of an economy built to navigate periods of significant global uncertainty," he said. The first-half numbers, however, mark a reversal from the 2.4 per cent annual growth recorded in the first quarter , when Dubai's economy reached Dh232 billion despite regional economic challenges.
