Behind the JAC E30X’s slightly cartoonish appearance lurks a capable and well-built car for its modest asking price. Although tiny in overall dimensions, the E30X's wheel-at-each-corner stance endows it with a 2,620 mm wheelbase, making it surprisingly spacious inside. With a single electric motor sending 95hp or 136hp (depending on trim level) to the front wheels, the JAC is no rocket ship, but it nevertheless feels decently zippy around town. Even the base model gets automatic LED headlights, retracting flush door handles, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, faux-leather trim, cruise control and a 12.8-inch infotainment screen. With a starting price under Dh90,000, the Polestar 2 seems an unbelievable value for money. There is a catch, though, as the cars on offer for this price are part of the dealership’s 2024 inventory. However, they still have zero kilometres on the odometer and are still considered new. With the Polestar’s 272hp electric motor delivering a brisk 0-100kph split of 6.4 seconds and a touring range of 546km, there isn't anything equivalent at this price. Top it off with Swedish (such as Volvo) levels of build quality and safety, and the Polestar 2 seems a compelling buy – even if you’re getting a 2024 model-year car. The perky-looking Smart #3 is a fusion of East and West, as the brand is German but the car itself is built in China. In its base form, the five-door compact SUV is equipped with a 66kWh battery and a single electric motor that sends a beefy 268hp and 384Nm to the front wheels. It’s a sprightly performer, sprinting from standstill to 100kph in 5.8 seconds, while touring range is also respectable at 430km (claimed). Standard features include a panoramic sunroof, a 12.8-inch central display and a 10-inch head-up display. The safety kit includes adaptive cruise control, automatic parking assist, lane-keeping assist, automatic emergency braking and a 360-degree camera. Billed as a Tesla Model Y rival, the GAC Aion V offers ample interior space and a generous feature list at a budget price. Propulsion for the Aion V is provided by a single e-motor that produces 204hp and 240Nm, channelled through the front wheels. GAC claims the Aion V, equipped with a 75.26kWh battery, can cover up to 510km on a full charge, based on the European WLTP test cycle. There’s also a lengthy list of standard features, such as a 14.6-inch touchscreen with Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, a nine-speaker sound system, navigation, a 9.8-inch digital instrument cluster, dual-zone climate control, a hands-free tailgate and 19-inch alloy wheels. The Volvo EX30 is another value-packed offering as it provides the Swedish marque’s customary levels of build quality and safety at a wallet-friendly price. The stubby SUV has a distinctive profile, and that’s not a bad thing in a sea of vehicles that seem virtual clones of each other. In base trim, a single electric motor sends 272hp and 343Nm to the rear wheels, delivering 0-100kph split in 5.7 seconds and a maximum touring range of 337km (claimed). Included at no extra cost are Harman Kardon premium audio, dual-zone climate-control air-conditioning, 19-inch alloys, reversing camera, front and rear parking sensors, and front, side andcurtain airbags. The ultra-futuristic-looking EV3 embodies Kia’s latest design language, and everything under the skin is similarly cutting-edge. The EV3’s minimalistic interior is dominated by a pair of 12.3-inch screens – one for the instrument cluster and the other for the infotainment system. Conveniences include a powered tailgate, sliding-table centre console, bottle holders in all four doors and a 25-litre "frunk" (front trunk) that supplements the 460-litre rear load bay. Safety is enhanced via a surround-view monitor, Smart Cruise Control (SCC), Reverse Parking Collision-avoidance Assist (PCA-R), Forward Collision-avoidance Assist 2 (FCA 2) and Remote Smart Parking Assist (RSPA). Hyundai’s stylish Ioniq 5 was launched five years ago, but it still looks just as good as it did back in 2021. With an expansive three-metre wheelbase, the Ioniq 5 offers acres of sprawling space inside, while the relatively high roofline makes for generous headroom and good visibility in all directions. Power output ranges from 170hp in single-motor entry variants to 305hp in the dual-motor flagship, with the latter accelerating from 0-100kph in only 5.2 seconds. Hyundai says the Ioniq 5, underpinned by an 800-volt architecture, can charge from 10 to 80 per cent in just 18 minutes with a 350kW fast charger. Quality cars at an affordable price are the key to BYD’s meteoric success (it now sells more EVs globally than Tesla), and the Sealion 7 is a case in point. The largeish coupe-mimicking SUV has great fit and finish inside and out and the extensive standard kit list includes a panoramic sunroof, 19-inch alloys, 15.6-inch infotainment screen, 12-speaker audio, LED headlights with cornering function and plenty more. The base model is propelled by a single electric motor that drives the rear wheels, and outputs of 308hp and 380Nm are sufficient to deliver sprightly performance – as evidenced by a 0-100kph dash in 6.7 seconds. Tesla has become ubiquitous in the electric vehicle market over the past decade as the Model 3 and Model Y are popular models in the UAE. The swoopy Model Y SUV offers greater space and utility than its Model 3 sibling, and a midlife refresh last year resolved the slightly awkward styling of the 2020 original. The Model Y’s cabin is ultra-minimalist, and the instrument cluster has been removed, as all information is now displayed on the central infotainment screen. Even the single-motor entry model is rapid (0-100kph in 5.6 seconds) and it has an impressive range (661km claimed). Xpeng debuted in the UAE only two years ago, but the Chinese brand has already carved a foothold, with stylish offerings at keen prices serving as its foundation. With a clean, elegantly sculpted profile, the medium-large G9 SUV manages to avoid the frumpiness that distinguishes many vehicles of this ilk. Inside, there's a 10.25-inch digital instrument panel, plus dual 15-inch high-definition displays – one for infotainment and one for the passenger – while soft-touch materials throughout the cabin make for a premium ambience. Xpeng quotes a 502km range for the base model, while its 800-volt architecture enables super-fast charging (10 to 80 per cent in just 15 minutes). Audi was one of the EV pioneers in the UAE, as the original e-tron SUV was launched locally at the end of 2018. The four-ringed brand has since fleshed out its battery-electric range, with the Q6 Sportback e-tron standing out as one of the marque’s best-value EVs. The entry version kicks off just under Dh250,000, and the price includes a five-year service package, roadside assistance and registration. This price gets you a stylish coupe-like SUV with Audi’s customary quality feel. Powered by a single 252hp electric motor, the Q6 Sportback e-tron offers a claimed 656km touring range and fast-charge capability (10 to 80 per cent in 22 minutes). The latest BMW iX3 is the first embodiment of the Bavarian marque’s "Neue Klasse" design language, and it therefore stands clearly apart from any models that preceded it. While the Neue Klasse platform is optimised for electric powertrains, it can also accommodate petrol engines. The initial iX3 model offered in the UAE is the high-spec dual-motor iX3 50 xDrive that is priced from Dh360,000 ($98,022), including a service package and insurance. One of its trump cards is a new "Heart of Joy" control unit that’s said to deliver class-leading dynamics and handling precision. BMW quotes a maximum touring range of 805km (claimed) and 0-100kph in 4.9 seconds, so the debutant’s stats bode well.

title: Liverpool v Man City ratings: Koumas 7, Wirtz 4; Doku 9, Haaland 8
description: Enzo Maresca's side maintain perfect Premier League start with a 3-0 win at a hostile Anfield
content: Manchester City maintained their perfect start to the Premier League season with a 3-0 demolition of Liverpool at a hostile Anfield on Sunday. Enzo Maresca's side were playing their first match since it was announced City had been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules – which the club are appealing – but turned on the style in the second half on Merseyside. A tight and edgy game opened up in the 62nd minute when Ryan Gravenberch was sent off after picking up a second yellow card. Three minutes later, Erling Haaland opened the scoring with a fine first-time finish. Substitute Jeremy Doku, who was sensational after coming on, curled home a second before Rayan Cherki made it three, with all the goals coming in 13 minutes. It was City's sixth win in six matches in the Premier League, and leaves them three points ahead of Arsenal - who beat Leeds 2-1 on Saturday - at the top of the table. Liverpool are ninth on nine points after falling to their first league defeat of the campaign in what was their joint biggest Premier League loss at Anfield. Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola: “The first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us. “The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us, and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. “We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances. You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It's a loss, and we didn't get anything from the performance, but I liked it a lot." Man City striker Haaland: “Every single person [who is a] part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time. It was tough, it was hard, but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone. “It's always tough to come here; if you look at the record, it's tough. With the Pep [Guardiola and [Jurgen] Klopp era it was tough for both teams; it always has been. “Important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do. “I missed a big chance right before so it was about focusing on getting another chance. The moment came and I took it. Proud to score three goals at Anfield because that doesn't happen often.” Alisson Becker – 7/10: Gathered City's only first-half strike from Fernandez comfortably. No chance with any of City's goals, which were all excellent finishes. Ronald Araujo – 6/10: Made a yellow-card gesture early on, asking the referee to book Guehi, earning himself a booking. Easily beaten by Semenya on the quarter-hour mark. Araujo and Munoz allowed Doku to cut inside for City's second. Virgil van Dijk – 6/10: Had not really been overly troubled by City but once the first goal went in after the sending-off, Liverpool's defence was quickly ripped apart in 13 brutal minutes. Late booking for a foul on Cherki. Jeremy Jacquet – 6/10: As above. The Frenchman had played Haaland well but the Norwegian, who had barely figured, cracked home the first goal not long after missing a sitter. Milos Kerkez – 7/10: Vital interception in the six-yard box to stop a Semenya cross finding Ndiaye. Kept the former Everton player very quiet. Alexis Mac Allister – 7/10: Acrobatic attempt on the edge of the six-yard box flew over the bar in the first half. Struck another effort just wide of the target after half-time. Hit another close-range first-time volley a few metres off target. Saw a free-kick saved. Ryan Gravenberch – 5/10: Booked at the start of the second half for a tackle on Anderson, then saw his shot saved by Donnarumma minutes later. Shown a second yellow for a clumsy challenge on Doku. Victor Munoz – 7/10: Buzzed around throughout and the summer signing from Osasuna showed plenty of promise. Hit a weak low effort straight at the City keeper on 33 minutes. Couldn't get close enough to Doku to stop the substitute from making it 2-0. Florian Wirtz – 4/10: Sliced a shot well wide from the edge of the box in the 55th minute. Set-piece deliveries and overall impact on games not good enough for a £116m player. Lewis Koumas – 7/10: Making his first Premier League start with Alexander Isak ruled out, the 21-year-old saw a thumping strike saved by Donnarumma just after half-time. Put in a good shift and can be happy with his efforts. Bradley Barcola – 6/10: Liverpool forked out £123m for the PSG forward but he is still finding his feet in English football. No attempts on goal, not much impact. Trey Nyoni (on for Wirtz, 66') – 6/10: Tough time for the teenager to come on with his team down to 10 men and City having just gone in front. Jeremie Frimpong (on for Araujo, 75') – 5/10: Skinned embarrassingly by Cherki ahead of City's third. Rio Ngumoha (on for Koumas, 75') – 6/10: City were 2-0 up by the time the English forward was introduced. Joe Gomez (on for Jacquet, 88') – N/A Federico Chiesa (on for Barcola, 88') – N/A Gianluigi Donnarumma – 7/10: Quickfire saves from Koumas and Gravenberch just after the break following a quiet opening half. The big Italian did what he had to do when called upon. Matheus Nunes – 7/10: One moment of sloppiness in possession ended in a chance for Koumas, but the Portuguese right-back was generally solid throughout. Ruben Dias – 8/10: Put in a real captain's performance at the back in an intense atmosphere, but up against a Liverpool attack without their two main strikers in Hugo Ekitike and Alexander Isak. Marc Guehi – 8/10: England defender was his usual excellent self at centre-back. Is such a reliable performer for club and country. Positioning and timing of tackles excellent again. Nico O'Reilly – 7/10: Booked for a foul on Munez on the edge of the penalty area just before the hour. Solid defensively and added to City's attacks down the left flank. Enzo Fernandez – 7/10: Midfielder had City's first effort on target in the 35th minute, but a curling effort was held by Alisson. His midfield partnership is quickly blossoming into a strong one for City. Elliot Anderson – 8/10: One thunderous, perfectly timed tackle beating Wirtz to the ball kept City on the attack at the end of the first half. England midfielder is turning into a Rolls-Royce of a player and was singled out for praise by teammate Haaland after the match. Antoine Semenyo – 7/10: Great wing play on 15 minutes with a run followed by a dangerous ball across the six-yard box that was crying out for a finish. Another great low cross at the start of the second half almost led to the opening goal. A threat for City. Rayan Cherki – 8/10: Some surging runs in the opening 45 minutes but made wrong choices with the final ball at times. Showed breathtaking skill to put Frimpong on his backside before putting City 3-0 up. Iliman Ndiaye – 5/10: Summer signing from Liverpool's Merseyside rivals Everton failed to make much of an impact and was hooked before the hour mark. Erling Haaland – 8/10: Should have scored with his first attempt on goal on the hour when through on goal but clipped the shot wide of target. Made no mistake with his second effort, smashing into the back of net in style for his sixth goal in six league games. Loves scoring against Liverpool. Jeremy Doku (on for Ndiaye, 55') – 9/10: Match-winning impact from winger. Drew a foul which earned Gravenbach a second yellow. His wing play ended with Haaland scoring. Curled home a stunning second for City. Involved in build-up for third Josko Gvardiol (on for O'Reilly, 68') – 7/10: Curled one shot high and wide. Lovely bit of skill to set up Cherki's goal. Allan (on for Haaland, 80') – N/A Ayyoub Bouaddi (on for Fernandez, 80') – N/A: Booked for bringing down Munoz.

title: UAE Property: 'Can my tenant legally list my apartment as a holiday rental without my consent?'
description: Subletting in Dubai is not illegal; however, the landlord must be informed and agree to the subleasing
content: Question: I own an apartment in Dubai Marina, which I've rented to the same tenant for two years. A neighbour recently contacted me because different people appear to be entering the apartment every few days with suitcases. I checked one of the holiday rental websites and, to my surprise, found what appears to be my apartment being advertised for short-term stays . I never agreed to this and my tenancy contract says the property is for residential use by the tenant. The tenant is paying the rent on time, so financially, I haven't lost anything, but I'm uncomfortable with strangers continually using a property I'm responsible for. Can a tenant legally do this without my permission, and could I as the owner face problems if something happens? Ahmed, Abu Dhabi Answer: I wouldn't ignore this simply because the rent continues to arrive on time. There's an important distinction between a tenant occasionally having friends or family stay and somebody commercially offering another person's property as short-term accommodation. Dubai's holiday-home sector is regulated, and properties being used for this purpose need to comply with the relevant licensing and registration requirements. Separately, your tenancy agreement determines what your tenant is permitted to do with the apartment. Subletting in Dubai is not illegal; however, the landlord must be informed and agree to the subleasing. Since you were not informed, his actions are illegal and he cannot simply decide to turn your property into his own short-term rental business. Before taking any action I suggest you document what you've discovered. Save screenshots of the advertisement, including photographs that clearly identify your apartment and keep any messages from neighbours or building management. I would then write to the tenant and ask for an explanation rather than immediately making accusations. I'd also establish whether the apartment has actually been registered as a holiday home and, if so, how this was done without your knowledge. There's another practical concern: short-term occupation can mean considerably more wear and tear than a conventional tenancy, as well as possible issues with access cards, building security and insurance. For landlords, this is a useful reminder that receiving the rent doesn't necessarily mean everything is fine with the property. Sensible asset management means knowing how your investment is actually being used. Q: My former partner and I bought a villa in Dubai several years ago in both our names. We have now separated. I want to sell the property so we can both move on financially, but my ex refuses. He says that because he owns half of the villa I cannot force him to sell his share. Neither of us can realistically afford to buy the other person out, and there is still a mortgage on the property. What happens when two people jointly own a Dubai property but one wants to sell and the other simply refuses? Are we effectively stuck owning it together indefinitely? Emma, Dubai A: This is unfortunately one of the complications of joint property ownership that people rarely think about when they're happily buying together. You cannot ordinarily sell your former partner's ownership interest simply because you want the whole property sold. Equally, however, joint ownership doesn't necessarily mean two people must remain financially tied together indefinitely. The first thing I'd establish is exactly how ownership is recorded on the title deed and the respective ownership percentages. Then have the property independently valued. Once you know the realistic selling price, deduct the outstanding mortgage and likely selling costs so both parties can see what equity would actually be available. Sometimes having a real number on the table makes negotiations considerably easier. Possible solutions include one party refinancing and purchasing the other's interest, an agreed sale on the open market or another mutually acceptable transfer arrangement, subject of course to the lender and Dubai Land Department requirements. I'd also check who has been paying the mortgage , service charges and other property expenses since the separation because those contributions may need to be considered when the financial position is ultimately resolved. If agreement genuinely cannot be reached, this moves beyond estate agency advice. You should speak to a Dubai lawyer experienced in property and co-ownership disputes about the legal mechanisms available to bring the joint ownership to an end. The wider lesson for unmarried couples, friends and relatives buying together is simple: discuss the break-up before the purchase. A written co-ownership agreement setting out what happens if one person wants to sell can prevent an enormous amount of difficulty later. The opinions expressed do not constitute legal advice and are provided for information only. Please send any questions to mario@evadxb.com

title: From Brazil to North Macedonia, Arabic literature finds new routes to readers through Frankfurt Book Fair
description: Publishers are looking beyond familiar markets as the Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Centre unveils new translation deals
content: Arabic books are finding new readers in Brazil, India and North Macedonia through a series of translation and co-publishing agreements signed at the Frankfurt Book Fair. The Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Centre announced 14 projects in seven languages, teaming up with 10 publishing and cultural partners, to mark the first anniversary of Kalima to the World . The programme was launched at last year's fair to support the translation and publication of Emirati and Arab books internationally. The new projects cover fiction, children's literature, history, heritage and social subjects, with editions planned in Portuguese, Macedonian, Hindi, Urdu, Greek, Spanish and English. Titles and publication dates are expected soon. North Macedonian publishing house Bata Press, which has released works by Egyptian Nobel laureate Naguib Mahfouz and contemporary Arab authors, is preparing to publish an Emirati novel about life in the UAE before its oil-driven development. Its publisher, Filip Batkoski, sees cultural connections between North Macedonia and the Arab world, particularly through their shared Ottoman history. “Actually, we have a lot of shared cultural heritage between the Arab world and North Macedonia. For example, we have been 500 years in the Ottoman Empire. And the Ottoman Empire has, of course, a huge impact from the Arabic world,” he said. “You cannot believe how many things we have in common between Arab people and us. I would say we are closer to Arab people than to western Europe or the United States.” The Frankfurt projects also include Hindi and Urdu translations through partnerships with India's National Book Trust and Pakistan's Book Corner and National Book Foundation. Greek publishers Kaktos and Vakxikon are also participating. The effort to reach more international readers has been extended through a separate agreement signed at the fair between the Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Centre and the Arab Publishers Association, an industry body representing publishers across the Middle East and North Africa. The partnership aims to expand the catalogue of Arabic titles available for translation and introduce them to international publishers. Speaking to The National , Mohamed Rashad, president of the association, said the aim was to reverse the "longstanding emphasis on translating foreign literature into Arabic", rather than taking Arabic writing to readers abroad. “For many years, what we have seen at Arab book fairs is that translation has always been from foreign languages into Arabic,” he said. “Yet we have enormous treasures in our heritage , history and civilisation.” Arab publishers were invited to nominate two or three books each, after which a specialist committee of writers, critics, translators and other experts examined more than 100 titles for inclusion in the catalogue. “Every publisher believes their book is the most important and deserves to be translated,” Rashad says. “Of course, that is not necessarily true. There must be certain criteria, and specialists who can make these decisions.” The catalogue is intended to introduce international publishers to a wider selection of Arab authors, with the centre's support helping to facilitate translation and provide funding. For Brazilian publisher Leonardo Garzaro, whose company Editora Rua do Sabao is among the partners, the opportunity is as much about challenging perceptions as it is about introducing new authors. “Many people in Brazil think about the Arab world as just one big thing. Literature can help them to understand, oh, this is the Emirates, this is Egyptian, this is Palestine. So they understand better the region and the different people who build the region,” he said. His company has already published almost 15 Arabic titles outside the initiative, including Iman Mersal's In the Footsteps of Enayat Al-Zayyat , which won the 2021 Sheikh Zayed Book Award for Literature. While its treatment of women's rights appealed to him, Garzaro said literary merit did not always translate into commercial appeal. “Sometimes a book is an award winner but doesn't work in Brazil because it's very specific,” he said. “But sometimes, as a publisher, you just like a book because you think it's important. You need to be brave and take a chance in order to help push your respective market and expand your readership.” Having worked with Abu Dhabi's publishing representatives for five years, Garzaro says that consistency can determine whether a publisher builds a collection of translated works or abandons plans to enter a new market. “That reliability is so important. While the budget is great, publishing is ultimately a business based on relationships. It's about building trust and ensuring the person you're dealing with is reliable. That's one of the first things we look for when meeting potential partners, apart from the budget,” he said. Saeed Al Tunaiji, executive director of the Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Centre, said the growing interest from international publishers was opening new markets for Emirati authors and Arabic literature. “Usually, Arabic books are translated into one or two languages, but now we are seeing interest in Arabic books and culture from speakers of these other languages,” he said. “Today, different cultures and language communities around the world have a real desire to discover Arabic literature and culture, as well as young, creative Emirati writers.”

title: MBZUAI fellowship puts Emiratis at forefront of AI research
description: Dr Mohamed Almarei to study at Oxford after being chosen as first Ruwwad AI Scholar
content: A new fellowship programme for Emirati postdoctoral researchers and academic leaders who incorporate artificial intelligence into their research has selected its first recipient. Dr Mohamed Almarei has been selected as the inaugural recipient of the Ruwwad AI Scholars (RAIS) Fellowship from Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI). He will take up a two-year research placement at the University of Oxford to continue applying AI to synthetic biology. Fellows are fully funded and sent to leading international institutions to build on their talents. “AI is becoming increasingly important to how we approach scientific research, particularly in fields such as biology, where complexity has long limited our ability to predict outcomes,” Dr Almarei told The National . Dr Almarei received his doctorate in bioengineering from Imperial College London, where he researched the engineering of biological systems for more sustainable bioproduction. The researcher came across the work of Prof Jean-Baptiste Lugagne, who works at the University of Oxford, and attended his presentation at the AI, Engineering Biology and Beyond conference in Bristol in January, which he described as a “turning point”. He found the methodology valuable in answering questions his own research had brought up and after reaching out, chose Prof Lugagne's lab for his fellowship placement. Dr Almarei said: “His research demonstrated how machine-learning could help predict cellular behaviour without requiring a complete understanding of every underlying process. I am now building on my experimental bioengineering background to investigate how data-driven AI models can help us better predict and control living systems.” His research at Oxford will harness AI to explore biological systems. “The aim is to develop accurate models that help us decrease our reliance on costly wet-lab experiments and design better biological systems for more reliable and sustainable biological production,” he said. Meanwhile, the UAE has been investing heavily in AI technology and infrastructure. Last week, Abu Dhabi's Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council met to review AI progress . A joint UAE-US AI Campus is planned for Abu Dhabi, while the Abu Dhabi government plans to become fully AI-native by 2027 , which would be a world first. Dr Almarei hopes to be part of this future and play a role in his country's development in the AI sphere. Fellows are considered for faculty positions at MBZUAI on their return. “The UAE has made AI a national priority, investing in research, education and the development of specialised talent,” he said. “Contributing to the UAE's future has always been part of my ambition. For me, success means gaining expertise that advances my research and strengthens the knowledge and capabilities I can bring back to the UAE.” The Emirati researcher wants his work to continue beyond Oxford to make a difference domestically and globally. “I see myself conducting research with both economic and societal impact, contributing to high-impact publications in world-class journals that reach the wider scientific community and mentoring the next generation of researchers on scientific rigour and integrity for the betterment of humanity,” he said.

title: Iran says US response to proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz is insufficient
description: National security chief Mohsen Rezaei says Washington accepted some conditions but others remain unresolved
content: Iran sent seven conditions to the US for reopening the Strait of Hormuz but the American response has been "insufficient", the head of the Supreme ⁠National ​Security Council told state media. Mohsen Rezaei said Washington had approached Tehran through three channels over the past two months – Pakistan, Qatar and Iraq – asking Iran to present its proposals for reopening the strategic waterway. “About two weeks ago, we communicated seven conditions to the Americans, stating explicitly that until these conditions are met, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened to them and no negotiations will take place,” Mr Rezaei said. “The Americans have now responded. While they have accepted some of our conditions, others remain unresolved. “We are no longer in the process of responding to the Americans. They have given their reply, and we consider it insufficient. They must clarify the issues that remain ambiguous to us.” Tehran effectively blocked the strait by attacking ships and laying mines after being attacked by Israel and the US in February at the start of the Iran war. The US has retaliated by imposing a blockade of Iranian ports. Iran and the US exchanged proposals to end the conflict through mediators during the UN General Assembly at the end of September. Sources close to the Iranian delegation and western diplomats told The National at the time that Tehran offered no concessions from its publicly stated position and was waiting for Washington to respond to demands presented at the talks. Mr Rezaei said Iran could derive economic benefits from controlling the strait, describing it as a major national asset. “The Gulf cannot be secure without Iran’s management of the Strait of Hormuz,” he said. “We do not merely mean closing the passage or collecting transit tolls; our interests extend far beyond that. Of course, we can certainly generate economic benefits from the Strait of Hormuz." The US has rejected Tehran's proposal that Iran and Oman , which sits on the southern side of the strait, should jointly manage the waterway, saying ships should have free passage under international law.

title: Manchester City block out the noise to defeat Liverpool at Anfield
description: Erling Haaland leads the way in 3-0 win against 10-man Reds
content: Manchester City completed a thumping win over Liverpool in an emotionally charged match at Anfield on Sunday. In their first game since the Premier League's findings , City secured a 3-0 win over a 10-man Liverpool. The match was evenly balanced in the first half but took a decisive turn in the second after Ryan Gravenberch was shown a red card in the 62nd minute. Erling Haaland gave City the lead three minutes later before Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki completed a statement win. An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period. The club have lodged an appeal against the verdict and continue to maintain their innocence, arguing that the commission's decision contains “clear material errors” and that City have evidence supporting their position. Liverpool fans, however, created a hostile atmosphere on Sunday with 60,000 in attendance. Home supporters drowned out the announcement of City's team ⁠with boos and chants. Victory gave City six wins from six and moved them three points clear of Arsenal on 18 points, providing an impressive response ​on the pitch after a turbulent period away from it. Liverpool are ninth after their first league loss of the season. Enzo Maresca 's side stood ​firm against Liverpool's early pressure and a fevered atmosphere before taking control after Gravenberch was sent off in the 62nd minute for a second booking following a foul on Doku. Haaland then struck three minutes later, smashing a left-footed shot past Alisson after Doku worked the ball into the box and his attempted shot was deflected into the path of the Norwegian. Doku doubled the lead in the 68th minute with ​a long-range shot that curled ‌into the far ⁠top corner. Cherki completed the ​rout in the 78th minute when he ​let ‌the ball roll through to Josko Gvardiol before turning into ⁠the box to meet his teammate's pass and ⁠slot the ball home. After the match, Haaland said the team showed amazing character. “Every single person [who is] part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time,” Haaland told sky Sports. “It was tough, it was hard but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone. “It's always tough to come here, if you look at the record, it's tough. “Important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do. And the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do.” City midfielder Elliot Anderson echoed Haaland's sentiments. “A tough place to come and we stuck together and fought for each other. We've showed courage,” Anderson told Sky Sports. “It was more than normal, arriving into Anfield and the first 10 minutes of the game. We did well to quieten the crowd. Struggled first half but second we were better and then the goals came. “I enjoy the crowd, the noise, I thrive on it and that's when I come alive. It gives me confidence.”

title: Riyadh airport attacked again after Houthi missile strike that killed 13 and injured hundreds
description: UN, EU and UAE strongly denounce attack on Saturday that also injured more than 300
content: Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was attacked again on Sunday after a missile strike by Yemen's Houthi rebels killed 13 people and injured more than 300, sparking global condemnation, including from the UN, the EU and the UAE. The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen 's government said a projectile struck the airport's Terminal 4, causing a fire, while a missile was intercepted in the vicinity. Operations at the airport were suspended after Saturday's deadly attack. Houthi military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree earlier on Sunday issued a warning to "all air shipping companies, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace – as they are subject to targeting". India's ​embassy ​in Riyadh said on Sunday ⁠that an Indian citizen injured in Saturday's attack had died. "We ⁠are in touch with ​the ⁠family ‌and will provide ​all support for ensuring the early repatriation of mortal remains," the embassy said in a post on X. The Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said Sunday's attack "resulted in injuries, and that an assessment of the damage and verification of the safety of the facilities is under way". The authority later reported that King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also attacked and that the damage was being assessed. In a statement earlier, the Houthis said the airports in Riyadh and Dammam were among four Saudi targets struck in the previous 24 hours. They also claimed to have carried out attacks on Saudi oil company Aramco's Shugadam gas site and Tanajib oil refinery in the Eastern Province, neither of which were confirmed by Saudi Arabia. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres said he was “deeply shocked” by Saturday's attack. “Attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law. These attacks must cease immediately,” Mr Guterres said in a statement. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas described the attack as an “appalling act of terror”, saying there could be no justification for indiscriminate attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. Ms Kallas expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia , offered condolences to the families of those killed and wished the injured a quick recovery. She said she remained in close contact with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan. EU foreign ministers will discuss increasing tension in the region on Monday, Ms Kallas said, adding that improved co-ordination between the bloc’s Red Sea naval Operation Aspides and the Saudi-led Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition was crucial. The UAE condemned the Houthi attacks in the strongest terms, saying they were a “flagrant violation” of Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and threatened its security and stability. The UAE Foreign Ministry reaffirmed the country’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for all measures aimed at protecting the kingdom’s security and stability. It also extended condolences to the victims’ families and wished the injured a quick recovery. Pakistan and Turkey, which signed a defence pact with Saudi Arabia in August, also condemned the attack. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called the attack “completely unacceptable”, saying strikes on civilians and critical infrastructure must cease immediately. He reaffirmed Islamabad’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. Turkey's Foreign Ministry said in a statement: "Actions that threaten regional security and stability and undermine the international community’s joint efforts to establish peace must be ended immediately." "Turkey also reiterated its support for Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity." UN special envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg described the attacks on Saudi Arabia as a “grave escalation” that threatened regional security, perpetuated violence and further complicated peace efforts in Yemen. “I repeat my call on [the Houthis] to cease these attacks,” Mr Grundberg said, repeating the need to respect international humanitarian law, including bans on directing attacks against civilians and civilian objects. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned what he called a “horrific terrorist attack” on the airport. “Terrorism targets innocent people and seeks to spread fear and instability. It must be confronted with resolve,” Mr Netanyahu said in a statement. “Israel looks forward to a strong Middle East – one that stands united against threats, protects its people, and builds a future of security, co-operation and prosperity for all the peoples of our region,” he said, extending condolences to the victims’ families and wishing the injured a full recovery. Russia also condemned the attack, with its Foreign Ministry saying the situation in the Middle East could be resolved only through diplomatic means that take into account the interests of all countries in the region, Russian news agency Interfax reported. Egypt condemned continued attacks on Saudi Arabia, describing them as a flagrant violation of international law. Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said Egypt was working to bring home the body of a citizen killed in the attack, who was identified as Azza Ramzy Mohamed Hassan, 28, a flight attendant who worked for Saudi airline flynas. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said he was "appalled" by the attack on the airport. "My thoughts are with those families who have lost loved ones, and those injured in this horrific attack,” he said on X, urging British nationals to avoid the airport, follow advice from Saudi authorities and consult the UK government’s travel guidance for the kingdom. Kuwait condemned the attack as a violation of international law and international humanitarian law, warning that it posed a serious threat to civil aviation and civilians. It reaffirmed its solidarity with Saudi Arabia and said the kingdom’s security was integral to that of Kuwait and other Gulf states. Iraq also condemned the attack, calling for a comprehensive halt to military operations and urging all parties to spare civilians and civilian infrastructure. Baghdad repeated its support for dialogue and diplomacy as alternatives to military action. Syria described the attack as a violation of Saudi sovereignty and a threat to regional security and civil aviation. Its Foreign Ministry expressed condolences to Saudi Arabia and the families of the victims, including a Syrian national killed in the strike, and backed measures to protect the kingdom’s security. Qatar reaffirmed its solidarity with Saudi Arabia, describing the attacks as a “grave violation” of the kingdom’s sovereignty and a direct threat to regional security, civilian safety and air navigation. Jordan condemned the attack after a Jordanian citizen was reported among the dead and four were wounded. Its Foreign Ministry said the Jordanian ambassador in Riyadh was co-ordinating with Saudi authorities to provide assistance and medical care.

title: Trump revokes decades-old restrictions on US-Lebanon flights
description: Decision follows meeting with Lebanese President Aoun in July
content: US President Donald Trump has lifted decades-old restrictions on flights between the US and Lebanon , removing a major obstacle to restoring direct air links. Mr Trump said restrictions imposed under four presidential determinations issued in 1985, 1992, 1998 and 2007 were “no longer necessary” to ensure the security of aircraft. He signed the decision on September 30 and it was published in the Federal Register. It follows a meeting between Mr Trump and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun at the White House in July, during which Mr Aoun requested that the restrictions be lifted. Mr Aoun welcomed the move, describing it as “a sign of confidence in the measures taken by the Lebanese state to guarantee the security of civil aviation”. He thanked Mr Trump for responding favourably to his request, as well as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio for following up on the matter. Mr Aoun also reaffirmed Lebanon’s commitment to international civil aviation security standards and expressed hope that the decision would strengthen co-operation between Beirut and Washington. Lebanese ambassador to Washington, Nada Mouawad, also welcomed the decision, saying it “opens the door to the resumption of direct flights between Lebanon and the United States”. The restrictions were introduced in 1985 by the administration of president Ronald Reagan after the hijacking of TWA Flight 847 by alleged Hezbollah militants. The flight, travelling from Athens to Rome, was forced to land in Beirut. The hijackers killed a US Navy diver aboard the plane during the subsequent 17-day hostage crisis. Subsequent US administrations gradually eased the restrictions. In 1992, foreign carriers were permitted to transport cargo to Lebanon. In 1998, ticket sales to Lebanon and flights with stopovers were authorised, while a 2007 decision granted exemptions to certain American carriers operating under contracts with the US government. The measures continued to prevent the restoration of direct commercial air links between the two countries. Mr Trump's decision revokes all four presidential determinations and directs the US Secretary of Transportation to implement the change immediately, including by removing any conflicting regulations, rules or orders. However, the lifting of the restrictions does not mean direct commercial flights between the US and Lebanon will resume immediately.

title: Trump says Russia and Ukraine agree to 'energy ceasefire'
description: Zelenskyy denies knowledge of deal, but adds that 'if Moscow agrees, so do we'
content: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday Russia and Ukraine agreed to stop attacks on each other’s energy infrastructure, and announced an immediate halt after an escalation in deadly strikes. “Effective immediately, there is an energy ceasefire in the war between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it,” Mr Trump wrote on social media. He provided no details on its duration, how it would be enforced or which sites would be covered. Ukrainian ⁠President Volodymyr Zelenskyy ​said in an ​interview with the news outlet Axios that he was ​not ‌aware of ⁠any ceasefire but added that if ​Moscow agreed to ‌it, Kyiv would accept it. “The ceasefire ‌announcement was news for ​me. But if Russians agree to an energy ceasefire Ukraine ​will agree. If ​President Trump negotiated it ​with [Russian President Vladimir] Putin – please tell us ​when the ceasefire begins – we are ready and we will accept ⁠it,” Mr Zelenskyy said. The announcement followed a dispute between Mr Trump and Mr Zelenskyy over attacks on Russian oil refineries. Mr Trump criticised the strikes on Saturday, a day after Washington temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were intended to limit Moscow’s revenue for its war. “I think it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president,” Donald Trump told reporters at the White House. Mr Zelenskyy responded on Sunday by offering to organise elections if Mr Putin agreed to a 60-day halt in fighting. “Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organise elections,” Mr Zelenskyy told ABC News . He also challenged suggestions that Ukraine’s attacks were responsible for rising fuel costs, saying it was easy to blame Kyiv “when everybody in the world understands (that) because of the war in (the) Middle East, the prices are rising”. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen voiced backing for Mr Zelenskyy amid his row with Mr Trump, and backed Kyiv's calls for an energy ceasefire with Russia. "Fully supported the call of President Zelenskyy for a ceasefire that would protect global food supplies and energy infrastructure in Ukraine and Russia," Ms von der Leyen wrote online after talking to Mr Zelenskyy. "And my full support for President Zelenskyy as he leads the fight for his people's freedom," she added.

title: Max Verstappen wins Singapore GP as Kimi Antonelli moves closer to title
description: Red Bull driver dominates weekend at Marina Bay ​Circuit but Mercedes star extends championship lead to 102
content: ​Red ⁠Bull's Max ⁠Verstappen dominated the Singapore ⁠Grand Prix as he won from pole at the ⁠Marina Bay Street ​Circuit ⁠on ‌Sunday for ​his second straight victory of the season. ⁠Verstappen had a few complaints about the circuit, lamenting the lack of overtaking opportunities, but enjoyed a near perfect weekend as he also won the Sprint race. It was a memorable way for the four-time world champion to celebrate his 250th grand prix weekend. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished ​second ‌while ⁠Mercedes driver ​ Kimi Antonelli ​was ‌third to ⁠extend his championship ⁠lead over teammate George Russell. Verstappen was in control of the race from the start, overcoming an early challenge from ⁠Leclerc. The Dutchman, who won ‌the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend, had never ​won in Singapore before and he had come into the race weekend stating he had “unfinished business”. “It's taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre, even though I think the medium tyre for everyone was more of a struggle,” Verstappen said. “But it worked out, so of course very happy to win here … The last two races have been really positive for us and it's just great to ​see. “We have a lot of motivation in the team to try and deliver even more results. It is a really good group of people, I really enjoy working with them and hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year.” Antonelli extended his championship lead over teammate ‌Russell to 102 ⁠points. The young Italian can ​win the title in the next round in ​Austin. “Can ‌I? Really?” Antonelli said when he was told after ⁠his 14th podium of the season. “Well, let's not worry about ⁠that. Let's try to do the best weekend as possible and finish the job. “It was a very tough race [in Singapore] but really happy with a podium at the end. I managed to take advantage of the fight of Lando and Lewis and to make a move on both and to bring home P3 is a great result for the team.” Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton had qualified third on the grid but endured a forgettable evening. The Briton slipped to ​sixth behind Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri after the two McLaren drivers overtook him in the dying stages as he struggled with his tyres. Hamilton spoke to his team over the radio and said the result was due to his call. “Sorry, boys. I let you down today with that strategy,” he said. “My call, and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it in the next one.”

title: Boat capsizes off Djibouti leaving 139 dead and scores missing
description: More than 80 survivors aboard vessel bound for Yemen were all Ethiopians, UN migration agency says
content: At least 139 migrants, including ​15 children, ​have died ​and more than 80 are ⁠missing after a boat carrying about 305 people ⁠capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, ​the UN's migration agency said on Sunday. The boat overturned ⁠near Guhere, north of Djibouti's port town of Obock, during the night of October 8 into October 9, the International Organisation for Migration said, citing survivor accounts. More than 80 people survived ⁠the shipwreck, all Ethiopian citizens, the agency said. The ⁠Ethiopian government did not immediately ‌respond to requests for comment from Reuters. The IOM raised its initial death toll of 109 released earlier on Sunday after 30 more bodies were recovered. Out of the 109 bodies recovered earlier, 52 were men, 42 women and 15 children, the agency said. "Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," said IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, Alexandre Coissac. "This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities," he added. Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM said, also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials. The tragedy follows renewed fighting in Ethiopia's Tigray region , nearly four years after a peace agreement ended a devastating two-year civil war there. The IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix shows more than 20,000 incoming movements to Djibouti from Ethiopia since September 10. Each year, tens of thousands of migrants from the Horn of Africa travel through Djibouti and cross the Bab Al Mandeb strait to Yemen, from where they hope to reach Gulf countries. The crossings continue despite fighting on Yemen's Red Sea coast between government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels since early September. At the same time, more than 3,700 people fled the fighting and made the crossing from Yemen to Djibouti, according to ​the IOM. With reporting from agencies

title: Carrie season 2: Mike Flanagan on Stephen King's ideas for what comes next
description: The director discusses major changes to the classic horror novel and how its potential continuation could unfold
content: When creator Mike Flanagan brought his plans for a new adaptation of Carrie to Stephen King, he had more in mind than another retelling of the author's 1974 horror novel. His eight-part Prime Video series follows Carrie White (Summer H. Howell), a bullied teenager discovering her telekinetic powers, but also expands on something King had only hinted at: the existence of others like her. Flanagan, who previously adapted King's Gerald's Game and Doctor Sleep , was uncertain how the author would receive his proposed changes. “I was very nervous to bring it to him because the pitch was loaded with changes, and my feeling was that if he didn't like them, I wasn't going to do the show,” he tells The National . But Stephen King embraced the approach, even contributing ideas to one of the new characters. His involvement could prove important to the series' future, with Flanagan having previously discussed the possibility of telling the story over three seasons. Prime Video has yet to announce a second, although the first season leaves several storylines unresolved. Warning: spoilers for all eight episodes of Carrie follow. The most significant departure from King's novel comes in the finale. The original story ends with Carrie dying after the destruction of her school and much of her hometown. Flanagan instead allows her to survive, escaping Chamberlain alongside Emaline (Thalia Dudek), another young woman with psychic abilities. “We decided very early that we really believed this version of Carrie deserved to survive the story, regardless of whether we were talking about future seasons or anything else,” Flanagan says. Her survival raises a question the novel never had to address: how Carrie might come to terms with the violence she has committed. Flanagan has also changed the circumstances of the prom massacre. The series preserves the humiliation that sets it in motion, when a bucket of blood is dumped on Carrie after she is crowned prom queen, but distributes responsibility for the deaths among several characters. Emaline, who has been secretly observing Carrie, takes control of her body during the disaster, with her permission. Other women with supernatural abilities are involved in the violence that follows. “I think the tragedy hasn't changed whatsoever. The scope of the tragedy is exactly the same,” Flanagan says. “But I do think tragedies have many authors.” There are three deaths, however, that he was determined to leave in Carrie's hands. The first is Tommy Ross (Joel Oulette), her prom date, whom she accidentally kills before Emaline takes control. Later, she confronts Chris Hargensen (Alison Thornton) and Billy Nolan (Arthur Conti), the teenagers responsible for humiliating her. Chris attempts to stop Billy from running Carrie over, causing their car to crash. Both survive, only for Carrie to kill them herself. Flanagan describes Carrie confronting Chris and Billy “eye to eye, and not in a moment of reactivity, but in a moment of clear and conscious sober decision”. “I do think it was important to me if she was going to live that she also be able to live with what happened,” he says. Chris's final attempt to stop Billy adds another complication. Having spent much of the series tormenting Carrie, she ultimately tries to save her life, only to be killed by the girl she has bullied. Flanagan is conscious of how audiences might respond to that moment, describing the satisfaction of “wanting that wish fulfilment of seeing people get their comeuppance”, alongside the discomfort of “realising we're kind of celebrating the death of teenagers and kids”. For Carrie, those conflicting feelings could become a central part of her story. She has escaped Chamberlain and the people who made her life miserable, but must now reckon with having killed two of them deliberately. “There's plenty for her to have to wrestle with what she did and why, and for her to deal with the complex feelings that she'll have,” Flanagan says. Carrie's escape also leaves her with an uncertain ally in Emaline, whose actions have put them both at odds with Adelaide (Kate Siegel), the powerful woman who sent her to observe Carrie. Throughout the series, Adelaide interviews survivors of the prom disaster, manipulating their memories to conceal her group's involvement. Emaline eventually defies her and helps Carrie leave Chamberlain, although Adelaide's interest in the teenager remains unresolved. Their escape provides another possible direction for a second season, with Carrie now connected to a group of women whose abilities resemble her own. Adelaide's intentions, Emaline's relationship with her former allies and the extent of their powers all remain to be explored. The foundation for this storyline comes from King's novel , which suggests Carrie is not the only person capable of telekinesis. The new characters, however, allowed Flanagan to develop that idea far beyond the original story. King himself played an active role in that process. “Most of his direct ideas and suggestions came to bear with the character of Emaline,” Flanagan says. That involvement is especially significant given Emaline's influence over the finale. Her intervention changes Carrie's responsibility for the massacre, and her decision to help her escape creates the opportunity for their story to continue. Flanagan expects some resistance to the character from readers familiar with King's novel, making the author's contribution all the more interesting. “That's a character I think that people who love the books have an initial resistance to, and that's the character that Stephen King had the most input into,” he says. Emaline also holds knowledge of Adelaide's group that Carrie has only begun to discover. Having turned against the woman who sent her to Chamberlain, she could become Carrie's guide to this unfamiliar world, although the full extent of her loyalties and motivations has yet to be established. Flanagan says King was particularly engaged by the direction these characters could take the story, and their potential influence on Carrie's life beyond the events of the first season. “He had a lot to say about that other world of powerful women and how it could impact Carrie's story and where it could go moving forward,” Flanagan says. “And he was very excited about the possibilities there.” All eight episodes of Carrie are streaming on Prime Video

title: Major road upgrades planned in Abu Dhabi's Mussaffah
description: Department of Municipalities and Transport announces 13km of improvements across industrial zone
content: Abu Dhabi is set to overhaul key roads in Mussaffah, with upgrades spanning 13km designed to cut congestion and improve safety. The Department of Municipalities and Transport has announced plans to upgrade roads along the E30 and 8th Street corridors in Mussaffah, improving connections between the industrial area, Mohamed bin Zayed City and Zayed City. The project aims to ease congestion, reduce travel time and improve road safety across the district. Central to the scheme is a new free-flowing motorway at 8th Street, featuring three lanes in each direction and three additional service lanes on each side to maintain access to shops and businesses. The upgraded street is expected to accommodate up to 4,000 vehicles an hour. The wider project includes upgrades to four interchanges along E30, improved connections with 8th Street and E20, and modifications to nine key junctions. The project also plans two new bridges linking Mussaffah with Mohamed bin Zayed City, along with a dedicated pedestrian bridge. Separate enhancement works will cover about 8km along 8th Street. Eisa Al Mazrouei, director general of infrastructure development at the DMT, said the upgrades were designed to serve the varied demands placed on Mussaffah's road network. “By separating traffic passing through the area from local access and improving connections with surrounding communities, we can support economic activity while making everyday journeys easier and safer,” Mr Al Mazrouei said. The Mussaffah project forms part of broader efforts to strengthen connectivity across Abu Dhabi emirate. Among the wider initiatives is a planned two-tunnel undersea link running from the eastern tip of Abu Dhabi island to Mussaffah, passing beneath Khor Al Maqta and the Hudayriyat Island channel. Officials said the decisions being made now were intended to support the emirate's long-term development needs.

title: RTA wins Dubai-it Award for delivering projects at record speed
description: Transport authority honoured for doubling global infrastructure delivery benchmarks
content: The first Dubai-it Award for Institutions in the Field of Government has been given to the emirate's Roads and Transport Authority in recognition of its record-breaking delivery of infrastructure. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence and Chairman of the Dubai Executive Council, presented the award to the RTA, citing its ability to deliver major roads, bridges and tunnels at twice the global benchmark for speed and efficiency. “Dubai-it means achieving something extraordinary with excellence in record time,” Sheikh Hamdan said. Dubai Metro has achieved a punctuality rate of 99.7 per cent, while the authority has completed more than 250 traffic improvements that reduced travel times by up to 60 per cent. It also executed major infrastructure projects, including the Infinity Bridge, at costs below the global average, while maintaining high-quality standards. The authority implemented 117 quick-win improvements within two years and made 82 services available with no waiting time. The RTA also developed AI-powered autonomous taxis and an air-taxi station, advancing Dubai's future mobility programme. Road feedback is now monitored and addressed within 24 hours, while cycle tracks have been expanded at pace. Mohammad Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs and Chairman of the Executive Office of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, said the award highlighted an institutional model built on sustained achievement and rapid response. “RTA's approach clearly reflected this philosophy on the ground by combining quality, speed and continuity, turning challenges into opportunities for development and service improvement,” Mr Al Gergawi said. The Dubai-it initiative was launched by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, to embed a culture of bold ambition and excellent execution across public and private institutions. The annual Dubai-it Award recognises people, projects, companies and institutions that deliver extraordinary results, setting the standard continued development in the emirate.

title: Driverless Glydways electric pods launched on Dubai's Bluewaters Island
description: Each vehicle carries between four and six people, travels at up to 50kph and has a range of 250km
content: Dubai has started testing a public transport system that uses small, AI-powered vehicles on Bluewaters Island. The Roads and Transport Authority launched the four-week trial of the Glydways autonomous transit system on Saturday, with director general Mattar Al Tayer taking the first ride along the designated route at the Dubai Holding retail destination. The system uses driverless electric pods, travelling on dedicated roads that can be built at ground level or elevated. Each vehicle carries between four and six passengers, travels up to 50kph and has a range of up to 250km on one charge. The vehicles are equipped with 20 high-resolution Lidar sensors, radar and high-definition cameras. Up to 10 vehicles can be virtually linked with headways of less than one second, giving the system a combined capacity of more than 20,000 passengers per hour in both directions. Mr Al Tayer said the trial reflected the RTA's commitment to testing advanced technology within Dubai's urban environment, with a particular focus on first and last-mile connectivity. “The trial operation marks an important stage in assessing the system’s operational and technical aspects, evaluating its ability to provide a safe, seamless and reliable mobility experience, and exploring opportunities for integration with the public transport network, particularly for first and last-mile journeys,” he said. Plans for the project include a 2.8km route linking National Paints Metro Station with Bluewaters, alongside proposed routes serving Jumeirah Village Circle, Dubai Festival City, Business Bay and Mohammed bin Rashid City. The system's developers say capital costs are up to 90 per cent lower and operating costs up to 70 per cent lower than comparable transport modes. The project is being delivered under a public-private partnership, with the Bluewaters trial implemented in collaboration with Dubai Holding, which is providing infrastructure and operational support. Mark Seeger, founder and co-chief executive of Glydways, said Dubai offered an advanced environment for testing future mobility solutions. “Through our collaboration with RTA, we look forward to utilising the results of the trial operation to assess the system’s performance and further develop its solutions, supporting Dubai’s aspirations for smart, seamless and sustainable mobility,” he said. The trial will assess vehicle performance, autonomous driving systems, safety and reliability, as well as passenger experience, generating data to inform decisions on future network expansion across the emirate.

title: Riyadh attack: Iran cannot distance itself from outsourced Houthi violence
description: Demanding the benefits of regional diplomacy while ignoring the consequences of its own strategy is not a credible position for Tehran
content: The deaths of at least 12 people and injuries to more than 300 others in Saturday’s shocking attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport is a reminder of the threat posed by Yemen ’s Houthi militia. Among the victims were Saudi and foreign citizens en route to work, travel or worship. An airport that should have been a place of safe passage became a scene of terror and devastation. The Houthis bear direct responsibility for this outrage. However, Iran – whose support for the rebels has helped turn a local insurgency into a force capable of killing innocent civilians far from Yemeni territory – is also culpable. Tehran cannot claim to be a responsible regional player while distancing itself from the outsourced violence that its influence enables. For years, Iran’s strategy of forward defence relied on cultivating armed partners who could project power beyond its borders. The numerous setbacks suffered by Tehran and its regional allies in recent years have exposed the limits of that approach. Nevertheless, the Houthis’ ability to launch missiles and drones against civilian infrastructure shows how much damage such networks can still inflict. Iran’s military support for the Houthis is well known. But it also runs counter to statements from some leading Iranians, such as President Masoud Pezeshkian, who have spoken about the need for regional engagement. Mohammad Javad Zarif, Iran’s former foreign minister, has challenged Tehran’s hardline approach that treats much of the outside world as a threat. Such arguments should be taken seriously but diplomacy cannot produce results while those in power in Tehran continue to support a militia that not only represses Yemenis at home but attacks soft targets overseas. Nor is Houthi escalation the source of influence that Iran might imagine it to be. As well as inviting retaliation, it strengthens the case for regional security co-operation and makes Gulf neighbours less likely to trust Iranian assurances. The result is a more dangerous and unpredictable environment in which miscalculation becomes increasingly likely. Gulf countries should not have to accept attacks on their cities, airports, energy infrastructure and civilian populations as the price of Iran’s regional ambitions. Saudi Arabia has every right to protect its people and avoid further attacks. The Houthis are themselves endangering Yemenis by their actions. If those in power in Tehran genuinely want to rebuild relations with their neighbours, they must do more than call for dialogue. Facing down their hardliners and rethinking military support for a destructive Houthi campaign would be a good place to start. Iran cannot demand the benefits of regional diplomacy while ignoring the consequences of its own strategy.

title: Pakistan President suspends government in province ruled by Imran Khan's party
description: Emergency declared in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa after unrest over demands for former cricketer's release from jail
content: Pakistan's President has suspended the government in a province ruled by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's party, declaring a state of emergency after unrest fuelled by a growing clamour for his release. Asif Ali Zardari followed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's advice to declare the emergency following a federal cabinet decision, his office said in a statement. The decision comes as Mr Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party steps up its campaign to secure his release, with supporters rallying for several days and threatening to march on the capital Islamabad. The emergency was declared in north-western Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, which is governed by the PTI. The advisory submitted by Mr Sharif said the provincial government had failed to tackle Islamist militancy, a statement from the Prime Minister's office read. Pakistan 's constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during a state of emergency. However, the presidential office did not specify how the province would be administered following Sunday's decision. Zulfikar Bukhari, a close aide to Mr Khan and a PTI spokesman, condemned the move, describing it as a “ridiculous decision” and saying Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had the country's “only legitimately elected government”. “This will only lead to further bloodshed, instability and collateral damage,” said Mr Bukhari. He added there had always been room for talks but the decision showed negotiations were never the government's intention. The move marks an escalation in tension between Mr Sharif's government and the PTI, which has accused the authorities of using legal and political measures to weaken the party and keep its leader behind bars. Mr Khan, a former cricket star who served as prime minister from 2018 to 2022, has been in jail since August 2023. He faces scores of charges, from corruption to treason, following anti-establishment riots that year. He and his legal team reject the allegations, describing them as politically motivated and intended to harm his popularity. The government has denied the accusations. Mr Khan's supporters have continued to demand his release, accusing the authorities of making the former prime minister a target despite his continued popularity among sections of the public. The PTI has also voiced opposition to the government's handling of the economy and its broader political agenda. The latest mobilisation comes amid growing concern over Mr Khan's health . His family and supporters warned his condition has deteriorated in prison, while his lawyers said he has lost significant vision in his right eye. His supporters have called for urgent action over his treatment and release. Mr Sharif has previously urged the PTI to abandon its planned march on Islamabad and return to negotiations with the government. Talks between the two sides had reached an impasse before the latest protests began. The Prime Minister has warned that demonstrations could damage the economy and said the government would take measures to maintain law and order, protect public property and prevent unrest. The declaration of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa raises the stakes as the government seeks to contain the PTI campaign. It remains unclear how the takeover of provincial functions will be implemented or whether the decision will deter supporters from proceeding with their planned march on the capital.

title: Dubai Parks and Resorts reopens with new attractions and live shows
description: Bowling and Lamborghini racing simulators join Riverland’s line-up as operator outlines plans for the new season
content: Dubai Parks and Resorts has reopened after more than six months of closure, with new attractions at Riverland, live shows at Motiongate Dubai and the return of dinosaur-themed glamping. The destination welcomed visitors back on October 7 to Motiongate Dubai , Real Madrid World, Legoland Dubai Resort and The World of Riverland. Fernando Eiroa, chief executive of operator Dubai Holding Entertainment, said preparations for each season begin with visitors. “Every year at the end of the season, we sit and we talk to our customers. We ask them how can we improve,” he told The National . Their feedback helps shape decisions about attractions, live entertainment and dining , he said. Riverland, the destination’s dining and entertainment district, now offers 14 attractions. New additions include bowling and Lamborghini racing simulators, where visitors can test their driving skills on virtual tracks. These joint activities include go-karting, archery, axe-throwing and mini golf. Motiongate Dubai is also introducing new shows alongside its Hollywood-inspired rides and attractions. At Real Madrid World , visitors can test their football skills, take penalties, play basketball and compete against friends and other guests. “You have to be part of the experience. You have to sweat a little bit to enjoy the experience,” Eiroa said. T-Rex Glamping , which opened last year, is also returning for the new season. The campsite combines themed tents with animatronic dinosaurs, whose moving tails, lifelike eyes and calls form part of the prehistoric setting. Eiroa said its appeal lay in making the stay itself part of the entertainment, with activities extending beyond a day at the parks. The company is also updating concerts, restaurants and cultural offerings at Global Village ahead of its new season. Eiroa said Dubai ’s reputation for theme parks and entertainment had grown over the past five or six years, adding to its established appeal through hotels, restaurants and hospitality. He compared its development with Orlando and Los Angeles, where several theme parks and attractions operate alongside one another. The expansion of attractions in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, he said, was giving international visitors more reasons to travel to the UAE. “We are competitors in a way, but at the same time this is helping the country,” he said. UAE residents also remain an important part of the business, although the balance between domestic and international visitors varies across the group’s destinations. “People don’t come to Dubai to go to a cinema,” Eiroa said, explaining why Roxy Cinemas primarily attracts residents. The View at The Palm draws more international tourists and residents who bring visiting friends and relatives. Through its Truly Amazing campaign, Dubai Holding Entertainment is bringing together attractions including Global Village , Dubai Parks and Resorts, The Green Planet, Roxy Cinemas and The View at The Palm. Eiroa said the company was looking to bundle different experiences, allowing visitors to combine more of its destinations in one trip.

title: Senne Lammens: Manchester United must learn quickly and cut out defensive errors
description: Goalkeeper admits Tottenham's late equaliser was a cruel blow with club having made worst start since 1986
content: Manchester United’s failure to beat bottom-of-the-table Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford on Saturday means the club have made their worst league start since 1986. United have only six points from their first six games and face a daunting run of fixtures, starting with Tuesday’s Champions League tie at Atletico Madrid. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens spoke to media, including The National , after Saturday’s 1-1 draw , which saw United lead through Bryan Mbeumo's 73rd minute strike only to see Dominic Solanke equalise in stoppage time. Q: Can you put your finger on what went wrong? Going ahead was encouraging, but to concede at the end was disappointing. A: It's very disappointing because you find a way to get the game, to get the advantage, to score a goal, to get 1-0 up against 10 men. That's the position you want to be in. So, it's very disappointing to concede the last goal at the end. We need to learn a lot from it, because these are the games you have to try to pull towards yourself. Winning these games is very important if you want to have a good season, so it's very important for us to learn from this and move on, to get these games behind us. What have you made of the team's start this season, with six points from six games? Obviously, it's not the start you would have wanted, especially after the success of last season. I think points say one thing, which is very important, because we are a team who wants to play at the top of the league. But it's not the only thing. In terms of our play, we do some things well, but I think defensively, we can be a bit better, a bit more solid. Today was better because, in the first half, it was a bit more difficult, but you survive, you keep it at zero, and then you are able to pull those games towards yourself. So, yeah, it's like you said. It's a bit like that feeling last season, where maybe we didn't have our A-game, but we were still able to pull those games out and win them. This time, the feeling is that you play better, but you don't really get the wins you deserve. So, it's a bit of a mix of both. You want to play well and also be able to win the games where maybe you don't have your A-game. Can I just bring it back to the equaliser? From your perspective, what happened there? It seemed to be another sort of miscommunication between you and Lisandro Martinez. I haven't watched it back yet, but I don't think there was really a miscommunication. First of all, I think the cross needs to be stopped. We need to put more pressure on the guy with the ball because his cross is too easy. Then I think it's a bit of a struggle, a bit of push and pull between the attacker and Licha (Martinez). And, yeah, I think he got away with it. But I don't think there was a miscommunication, no. What did you make of the overall performance today? Tottenham were very dominant in the first 25 or 30 minutes. I think in the first half, everyone could see that we needed to be better with the ball and without it.
