A previous amendment in 2020 to the legislation on attempted suicide gave judges the discretion to offer mental health treatment as an alternative to prison. “The removal of criminal liability for attempted suicide recognises that someone experiencing a crisis needs care and support,” said Dr Hassan Elhais, a lawyer at Amal Al Rashedi Lawyers and Legal Consultants. “Removing the fear of prosecution can encourage people to seek help earlier and give families greater confidence to request urgent assistance.” Dr Elhais said the latest reform removed the prospect of people facing criminal action in relation to attempted suicide, further strengthening the focus on treatment and support over punishment. "The new amendment removes criminal liability for attempted suicide itself. "That is the substantive difference. Treatment was previously an alternative available to the court within a criminal framework. The new amendment removes punishment for the attempt itself." The key change to existing legislation improves the chances of early intervention, provides the care and support needed, and supports suicide prevention efforts, state news agency Wam said. The new laws also lay out penalties for those whose actions cause someone to try to take their own life. A three-to-five year prison sentence awaits anyone convicted of causing somebody to attempt suicide, who then suffers a serious injury or permanent disability as a result. If someone's actions are found to have caused another person to take their own life, the sentence is increased to up seven years in prison. If someone causes a person under the age of 18 to attempt suicide, the charge is raised to premeditated murder. Foreign citizens found guilty of these charges face deportation. The amendments include imposing a minimum prison sentence of 15 years for those convicted of intentionally killing someone. Under the new rules, even if a family of a victim waive their right to qisas, which entitles them to seek the maximum punishment, the offender must still serve 15 to 20 years in prison. “This amendment strengthens the effectiveness of legal deterrence,” Wam reported. “It balances the right of the victim's heirs to concede their right to qisas, and the requirements of the public right and the protection of society from extremely serious crimes, within a justice system that safeguards rights and supports security and societal stability.” Previously it had been the case that an offender still had to serve a minimum of seven years in prison, even if the victim's family waived their right to qisas. “The 2026 amendments make the law easier to apply in two sensitive areas: they preserve a 15 to 20-year prison sentence after a family waives qisas in an intentional-killing case, and they set clearer, outcome-based penalties for anyone who encourages or assists another person’s suicide,” said Nikhat Sardar Khan, a Dubai-based lawyer.

title: Trump rules out attack on Iran before midterm elections
description: President says US having ‘productive discussions’ with Tehran as blockade of Strait of Hormuz remains in place
content: President Donald Trump on Thursday said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections and that Washington was engaged in “productive discussions” with Tehran. In a post on Truth Social, Mr Trump said Iran was in a “very bad condition” economically and militarily and the blockade on the Strait of Hormuz would remain in “full force”. “We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3,” he wrote. “We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran.” The announcement comes a day after reports in US media that Washington was preparing to launch renewed military action against Iran before the midterm elections. Last month, Mr Trump said the war with Iran would end “immediately” after the midterm elections. He has also previously said the US was no longer seeking a negotiated end to the war. Shortly afterwards, he said fuel prices and the cost of living would go down. But polls show the war Mr Trump started alongside Israel in February is unpopular among US voters . A major issue has been the rise in fuel and everyday prices, which has followed disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway, through which about a fifth of the world’s oil supply typically flows, has emerged as a major sticking point for Mr Trump. The Republican President had campaigned on promises of lower costs and repeatedly blamed inflation on his predecessor, Joe Biden. With the elections less than a month away, Mr Trump is also facing historically low approval ratings. The midterm elections are critical for Mr Trump, who still has two years left in office. At stake is control of Congress, where Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers.

title: Two arrested inside US airbase in UK as counter-terror police investigate
description: Pair of Latvian men detained on suspicion of trespassing in fresh breach
content: Two men have been arrested after being found inside an RAF base used by the US military in the UK. The Metropolitan Police said two Latvian men, aged 36 and 32, were arrested in the early hours of Thursday by Ministry of Defence Police (MDP) on suspicion of trespassing inside the base perimeter at RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire, 100km north of London. RAF Molesworth is home to US intelligence-operation centres for Europe and Africa, as well as a Nato intelligence hub, according to the CIA's website. It is the second airbase used by the US in Britain to be subject to a security alert in the past two weeks. The US pulled all its strategic bombers out of the UK over concerns at RAF Fairford after an incident. Four hours after a suspicious vehicle was found on the perimeter, the men were taken into police custody launching an investigation that is being carried out by counter-terrorism police. At this stage, the incident is not being linked to the several arrests that were made in connection to RAF Fairford. The breach of the perimeter fence was identified by chance and the two men later found and arrested. They were initially held on suspicion of trespassing on a prohibited site and criminal damage, and were taken to a Cambridgeshire police station. The pair have since been arrested again on suspicion of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK under the National Security Act 2023 “We’re very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites, but at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford last week,” said Commander Helen Flanagan, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, which is leading the investigation. “Our investigation into this incident is at its very early stages. A big part of this is looking at any potential motivation as to why the men were present at the site, but I must stress we are keeping an open mind at this stage and enquiries are very much ongoing.” Officers carried out two searches at addresses in the Peterborough area, about 30km from the RAF base, in connection with the investigation. The abandoned vehicle was recovered by police and is undergoing further searches. Concerns over the vehicle led to the deployment of specialist ordnance disposal officers to carry out additional checks. As a precaution, a cordon was put in place but was lifted after nothing of concern was found. On Tuesday, a British citizen, 22, was arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with the incident close to RAF Fairford, counter-terrorism police said. Five men, aged 23 to 25, had already been arrested on September 27 near the base on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail in what police called an “investigative decision” that was “grounded in experience and strategy”. A sixth man, a 25-year-old dual Iranian-British citizen, was arrested on October 1 in Westminster, central London and was later released on bail.

title: EU parliament calls for Muslim Brotherhood terror listings
description: Vote by MEPs asks EU member states to list individuals and organisations linked to the Brotherhood
content: The European Parliament backed proposals on Thursday to “counter the influence” of the Muslim Brotherhood and list some of its supporters as terrorists. The resolution passed by a vote of 381 to 167, and asks the EU's member states to add people and organisations linked to the Brotherhood to the bloc's joint list of terrorists. It says EU countries should provide information “enabling the assessment” of the Brotherhood's leaders and structures and whether they should be classified as terrorists. The review should go beyond formal organisations and include "front organisations", financial networks, youth groups and "ideological platforms" linked to the Brotherhood, the resolution says. The European Commission is also asked to provide a “comprehensive overview” of any cases in which EU funds have been awarded to associates of the Brotherhood. Experts and officials in Europe have for years been warning about the threat the Brotherhood poses to social cohesion and democracy. Analysts have also questioned the group's claims of non-violence. The parliament expressed “deep concern at the strategies of influence” pursued by the Brotherhood and its supporters. It described the Brotherhood as “a political project based on the primacy of religious norms over common law, which is incompatible with democratic principles, the rule of law and equality between citizens”. The Muslim Brotherhood is outlawed in several Middle East countries including the UAE , Saudi Arabia and Egypt . The US has designated certain branches of the movement, such as in Egypt and Jordan. Pressure has been increasing on the EU to take similar steps. The French parliament in January passed a resolution calling on the union to list the Brotherhood as a terrorist organisation. The European Parliament does not have independent decision-making power but can apply pressure to other EU institutions to take action. The parliament's largest party, the centre-right European People's Party, said the EU “must never fund Islamists”. “Islam as a faith and political Islam as an ideology must not be conflated. We must protect both democracy and religious freedom,” said one of its members of the parliament, Celine Imart. “Where rules allow, the Council [of the European Union] should list individuals and organisations linked to the Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist entities.”

title: Nicolas Maduro and wife charged with torturing US citizens in new indictment
description: Former Venezuelan leader and spouse accused of presiding over 'system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition'
content: Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores were charged with conspiring to torture US citizens and others in a new indictment released on Thursday. Mr Maduro, who served as Venezuela 's president for about 13 years, and his wife were captured by US soldiers from the presidential compound in Caracas in early January, after they were indicted by Washington on drugs and weapons charges. Ms Flores was expected to appear in court on Thursday. The new indictment accuses Mr Maduro and Ms Flores of presiding over “a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention and the torture of detainees”. “That torture included electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells and psychological torture, such as threats to harm and kill victims’ families, including children,” it said. Victims of their alleged abuse included US citizens “believed to pose a threat” to Mr Maduro. “One particular United States citizen was detained in Venezuela and subjected to, among other things, deprivation of food and water, simulated drowning, repeated beatings, electric shock to his testicles and forced injections,” the indictment said. The former Venezuelan president and his wife have been in custody awaiting trial in New York in the months since their capture. Both pleaded not guilty to the original indictment against them , under which they are accused of narco-terrorism, conspiracy to import cocaine, and possession of machine guns and destructive devices. Mr Maduro came to power in Venezuela in 2013, after the death of long-time leader Hugo Chavez. During his time in office, critics accused him and his administration of political repression, corruption and criminal activity, amid the country's economic collapse.

title: UN Security Council extends arms embargo in Sudan's Darfur as US pushes for nationwide ban
description: China and Russia want to keep the sanctions confined to the region
content: The UN Security Council unanimously voted on Thursday to extend an arms embargo on Sudan ’s Darfur region until December 11, buying time for negotiations over a US proposal to widen the restrictions to the entire country. The short extension highlighted disagreements over how to stop weapons from reaching those fighting in Sudan’s civil war, now in its fourth year. Washington has pushed for a nationwide embargo, while China, Russia and other council members want to keep the sanctions confined to Darfur. Although the embargo has failed to stop weapons reaching Darfur, it allows UN experts to investigate arms shipments and identify those responsible for breaches, paving the way for any further sanctions. Massad Boulos , US senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, said in a social media statement that Washington agreed to the short extension after consultations with its Quad partners, allies and Security Council members, to give diplomatic efforts more time to secure a negotiated settlement, humanitarian truce and lasting ceasefire. “This extension is not a lapse in our resolve,” he said, adding that the US remained committed to expanding the embargo across Sudan to protect civilians from increasingly sophisticated weapons, including drones. “External military support to the warring parties must end,” he added, warning that continued weapons supplies were prolonging the conflict, undermining diplomatic efforts and worsening the humanitarian crisis. Mr Boulos proposed expanding the embargo in August. Working with Mike Waltz, Washington’s ambassador to the UN, he sought to increase pressure on the warring Sudanese Armed Forces and paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. “The United States has presented a resolution to the Security Council that would expand the arms embargo nationwide, making clear that sanctions and member state implementation of those rules apply to all the networks keeping this war alive on both sides, with no carve-outs,” Mr Boulos and Mr Waltz wrote in an opinion piece for Foreign Policy in September. The two said that nationwide restrictions would take aim at arms traffickers, financiers, mercenary recruiters and drone suppliers. But the proposal met resistance from China and Russia, which hold veto power, as well as the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Liberia, Somalia and Pakistan. Tension between Washington and Khartoum increased after the US reportedly withheld a visa for Gen Abdel Fattah Al Burhan, head of the Sudanese Armed Forces, before his scheduled UN General Assembly address last month. Reuters reported that the decision appeared to be linked to his resistance to a US-backed ceasefire plan. Sudan has claimed it did not reject the US ceasefire proposal but instead submitted comments on it. US State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said last month that neither the SAF nor the RSF represented a legitimate constitutional government for Sudan.

title: UK must remain in Jerusalem 'at all costs', says former diplomat
description: Opportunity to renegotiate mission status could arise after Israeli election, says Sir Vincent Fean
content: The UK should keep a diplomatic presence in Jerusalem at all costs to prevent Israeli claims to the disputed city, a former British diplomat has said. Sir Vincent Fean, who served as British Consul General in Jerusalem , said the UK’s historic presence in Jerusalem was critical to maintaining British policy that views the city as a shared capital. It has held a mission in the city for 200 years. He spoke to The National after Israel announced the closure of the Consulate General in Jerusalem, with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband responding that the building would remain open as a mission. Israel used different wording, saying the building would house a British government-operated task force. “Their scope of activity will be very limited,” Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said. The downgrade in status follows a dispute over British trade sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Avoiding full closure of the consulate allows the two allies to continue talks and minimises the risk of a permanent rupture amid intense domestic debate over the relationship in both countries. In recent days, there have been suggestions Britain was prepared ⁠to consider ejecting Israeli diplomats if the mission were ‌closed. “It will be known as the UK mission. It doesn’t really matter. What matters is that the mission is in Jerusalem,” Mr Fean told The National. “If it's not there it will be very hard to get it back. One of the Israeli aims is to ensure any future embassy is in Ramallah [in the West Bank]. British officials could be seen leaving the building on Thursday, as all but seven staff members were made to move by the Israeli government to the embassy in Tel Aviv. Workers removed ​signs ​and plaques from the walls overnight. The decision came after weeks of negotiations, which may have continued until late on Wednesday when the Israeli decision was announced. Mr Saar acknowledged the building was UK property, which prevented the Israeli government from seizing control of it and expelling all the diplomats. The UK first established a Consulate General in 1838, 110 years before the state of Israel was declared, and has been operating from the building in Sheikh Jarrah in East Jerusalem since 1965. It is thought Mr Miliband could be buying time until after the Israel elections at the end of this month, before resuming talks with what could potentially be a new government, Mr Fean said. “There is a time factor, which is October 27 and the Israeli elections. That could mean a different set of interlocutors,” he added. Both Downing Street and the Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) were involved in the negotiations leading up to Thursday, with UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell visiting Jerusalem last week. The Israeli decision was “unlawful and disproportionate”, Mr Fean said. “Israel is taking it out in essence on Palestinians and British nationals, rather than on bilateral relations between Israeli and the UK.” Concerns have been raised about the implications for consular services for British citizens and Palestinians, but the visa service is expected to remain “intact”, with an office in Ramallah that does not have diplomatic status, Mr Fean said. But some British charities have raised concerns over the potential impact on their ability to deliver aid in the Palestinian territories. “The British Consulate General is a lifeline,” said Aseel Baidoun of Medical Aid for Palestinians. “It is the UK's main channel to Palestinians in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza. “It is essential for enabling close co-ordination with humanitarian and health organisations working there, including Medical Aid for Palestinians. Downgrading the Consulate General will reduce the UK's ability to protect Palestinian civilians, support aid delivery and uphold international law at the very moment these are most needed,” she told The National. “Israel's closure order was retaliation for the UK taking lawful action against illegal settlements. The UK should make clear that it will not reward attempts to entrench Israel's annexation of East Jerusalem.” Last week, Dominic Grieve KC, who was the government’s senior legal adviser from 2010 to 2014, said the closure was “an unlawful assertion of Israeli sovereignty over occupied East Jerusalem ”. He wrote to the FCDO to argue Israel was furthering its agenda to annex East Jerusalem by closing the British consulate.

title: Highly anticipated Palestinian elections likely to be postponed, sources say
description: Decision expected shortly on whether the first Legislative Council election in 20 years will go ahead as scheduled on November 28
content: Discussions are continuing to postpone next month's highly anticipated Palestinian legislative elections , sources told The National on Thursday, with a decision expected in the coming days. The last election for the Palestinian Legislative Council was held in 2006 and won by Hamas , leading to the rift between the group and the ruling Fatah party. Fatah leader and Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas , who was elected in 2005, has overstayed his term by 17 years and now rules by decree. The PA has faced mounting pressure from Palestinians, the region and the West for internal reforms and presidential elections. Mr Abbas, 90, and his administration are widely regarded as corrupt and ineffective. The election of his son, Yasser, to Fatah's central committee this year has raised concerns that he was setting him up as his successor in a presidential election expected next year. Mr Abbas called off an attempt to hold a presidential election in 2021, which polls indicated he would probably lose, citing Israel 's refusal to allow Palestinian voters in occupied East Jerusalem to participate. The current conditions are even less conducive for elections after the devastation of Gaza by Israel in a war sparked by Hamas's October 2023 attacks, and the related increase in Israeli violence and settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank where the PA is based. Nevertheless, Mr Abbas publicly promised that 2026 would be the year for Palestinian democracy after EU threats to cut funding if he failed to comply with their demands for reforms. Election commission head Jamil Al Khalidi told Palestinian media this week that preparations were being made to hold elections in Gaza and the West Bank despite security, logistical and technical hurdles. He said alternatives to traditional ballot boxes and voting ink were being sourced, as Israel continues to block their entry into Gaza. It is unclear how Palestinians might react to a delay in the legislative elections, but many were already bracing for it, an August poll by the Palestinian Centre for Policy and Survey Research showed. Out of 1,270 respondents interviewed, 44 per cent said they did not believe the elections would take place as scheduled. The conditions of the postponement will be noteworthy, one of the sources told The National, given the EU's continued pressure for the vote to be held. Another source, who previously worked closely with Mr Abbas, said the Palestinian President was shortsighted and unlikely to have planned beyond postponing the vote. "He only thinks one step ahead. And he has absolutely no concept about the importance of public opinion," the source said.

title: UAE-backed GlobalFoundries and TSMC announce $2bn manufacturing agreement
description: New York-based GlobalFoundries to supply TSMC with silicon interposers
content: UAE -backed semiconductor manufacturer GlobalFoundries has announced a $2 billion deal with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company to bolster US chip manufacturing. GlobalFoundries , based in New York, said it would be supplying TSMC with silicon interposers, which help chips communicate on logic boards. The company's stock reacted positively to the news on Thursday, gaining 2.8 per cent to 49.44 per share. Interposers are increasingly important as artificial intelligence creates unprecedented demand for semiconductors. “Advanced packaging is becoming increasingly critical to delivering the performance, power efficiency and scale required for next-generation AI systems,” said Ed Kaste, a senior vice president at GlobalFoundries . “By providing manufacturing services using GlobalFoundries' trusted US manufacturing footprint, we are creating a secure, scalable source of essential advanced-packaging elements that will help customers accelerate innovation and strengthen the semiconductor supply chain.” GlobalFoundries said large-scale production of silicon interposers is expected at the start of 2028. “The agreement provides a foundation to expand capacity over time as customer demand grows,” the company's press release said. TSMC is one of the world's largest chip makers. Last year, President Donald Trump announced the Taiwan-based company would be investing at least $100 billion in the US to bolster manufacturing and research. Semiconductor manufacturing is fast becoming a major asset, as the US and China compete to exert influence in the AI sector. At the time of the announcement, Mr Trump said, alongside TSMC chief executive CC Wei: “This is a tremendous thing for our country and hopefully his company. The most powerful AI chips in the world will be built right here in America and it will be a big percentage of those chips made by his company.” GlobalFoundries is owned in part by Abu Dhabi’s sovereign fund, Mubadala Investment Company .

title: Elon Musk's Boring Company to explore tunnel projects in Abu Dhabi
description: Agreement comes as work continues on Dubai Loop
content: Elon Musk's Boring Company has signed an agreement to explore underground transport, utility tunnels and related infrastructure opportunities in Abu Dhabi . The deal with the Abu Dhabi Projects and Infrastructure Centre (Adpic) was signed during the Liveability and Investment (LIVEX) conference, the emirate's media office said on Thursday. “Abu Dhabi provides an ideal environment to explore the next generation of underground infrastructure solutions, supported by its ambitious growth vision and strong commitment to advanced technologies,” said Steve Davis, president of The Boring Company. “Through our collaboration with the Abu Dhabi Projects and Infrastructure Centre, we look forward to assessing how advanced tunnelling solutions can create new possibilities for transport and utilities, expand urban capacity more efficiently, and enable better use of available space.” Last month, The National reported how the Boring Company planned to to build 150km of tunnels in the Emirates after it raised $3 billion in a funding round, led by the UAE. Construction is under way on the Dubai Loop in May, a high-speed underground transport network aimed at cutting congestion in the city. The Dubai Loop, led by the government in partnership with The Boring Company – is expected to start operations within two years. “Infrastructure is one of the most important drivers of future opportunity, enabling cities to grow efficiently, strengthen connectivity and create lasting value for communities,” said Mohamed Ali Al Shorafa, chairman of the Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT). “As Abu Dhabi continues to evolve, we remain focused on exploring new approaches that can optimise the use of space, strengthen connectivity across the urban landscape and support sustainable urban growth in a way that meets the needs of future generations.” Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority said in February that the first phase of the Dubai Loop would cost Dh565 million ($153.8 million) and connect DIFC with Dubai Mall using autonomous Tesla cars. The first four stations will be at Burj Khalifa, DIFC 2, Zabeel Dubai Mall Parking and ICD Brookfield Place. The Dubai network will eventually cover 22km and comprise 19 stations. The estimated final cost is about Dh2 billion. “Our collaboration with The Boring Company provides an opportunity to explore advanced underground transportation and utility tunnel solutions, drawing on global expertise, technical innovation and international best practices to assess their potential role in supporting Abu Dhabi's future infrastructure requirements and development priorities,” said Maysarah Mahmoud Eid, director general of Adpic.

title: DP World signs 15-year concession for terminal at Bangladesh's Chittagong port
description: Deal expected to improve supply chain efficiency
content: Global ports operator DP World has signed a 15-year concession agreement with Bangladesh's Chittagong Port to operate a new terminal that is expected to boost economic activity in the South Asian nation. The public-private partnership deal for the New Mooring Container Terminal (NMCT) is anticipated to improve supply chain efficiency and strengthen Bangladesh’s trade and logistics capabilities, the Dubai company said in a statement on Thursday. Under the agreement, which also includes the operation of the overflow container yard, the NMCT will remain under the ownership of the Chittagong Port Authority. DP World did not disclose the value of its investment in the project. The partnership will allow the NMCT to tap into DP World's global network, which includes ports, infrastructure and supply chain services, DP World executive chairman Essa Kazim said. “Bangladesh is an increasingly important trading and manufacturing economy, and we are committed to supporting its continued development,” he added. The collaboration builds on an initial pact signed between the Dubai government and the Public-Private Partnership Authority under the Bangladesh Prime Minister's Office, aimed at advancing strategic infrastructure development through PPP initiatives. The development plan includes upgrades to the terminal’s civil and equipment infrastructure, use of digital solutions and operational enhancements to improve cargo handling efficiency and growing trade volumes. Working with the Chittagong Port Authority, DP World will focus on key operational areas including berth planning, yard management, equipment utilisation, preventive maintenance, safety and sustainability, it said. The partnership is expected to support local workforce development and the introduction of international operating practices. “By supporting domestic industry and facilitating more efficient trade flows, the partnership [with DP World] will strengthen Bangladesh's position in regional and global supply chains while creating a stronger platform for investment and long-term economic growth,” said SM Moniruzzaman, chairman of the Chittagong Port Authority. DP World has a global handling capacity of 110 million 20-foot-equivalent units and is responsible for the movement of 10 per cent of global daily trade, according to its website. It has invested about $10 billion in a logistics network that now spans 85 countries. The company is aggressively expanding internationally. Its latest ventures include investing $90 million to upgrade Angola's Port of Luanda and exploring two major port and economic zone projects in Nigeria .

title: Ex-prince Andrew search warrants quashed after police accept legal error
description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested on his 66th birthday on suspicion of misconduct in public office
content: British police on Thursday said ​that ​search warrants ​it secured to ⁠search properties linked to King ⁠Charles's younger brother Andrew ​Mountbatten-Windsor had been incorrectly granted and must be quashed. The former prince was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office in February and searches were ⁠carried out at properties in Sandringham ⁠and Windsor. However, Mr Mountbatten-Windsor ‌applied for the search warrants to be ​quashed and Thames Valley Police said it accepted that they had not been properly granted. “We accept the position that the initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect and therefore these must be legally quashed,” a Thames Valley Police spokesperson said. “Legal proceedings are currently ongoing to decide how material seized during the searches will ​be managed and whether we ‌can lawfully retain ⁠it in support ​of our ongoing investigation.” The force said the criminal ​investigation ‌which began after the release of millions of ⁠documents by the US Department of Justice relating ⁠to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was continuing. Andrew, the second son of the late Queen Elizabeth, has denied any ​wrongdoing in relation to Epstein and said he regretted their friendship.

title: UAE worshippers gather to hold rain prayers on Friday
description: Salaat Al Istisqaa to be performed half an hour before the Jumuah prayers
content: President Sheikh Mohamed has called on UAE residents to perform Salaat Al Istisqaa , the Islamic prayer for rain. This special congregational prayer will be held at mosques across the UAE on Friday. Worshippers are encouraged to join in to seek divine mercy and blessings for the country. The prayer will begin half an hour before the weekly Jumuah prayers at 12.45pm. This year, the UAE witnessed scattered rains, but most areas remained dry. Additional rainfall plays a key role in agriculture, helping farmers grow healthy crops in tough conditions. The level of rainfall is declining in across part of the Middle East. Throughout most of 2025, cumulative rainfall in the UAE was significantly below average , about 38 per cent less than the historical baseline and nearly three times lower than in 2024. Salaat Al Istisqaa involves some of the practices, teachings and traditions of the Prophet Mohammed that Muslims are encouraged to follow. There is no adhan, or call to prayer, and no iqamah for this special prayer. Those who arrive early may perform voluntary prayers, or nawafil, before or after Salaat Al Istisqaa. After completing the two-rak'ah prayer with the Salam, the imam delivers a sermon while standing on the ground instead of ascending the pulpit, as an expression of humility before Allah. At the end of the second sermon, the imam faces the qibla, the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah , and raises his hands in supplication, asking Allah to send rain to the people and the land. A distinctive tradition of Salaat Al Istisqaa is the turning of the imam’s cloak. At the end of the second sermon, the imam turns his cloak inside out in a gesture symbolising the hope that Allah will transform hardship into ease and bring rain after drought. The imam then raises his hands and offers supplication for rain and divine mercy. The prayer coincides with a forecast of possible rainfall in the coming days. Dr Ahmed Habib, a meteorologist at the National Centre of Meteorology, told The National scattered rainfall could develop in parts of the country. The likelihood of rain is expected to increase over the weekend and into early next week, with Saturday, Sunday and Tuesday highlighted for possible showers. However, rainfall is expected to remain localised rather than widespread. Some areas may experience moderate or heavy showers, while others may remain dry. The developing weather pattern may create further opportunities for rainfall throughout the month.

title: Making e-scooters safe requires more than fines and enforcement
description: Safety compliance and education will be key to beating back the rising tide of accidents
content: Dubai Police said this week it had seized hundreds of e-scooters and e-bikes for a variety of traffic offences during a road safety drive in one of the emirate’s neighbourhoods. It is the latest action taken to tackle unsafe use of so-called last-mile vehicles. The same authority said last month that it had confiscated more than 13,000 e-scooters since the beginning of the year for dangerous riding, such as speeding. The authorities noted that accidents, incidents and injuries have risen. Abu Dhabi has this year also issued warnings about improper use of such vehicles, as well as disseminating public safety information videos. There has not been a nationwide “census” conducted regarding the volume of e-scooters in active use in the country – nor does there need to be one – but e-bikes and e-scooters are now a ubiquitous presence on neighbourhood roads and cycle path networks, helping reduce congestion and pollution in the process. What is becoming obvious is that more scooters and more journeys means, in all likelihood, the potential for more accidents and incidents. The National reported earlier this year that Ministry of Interior data showed significant e-scooter accidents had increased by 97 per cent last year, from 61 cases to 120. Despite the rapid rise in the headline number, the overall figure is still low. That, of course, provides no comfort to anyone or any family that has been affected by one of those serious accidents. It is in all of our interests to reduce the number of significant incidents to zero, while also recognising we are not sat in the middle of a contagion-level event. Statistical models produced elsewhere in the world suggest every 100,000 e-scooter rides might result in between 10 and 20 accidents requiring medical support or intervention. A significant contributory factor to that global modelling is alcohol intoxication by the e-scooter user, which may be less of a determinant in this region. World Health Organisation figures also report that road traffic injuries of all forms tend to disproportionately affect young people. Globally, unintentional injury, such as that resulting from vehicle collision, is the leading cause of death for people under 30. The rules for e-scooters say riders must be at least 16 years old and wear a helmet when using one. The maximum speed permitted by one of those vehicles is 20 kph. Riders are also required to keep a safe distance from pedestrians, are not allowed to carry passengers or use mobile phones while using them. Reflective clothing is also advised, and any vehicle is meant to be equipped with front and rear lights. Authorities have said they would take action against riders who cross roads dangerously, weave between lanes or ride outside demarcated or approved zones. Improper use leads to confiscation and fines. Anecdotally, if it is not controversial to say that most road users will have seen an e-scooter rider breach at least one of those rules in day-to-day life. A counter-argument would also say that most drivers break road rules on their daily drives, whether that is speeding, distracted driving , tailgating or another form of anti-social or potentially reckless behaviour. Few drivers are the paragons of road-using virtue that we may think we are and only a small number of drivers willingly identify themselves as “bad” even if their fellow road users might absolutely attest that they are. It is down to every road user to take a higher level of personal responsibility to keep the roads safe. So, how can we realistically reach a state of accident-free nirvana? Education and awareness are key to beating back the rising tide rather than enforcement with last-mile vehicles. Only the utterly rules-driven among us would advocate for round-the-clock and always-visible enforcement of regulations regarding e-scooters, which would be a drain on resources that could not be justified by the thankfully low volume of incidents and accidents. Each time authorities share video footage of e-scooter misuse, however, it will help subtly change behaviour and attitudes towards risk. Road safety campaigns elsewhere in the world on the dangers of driving while intoxicated or failing to use seat belts or child seats have helped change habits and save lives over a prolonged period. Campaigns by Abu Dhabi Police to highlight the dangers of rubber-necking , tailgating and speeding have garnered widespread attention and, inevitably, offer pause for individual reflection and thought. Dubai has set up a unit in relation to e-scooter use to help education and improve safety. All of these things will help. There is also the question of performance-limiters. E-bikes are typically able to achieve limits far in excess of the permitted maximums for the path network, much in the same way as performance cars have the potential to be driven at more than double the speed permitted on the nation’s motorways. While speed limiters are also common in both performance cars and e-bikes, software has the potential to be overridden. Awareness campaigns about the dangers of speeding and the increased risk of injury to the e-scooter user or pedestrians are the best defence in such circumstances. The drip-drip of persistent messaging does increase the likelihood of bringing about behavioural change and keeping our path and road network safe.

title: Nine Syrians missing after cargo ship sunk by drone in Black Sea
description: Syria asks why search and rescue operations were called off following suspected Russian attack
content: Nine sailors from Syria and one from Egypt are missing after a cargo ship was sunk in the Black Sea, with search-and-rescue operations called off. The Turkish-owned Alfa Watan was hit by a drone off the Bulgarian coast on Tuesday. Russia is suspected of involvement in the latest of several such incidents during the war in Ukraine . Bulgaria said there were “no traces” of the 10 crew members and called off the search on Wednesday. A second ship was damaged on the same day as the Alfa Watan, with all its crew rescued. Syria on Thursday called for an investigation by Bulgaria and the International Maritime Organisation. Mazen Aloush, a director at the Syrian General Authority for Ports and Customs, said it should examine why the search for the Alfa Watan crew was called off before their fate was determined. He said “all available technical means” should be used to reach the wreck and determine what happened. “The file should not be closed before exhausting all available possibilities,” Syrian state media quoted him as saying. Vice Admiral Rumen Nikolov of Bulgaria's Maritime Administration Executive Agency had said a boat, ​three life rafts and parts of the ship's equipment were found before the Alfa Watan search was called off. It was not certain who carried out the attack, which took place off the coastal town of Byala in eastern Bulgaria, but there are growing concerns about attacks by Russia on European Union and Nato countries. “If we look at the nature of the cargo and the direction in which the ships were moving, then logically speaking the result argues in favour of Russia,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev said after a meeting of Bulgaria's National Security Council on Wednesday. “But that does not mean that we can claim that the strike was carried out by Russia without having evidence.” The Russian embassy in Sofia denied involvement, saying the merchant ship was not among targets hit by Russian drones on Tuesday. Ukrainian ⁠President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia and said his country's forces were not operating in that area. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said the country would invite its Black Sea neighbours Turkey ⁠and Romania for talks on protecting shipping. It may ⁠also ask Nato allies to deploy “additional air and maritime surveillance capabilities and counter-drone systems”, she said. Nato member Bulgaria does not border Russia or Ukraine but lies on the Black Sea, where both countries have major ports and shipping has been caught in the conflict. The ⁠drone attack follows an incident in which Romanian authorities said on Monday two people had died in a fire on a ship in the Black Sea. It also comes in the wake of drone incidents in Poland and Romania, raising fears that Russia is testing Nato's defence posture without waging full-scale war against its members.

title: EU and GCC to strengthen relations at leaders' summit in Riyadh
description: Europeans want to showcase bloc as reliable and long-term partner for Gulf
content: The European Union hopes to deepen security and energy relations with Gulf countries at the second leaders' summit in Riyadh next month. Since the start of the Iran war on February 28, Europe has cast itself as a solid ally to the Gulf , despite being unable to match superior US military capabilities. “In the current geopolitical context, there is an opportunity for deeper and more ambitious EU-GCC partnerships,” European Council President Antonio Costa said in a letter of invitation to Gulf and EU leaders dated Tuesday and seen by The National . As the closest neighbours geographically, with long historical and cultural ties, and recognising the growing shared challenges we face, I propose that our discussions will focus on key regional issues,” Mr Costa, who will co-chair the summit with Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman, wrote. He called for strengthening co-operation in priority areas such as “peace and security, connectivity, trade, economic co-operation, energy and mobility”. The Houthi- Saudi Arabia conflict escalated on Wednesday, with three people killed in attacks by the Yemeni rebels on airports in the kingdom, disrupting flights. Following a major escalation of the Houthi offensive last month, in which the Iran-backed group seized key energy and maritime infrastructure, France and the UK – which is not an EU member – were among the first to send Riyadh military support, including fighter jet-refuelling capabilities and defence systems. This week, Turkey and Pakistan , which signed a defence agreement with Saudi Arabia, said they would send troops. The US, historically a key Saudi ally, has been notably absent from announcements of military aid. The physical presence of the EU's 27 leaders in Riyadh for the EU-GCC Summit on October 24 is likely to represent an important signal of support to Saudi Arabia and more widely to Gulf states affected by regional instability. Early in the war, France and Italy sent air-defence systems to the UAE to help it fend off Iranian drone and missile attacks. “The Riyadh summit can showcase the EU as a reliable and long-term partner to the Gulf countries and unlock shared opportunities,” Mr Costa said in the letter. Cinzia Bianco, a research fellow on Europe and the Gulf at the European Council on Foreign Relations, told The National that Europe's backing did not mean pivoting away from the US. “Europe can offer different things,” Ms Bianco said. “It is about a strategic partnership maturing and showing concrete defensive support is only your entrance ticket, in a way.” The previous EU-GCC Summit took place in Brussels in 2024 and was the first since the signing of the initial EU-GCC co-operation agreement in 1989. The EU is the second-biggest trading partner of the GCC countries: the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar. The European Commission said that over the past decade, EU-GCC trade has increased by about 30 per cent, with imports growing about 54 per cent and exports 20 per cent. The key traded good is fuel, accounting for more than 75 per cent of the EU’s imports from GCC countries. In a joint statement issued on Wednesday, nine Southern Mediterranean EU leaders said the summit would provide an opportunity to “strengthen engagement with Gulf partners on regional peace, security and prosperity”. “The EU should continue to work closely with Gulf partners and other partners in the region, using its diplomatic, economic, humanitarian and security instruments to support regional co-operation and peacebuilding,” they said. Kaja Kallas, the EU's foreign affairs and security policy chief, has been pushing for months to strengthen Aspides, the bloc's defensive maritime mission. Aspides' mandate covers a wide area including the Bab Al Mandeb strait, the Strait of Hormuz and international waters in the Red Sea. It is currently operating in the Red Sea. “The mandate covers also Hormuz but it needs to be activated, including with more ships,” Ms Bianco said. “This is already happening, to get to the summit in Riyadh in a more credible position.” Ms Kallas' efforts have been backed by Italy, which recently complained in a letter to her that other EU nations were not being supportive enough and suggested they contribute financially instead. Italy and France both have one frigate deployed to the mission, which is under Greek strategic command. Speaking last month in Brussels, Ms Kallas said the quality of vessels was as important as their number. “For example, Aspides does not have a minehunting mandate, which means that you need frigates, you need air-defence support, you need vessels that can do the escorting of the ships,” she said.

title: Barcelona hero Pedro calls time on remarkable career 'having lived my dream'
description: The 39-year-old played more than 900 matches in Spain, England and Italy, while also winning the World Cup and European Championships with his country
content: So little was known of Barcelona ’s Pedro at the start of his breakthrough 2009-10 season that one respected British website listed him as four different people. The son of a petrol station worker from Tenerife’s capital Santa Cruz, Pedro Rodriguez Ledesma’s 23 goals from 52 games were shared between ‘Pedro’, ‘Pedrito’, ‘Rodriguez’ and ‘Ledesma’. Those goals were often crucial and when Pedro scored in the Fifa Club World Cup in 2009, he became the first to score in six different club competitions in one season. Seven months later, he was a World Cup winner with Spain. “I can’t believe what’s happened,” he said at the end of the 2009-10 season. He was a character – as was noted during Barca’s title celebrations. As the victors took to the microphone and shouted “Forever Barca, Forever Catalunya”, Pedro stepped up and hollered “Forever Barca, Forever Tenerife!” Even the most earnest Catalans laughed. “In 12 months I established myself a regular for Barca,” he says. “I’d only played eight first team league games before last season – though I did come on in the 2009 Champions League final against Manchester [United]. In 2009-10, we won the league with Barca again and I was selected for Spain. Then Spain won the World Cup. Incredible – it was beyond a dream.” Pedro became a World Cup winner just six weeks after making his Spain debut. “I played against Saudi Arabia in May,” he explains, “then scored my first goal a week later. I played in five World Cup games.” Being one of seven Barca men in the Spain squad, most of whom were regular starters in South Africa, also helped. Sixteen years on and there’s no confusion about who Pedro is. After 776 first-team matches for Barcelona, Chelsea, Roma and then their deadly rivals Lazio, plus another 65 for Spain, he’s calling it a day. Along the way he won 25 trophies including one World Cup, one European Championship, three Uefa Champions Leagues, five La Liga titles and one Premier League. On Thursday, he visited Camp Nou, scene of most of those triumphs. On Friday, he held a press conference to announce his retirement. It was met with lavish praise for a fine career. Early on he put much of his success down to Barça’s youth academy, which included a season under Luis Enrique for Barca B. “The club have a very clear idea of how we should play football,” he said. “Receive, pass, move. Learn to do this very quickly and you have an advantage. “We also have role models in front of us. I could see players like Xavi and [Andres] Iniesta, they could see players like El Mister [Pep Guardiola]. Youth gets a chance here.” Opinion was long divided on the best position for the two-footed winger. “I can play on both sides, but I play more on the left so I’d have to say that,” he said. “As for my feet, I use my right more. I tend to score twice as many goals with my right as my left.” Pedro was fortunate in that he entered the best team in the world and played alongside its greatest player, Lionel Messi. “Messi is the best player in the world, we all know that,” he said. “The skills he has, his pace and vision, they make it impossible for defenders. But the best thing about Barca is that we’re a team. We work for each other, not for ourselves and we have great players in every position”. Pedro’s footballing education allowed him to thrive wherever he went. Manchester United wanted to sign him but he went instead to Chelsea in 2015 after 321 games for the Catalans. At Stamford Bridge, he learnt English and celebrated the League title and FA Cup. He also averaged 45 games per season in his first four years in London, the mark of a player seldom injured. He played more than 50 club games in four different seasons at Barcelona. After 206 Chelsea games he moved to Rome, first for 40 games in a season at Roma, then five full seasons at Lazio where he again averaged more than 40 club games per season. As recently as 2024-25, when he was 37, he still scored 14 goals, including Lazio’s goal of the year. Pedro is 39 but the stats don’t tell the full story since his games for Barca B aren’t counted, yet in more than 100 games for Barcelona’s junior sides he was playing against the first teams of clubs such as Real Betis and Zaragoza as a full professional. In total, Pedro played an astonishing 902 club games and scored 215 goals, plus another 65 goals and 17 games for Spain. He played his last game for Spain almost a decade ago and courted rare controversy when he said his role as a substitute during Euro 2016 was not worth his time, a rare, outspoken comment for this always loyal and unselfish servant. “I feel that the time has come,” he said as he retired. “The time to take a step forward and begin a new stage in my life. I leave proud of having lived my dream and of all the people who were by my side to make it come true. Thank you, football, for making me so happy”.

title: EU to establish training and support mission for Lebanese army
description: Foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas insists mission will not be Unifil replacement
content: The European Union will establish a mission to support and train the underfunded Lebanese Armed Forces , the bloc's foreign affairs chief said on Thursday. Kaja Kallas, who was visiting Beirut, said the mission was not a replacement for the UN's peacekeeping mission in south Lebanon (Unifil), whose mandate is set to expire at the end of the year. “It will advise and assist the LAF and Internal Security Forces to strengthen territorial control, border security and also internal security,” she said, alongside Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi. “It's not the Unifil replacement and it will not only focus on southern Lebanon,” Ms Kallas added, saying a continued UN presence remained under discussion. The mission is expected to be formally established on October 12 at a meeting of EU foreign ministers, after a formal invitation from Lebanese authorities. The EU already provides financial, humanitarian and security assistance to Lebanon through a €1 billion ($1.12 billion) support package covering 2024 to 2027. There are fears of a security vacuum in south Lebanon – where Israel occupies about 65 towns and villages and Hezbollah continues to hold influence – as the UN mission prepares to withdraw with no successor formally announced. There have been suggestions that EU member states France and Italy could play a role. “We remain ready to work with Lebanon and UN Security Council members on what comes next,” Ms Kallas said. “There cannot be a security vacuum when Unifil leaves. Lebanon must have full control of its whole territory. That also means moving towards the disarmament of Hezbollah,” she added. Any international force must have a UN mandate, she said. The LAF, which is severely underfunded and relies on international donors, has sought to expand its presence in south Lebanon but has faced intense difficulties amid the latest Israeli occupation. Hezbollah's military arsenal and continued support in parts of Lebanon have raised fears of internal discord or even civil war should disarmament be done by force, amid pressure from the US and Israel to take a firmer stance. Israel's latest war on Lebanon , which was renewed again March against the backdrop of hostilities against Iran, has killed more than 4,300 Lebanese people and led to the destruction of a large number of border towns and villages. It came after Hezbollah fired rockets at Israel following the killing of Iran's supreme leader. Ms Kallas is on a two-day trip to Lebanon, where she also met with President Joseph Aoun among others.

title: Why Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Canadian poet and classical scholar recognised for her work drawing on ancient Greek literature
content: Canadian poet Anne Carson has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature, with the Swedish Academy recognising her experimental approach to writing and her ability to bring ancient Greek literature into the modern world. The 76-year-old author , whose best-known works include Autobiography of Red , The Beauty of the Husband and Nox , was announced as this year's laureate on Thursday. The academy awarded Carson the prize “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature”. Anders Olsson, chairman of the Nobel Committee for Literature, said Carson's achievement lay in her ability to combine classical scholarship with poetry, fiction and other literary forms. “Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning,” he said during the announcement. Carson has spent four decades drawing on ancient mythology, poetry and philosophy to explore love, grief, desire and identity. Her books frequently combine poetry with fiction, essays, translation and visual art, challenging conventional distinctions between literary forms. Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy, said she had reached Carson by telephone shortly before the announcement. The writer was in Iceland, where she had been “listening to the wind”. “She was taken by surprise, but very happy. I can hear that in her voice,” Carlberg said. Carson succeeds Hungarian novelist Laszlo Krasznahorkai , who won the prize in 2025, and South Korean author Han Kang , the 2024 recipient. The award carries a prize of 12 million Swedish kronor (approximately $1.2 million) and will be presented in Stockholm on December 10. Born in Toronto in 1950, Carson developed an interest in ancient Greek literature while at secondary school, where a Latin teacher began teaching her Greek during lunch breaks. She went on to study classics at the University of Toronto, earning a doctorate in 1981, and subsequently taught at universities across Canada and the United States, including McGill University and the University of Michigan. Carson has also translated major ancient Greek writers, including Sappho, Sophocles and Euripides, while reimagining their stories in her own work. Her previous honours include a MacArthur Fellowship in 2000, the TS Eliot Prize in 2001 and Spain's Princess of Asturias Award for Literature in 2020. She has also won the Griffin Poetry Prize twice, in 2001 and 2014. Among the works highlighted by the Nobel Committee was The Glass Essay (1995), a long poem about a woman recovering from a failed relationship who visits her mother in the moorlands, bringing with her the writings of Emily Bronte. Olsson said the work demonstrated Carson's ability to combine poetry, storytelling and literary criticism, with the narrator's experiences becoming entwined with those of her mother and Bronte. “The poetry needs the story, and the story is in turn given energy by the leaps and scene shifts of poetry,” he said. One of Carson's most acclaimed works is Autobiography of Red (1998), a novel written in verse that reimagines the ancient Greek myth of Geryon, a monster killed by the hero Herakles. Carson transforms Geryon into a young man with red wings, following his journey through adolescence, heartbreak and self-discovery. The book combines a contemporary coming-of-age story with the fantastic imagery of classical mythology. Olsson praised Carson's “extraordinary ability to give the classical literary tradition an intensely contemporary feel”, highlighting her use of modern language and experiences to reinterpret ancient stories. He also recalled that Carson had once described boredom as her greatest enemy, saying she confronted it with “drastic humour and wit”. She followed Autobiography of Red with The Beauty of the Husband (2001), subtitled A Fictional Essay in 29 Tangos . The book follows a woman reflecting on her marriage to an unfaithful husband, with each of its 29 sections opening with lines from the Romantic poet John Keats. Olsson described the work as a confrontation between Keats's ideas about beauty and the painful realities of a deteriorating marriage. The book won Carson the 2001 TS Eliot Prize, making her the first woman to receive the British poetry award. Grief became the subject of Nox (2010), created following the death of Carson's brother Michael. The book is presented as an accordion-folding collection of photographs, letters, drawings and poetry, drawing on an elegy by the ancient Roman writer Catullus, who also mourned the death of his brother. Olsson described Nox as “a creation as sculptural as it is literary”, highlighting how Carson uses the physical form of the book to examine memory and loss. Her engagement with Greek tragedy also produced Antigonick (2012), an illustrated reworking of Sophocles' Antigone , while Red Doc> (2013) returned to the characters of Autobiography of Red as adults. Carson's most recent collection, Wrong Norma (2024), contains 25 pieces of poetic prose accompanied by her own artwork. It was a finalist for the 2024 National Book Award for Poetry and won the National Book Critics Circle Award for Poetry in 2025. Olsson said Carson's influence extended beyond literature through collaborations with visual artists, choreographers and theatre directors. “This demonstrates the freedom with which she relates to literary expectations and rule systems,” he said, describing her work as an important influence on international art and literature since the 1990s.

title: Diplomacy or war? US-Iran deadlock reaches fork in the road
description: Washington and Tehran continue to exchange messages through regional mediators, but both capitals are weighing up further military action
content: Communication channels between the US and Iran remain open, with new messages exchanged through mediators, five diplomats and sources have told The National , as efforts to reach a lasting agreement to end the seven-month-old war remain elusive. The push to establish a fresh diplomatic path following the failure to achieve a breakthrough in New York during the UN General Assembly last month is unfolding against a backdrop of growing signs that both sides are bracing for a major confrontation. Last week, a source in Tehran told The National that Iran was preparing for a “major round of fighting”. Days later, US media reports suggested that the administration of US President Donald Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, and that the Pentagon had ordered preparations for possible major combat operations. Gulf and Pakistani diplomatic sources said Qatar and Pakistan remain engaged in diplomacy with both sides, seeking to bring Washington and Tehran back to the negotiating table. “We remain engaged,” said a Pakistani diplomatic source. “Behind the scenes, negotiations are still happening, messages are being passed and engagement is continuing.” Qatar and Pakistan have been acting as key intermediaries in the conflict, which erupted following US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. The two countries helped facilitate a settlement and brokered a provisional truce agreement in June that quickly fell apart. The war in the Middle East has jolted global energy markets and fuelled inflation. Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Mr Trump rejected Tehran’s latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterm elections. “After Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned from New York, all diplomatic channels were effectively closed,” said an Iranian source with direct knowledge of the matter. “This was one of the reasons behind the unusually strong warnings subsequently issued by Iran’s armed forces and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps [IRGC] regarding any further attack.” But a source close to Iranian negotiators said message exchanges have since resumed. “China has also occasionally played a role in trying to bring the two sides’ positions closer, at Washington’s request,” the source added. “The current exchange does not appear likely to produce meaningful results. The new US strategy is to continue exchanging messages while applying pressure intended to force Iran to submit to American demands. At the same time, Washington is mobilising for a third round of attacks against Iran.” On Thursday, Mr Araghchi said Iran is still reviewing Washington's ​response to ⁠its proposal under which ⁠the ​Strait ⁠of Hormuz ‌could ​be reopened within seven days, and could reply within days. "The ⁠diplomatic process is still continuing," he confirmed. Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said on Wednesday that Iran’s military could carry out further pre-emptive attacks if it deemed them necessary to deter future strikes. He also said the army had built up a large stockpile of newly developed offensive and defensive weapons, including missiles and drones, and was continuing to produce them. US officials have similarly refused to rule out further escalation after Washington sent a third aircraft carrier to the region. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said during a visit to Greece on Wednesday that Iran had missed multiple opportunities to reach a deal over its nuclear programme . Earlier, Vice President JD Vance stressed that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to meet Washington’s demands and end the war. On Tuesday, Qatar said that its mediation efforts between the US and Iran were ongoing, confirming that the two sides were exchanging messages and that Doha was still acting as a mediator. The comments came as Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni visited Doha and met Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim. “The visit was publicly presented as being focused on the fate of the missing Iranian pilots, but there has also been a broader diplomatic purpose behind it,” said one of the Iranian sources. Iran says three pilots were detained by Qatari forces after their military aircraft were downed in Qatar’s airspace in March. Doha has denied the claim, saying its search-and-rescue teams recovered the remains of one Iranian pilot and handed them over to Tehran. The latest diplomatic activity also coincided with a visit to Pakistan by UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, who called on the US and Iran to end the conflict and return to diplomacy. But the latest exchanges have yet to overcome fundamental differences over how a potential agreement should be structured. “The US is making demands of Iran, but the Americans are not providing the Iranians with any guarantees,” said a source in Tehran with knowledge of Iran’s position. “The Iranians want firm guarantees that cannot subsequently be reversed. “There is a strong internal struggle between the IRGC, the official diplomatic channels and Parliament. There is significant opposition to negotiations because talks with the Americans have been tried repeatedly in the past and have failed.”

title: Turkish mayor defects to Erdogan's party in opposition stronghold
description: Ruling party has never won election in Izmir but now controls city
content: The mayor of Turkey ’s most prominent opposition stronghold has defected to President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling party, in a move that prompted protests and criticism over the state of the country’s democracy. Mr Erdogan’s Justice and Development Party (AKP) has never won a mayoral election in Izmir, Turkey’s third largest city. It is widely seen as a bastion of secular opposition parties who reject the president’s brand of Islamist nationalism. But mayor Cemil Tugay joined the AKP in a ceremony on Wednesday, and in a short speech described the party as “protector of the defenceless.” Mr Erdogan said he would support Mr Tugay “with all our resources in the effort to serve Izmir.” Taking control of Izmir, a province home to 4.5 million people, is a major win for the Turkish President, whose party has long criticised the opposition’s governance of the key Aegean coast centre. It was “a new era” and “a fresh start for Izmir,” local AKP chief Bilal Saygili said in a post on X. The move is the most prominent of a spate of recent defections to the AKP, in what critics have described as efforts by the ruling party to maintain rule over city governance despite an overwhelming defeat in local elections in 2024. “What does this tell us about the state of Turkish democracy? Well, it tells us that it doesn't exist,” Berk Esen, an Istanbul-based political scientist, told The National. Following Mr Tugay’s move, more than 1,000 protesters took to the streets in Izmir chanting slogans criticising the move, but were met with security barricades and anti-riot police, AFP reported. Local professional groups said Mr Tugay no longer had legitimacy and had disrespected the electorate’s wishes. “At this point, what must be done is to step down from that office,” Izmir Bar Association said in a statement on social media. He has “betrayed the duty entrusted to him,” the medics’ association said. Nine people resigned as advisers to the municipal theatre, saying that Mr Tugay’s defection “disregards the will of Izmir’s people and our audience.” Mr Tugay had previously denied he was considering joining the AKP. His wife had told him she would divorce him and his mother that she would disown him if he did so, he told Turkish media in January. Despite this, his wife Oznur Tugay appeared alongside her husband and Mr Erdogan at Wednesday's ceremony. Mr Tugay had won the mayoralty in 2024 with 48.97 per cent of the vote for the Republican People’s Party (CHP). At the time, the CHP was Turkey’s main opposition party, but in May this year it was hit with a lawsuit that saw its leadership removed and replaced. That prompted the formation of another group, the New Party, which has since taken over as the country’s largest opposition force. Mr Tugay left the CHP following the May lawsuit but did not join the New Party and continued to serve as an independent mayor. Opposition parties retain control of the municipal council. Critics of Mr Erdogan’s AKP characterise the defection as part of a pressure campaign on Turkey’s political opposition, which has faced arrests, lawsuits and defections over the past two years. “Elections are losing their meaning and significance because even if the ruling party loses elections, it can figure out extra-legal, extra-constitutional ways of reversing the outcome of these elections – in other words, reversing opposition victories,” Mr Esen said. Mr Tugay is not the first provincial mayor to defect to the AKP. Last year Ozlem Cercioglu, the mayor of Aydin in western Turkey, resigned from the CHP and switched to the AKP. Tens of district-level mayors, a less senior position than a provincial mayor, have also defected, alongside two MPs. Other opposition officials have been arrested. Seven opposition provincial mayors have been arrested since the 2024 vote, six of whom are still in prison, according to a tally published yesterday by news website Oksijen . The most prominent case is Istanbul’s mayor Ekrem Imamoglu , who remains in prison following his arrest in March 2025. He denies wrongdoing in multiple corruption cases that are currently going through the courts. Twenty-nine district-level mayors have also been arrested, including 13 in Istanbul. Mr Tugay’s predecessor as mayor of Izmir, Tunc Soyer, who is currently also in prison on corruption-related charges, criticised the defection in a message written from the high-security facility where he is being held. “Do not bow your head, beautiful Izmir,” he wrote. The Turkish government denies political motives in any lawsuits and says the judicial system is independent.

title: What is Crazy Horse Paris? Famous French cabaret show to open in Dubai
description: The 75-year-old institution is bringing a permanent production to Palm Jumeirah, with performances adapted for local audiences
content: One of Paris's most famous cabaret shows is coming to Dubai, bringing its signature blend of dance, music, elaborate lighting and theatrical illusion to the Middle East for the first time. Crazy Horse Paris will open a permanent production at Zabeel Theatre in Jumeirah Zabeel Saray on Palm Jumeirah on November 12, with tickets starting at Dh400. Called The Dubai Edition , the show has been created specifically for the emirate, adapting the Parisian institution's distinctive performances to regional culture and customs. It will also be the only permanent Crazy Horse Paris production outside the French capital, where the cabaret has been entertaining audiences for 75 years. Featuring 18 international dancers, the Dubai show will combine choreography, visual projections, music and optical illusions in an intimate 200-seat venue. Founded in 1951 by French artist and entrepreneur Alain Bernardin, Crazy Horse Paris opened at 12 Avenue George V, close to the Champs-Elysees. Unlike traditional cabaret productions built around elaborate costumes, comedy and large ensemble performances, Crazy Horse became known for its sensual, highly stylised approach to dance. Its signature performances use carefully positioned lighting, shadows and projections to transform the dancers' bodies into part of the visual spectacle. The shows often feature artistic nudity, although the emphasis is on choreography, illusion and the interplay between light and movement rather than conventional striptease. Over the decades, Crazy Horse has become a fixture of Parisian nightlife, attracting international visitors and developing a reputation for combining glamour with experimental stagecraft. It has also collaborated with prominent figures from fashion, music and entertainment, including Beyonce, Christian Louboutin, Jean Paul Gaultier, Elie Saab, Dita Von Teese and Lisa from K-pop group Blackpink. While the original Paris production is known for its provocative performances, organisers say The Dubai Edition has been reimagined to reflect regional culture and customs. The production will retain Crazy Horse's signature visual techniques, including lighting effects, optical illusions and precisely choreographed routines, while introducing new elements created for its Dubai audience. The extent of the changes, including how the original show's more revealing performances will be adapted, has not yet been detailed. Under the artistic direction of Andree Deissenberg, chief creative and brand officer of Crazy Horse Paris, the production will feature 18 dancers selected from hundreds of international applicants. The performers underwent six months of specialised training in Paris before joining the Dubai cast. "With The Dubai Edition, our objective was to create a show that is immediately identifiable as Crazy Horse Paris while developing a production specifically conceived for Dubai," Deissenberg said. "It draws on our artistic heritage, visual language and creative precision, while introducing new elements adapted to the venue and its audience." The production will take place at Zabeel Theatre inside Jumeirah Zabeel Saray on Palm Jumeirah. The venue has been transformed into an intimate cabaret with seating for 200 guests, designed to bring audiences closer to the performers. The Dubai production is being operated by 111 Management, a hospitality group based in the emirate. There will be two experiences available each evening. The Show is a 90-minute performance featuring choreographed dance routines, visual effects, a DJ and a master of ceremonies. For those looking for a longer evening, The Show & Dinner combines the performance with a three-course dining experience over approximately three hours. The entertainment continues after the final performance with a DJ set. There is also a private Crazy Suite for groups of up to 14 guests, designed for celebrations and exclusive bookings. Crazy Horse Paris – The Dubai Edition opens on November 12, with performances scheduled daily. The show begins at 7pm, with doors opening at 6pm. The Show & Dinner experience begins at 9.30pm, with doors opening at 9pm. Tickets for The Show start at Dh400 while tickets for The Show & Dinner start at Dh900, with higher-priced categories offering premium seating and additional hospitality benefits for each. Admission is restricted to guests aged 21 and above.

title: Ethiopia and Eritrea edge closer to direct conflict as troops enter Tigray
description: Conflict monitor says Eritrea wants to stop Ethiopian federal forces reaching its border
content: Eritrean troops have crossed into Ethiopia 's Tigray region and come under fire from Ethiopian drones as they pushed south, a conflict monitor said. It is the clearest sign yet that Ethiopia's renewed internal troubles could spark a war between the two neighbours. Eritrean troops have crossed the border at the town of Zalambessa and headed for the road between Adigrat and Idaga Hamus, said Dr Jalale Getachew Birru, East Africa analyst at the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project (Acled). “Ethiopian National Defence Forces drones targeted Eritrean troops at Guada as they travelled by vehicle towards Idaga Hamus,” he said. Residents of Adigrat, about 25km south of the border, told Reuters they saw two military vehicles carrying dozens of Eritrean soldiers pass through the town on Wednesday morning. Ethiopia demanded that the troops leave. “All foreign military forces operating within our sovereign territory must withdraw immediately,” said Enatalem Melese, Government Communication Minister. Eritrea did not deny its troops had crossed the border. In a post on X, Information Minister Yemane Meskel on Wednesday accused Ethiopia of building “a fallacious narrative of 'self defence' to rationalise and camouflage its war of aggression”. The crossing into Ethiopia comes days after federal forces retook Mekelle, the Tigrayan capital, from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). According to Acled data, Tigray Defence Forces, the TPLF's armed wing, have a heavy presence in Idaga Hamus and Adigrat. Many TPLF leaders are in the rural Ahferom district of central Tigray, Dr Jalale said. He said Eritrea is suspected of backing the Alliance for Survival, a coalition of seven armed groups, including the TPLF, that was formed last month to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Eritrea has two possible motives, he said. It was unhappy with the 2022 Pretoria agreement, which ended the war in Tigray, because it wanted the TPLF destroyed. Asmara's grievances against the TPLF date back to the 1998-2000 border war, when the party led Ethiopia. Dr Jalale said it wants to turn Tigray into a buffer zone that is hostile to Addis Ababa. “Hence, Eritrean forces entered the war in Tigray to halt the Ethiopian government and allied forces from reaching the border and potentially fighting within Eritrea's territory,” he said. The commander of the pro-government Tigray Peace Force, Gebreigziabher Beyene, made a similar point.
